### Joint choice of language teaching and timing

Results for the November 24 preregistration. Source 6144 randomized Karen installations, 4922 purchases, 6406.5 units in simulated fees. Training net 11619.5 vs 16000 for skipping (4380.5 source deficit). Across all eight held-out deployment conditions together the fitted policy recovered 4174 units vs skipping, leaving a cumulative deficit of 206.5. No empirical whole-study break-even. Each condition contains 64 paired simulated streams of 32 installations using recorded acoustic/meaning forks; the streams do not represent independent human speakers.

Mean net per installation in persistent/alternating regimes: Karen learner 2.778/2.704 vs skip 2.635/2.585, tuned partition-and-price rule 2.753/2.687, transition forecaster 2.748/2.713. Moira learner 3.257/3.214 vs skip 2.893/2.843, partition rule 3.187/3.121 and forecaster 3.288/3.252. Paired learner-minus-partition means and 95% intervals: Karen .024 [approximately 0,.049] / .017 [-.005,.039]; Moira .070 [.046,.095] / .094 [.071,.116]. None of the four point estimates met the preregistered +.1 margin vs partition rule. On unordered Moira persistent menus the learner selected 232 endpoints, 969 full paths and 847 skips out of 2048. One held-out candidate phrase also occurred in the rare future workload. Fit shared-position acoustic exemplars with each method, separate ordinary and both warped regimes. Require ≥80% complete trajectories and ≥3/24 gain over equal durations per voice per warped regime before claiming robust learned boundary placement. The experiment measures timing perturbations of features and downstream actions, not natural prosody or true boundary error.

Additional attribution control before examining scores: invert which identities are matched only inside the boundary-selection objective, keeping the true labels on the resulting excerpts during final enrollment. This tests whether correspondence contributes beyond choosing non-equal cuts. Report all timing regimes.

Complete trajectories /24 under uniform, (2,.5), (.5,2) respectively. Tessa: joint 24/11/5, equal 24/3/3, source alignment 24/19/6, reference 24/19/17, inverted 6/0/2. Under uniform timing recurrence retained all ordinary accuracy. Correct correspondence improved downstream decisions over the inverted control in every cell, even though final exemplar labels were correct in both arms. Under distortion it exceeded equal slicing in all four cells, by only two jobs in the weakest Tessa cell; it missed the 80% target in every distorted cell. Source alignment also surpassed recurrence on both distorted Tessa panels. Warp-aware reference restores the assumed equal split in the original time coordinate, not a true-boundary oracle. Remaining gaps may include landmark-grid resolution, descriptor robustness to within-segment warping, and insufficiency of same-name similarity; not localized among these. ### Candidate resolution versus scoring in grounded acoustic alignment

On the opened two warped panels, compare the identical recurrence objective on eighth and sixteenth cut grids (include equal cuts in both, same four-frame floor and tie rule). Within each grid, a diagnostic uses the candidate nearest the known warp-transformed equal boundaries in total absolute frame distance, ties by lexicographic cut order. That candidate is a feasibility witness, not a ceiling or input to the listener. Report preselection recurrence rank of the witness and paired differences in action hits vs the chosen same-grid candidate. Positive difference proves at least that much attainable improvement in that placement; worse witness cannot certify absence of headroom. Additionally test a frozen alternative score on the coarse grid: ratio of average same-name cross-phrase squared distance to average different-name cross-phrase squared distance, with 1e-12 denominator floor. Only the denominator distinguishes this policy from recurrence in its evidence; assess separately from diagnosis. Require >=3 additional correct jobs and no regressions across the four cells for a consistent scoring improvement. No use of held-out outputs when ranking candidates. Verify exact reproduction of historical coarse choices.

Separate recording-level confirmation after coarse/fine diagnosis: keep recurrence, both grids and all splits fixed. Change teaching recordings to 187 wpm, terminal recordings to 227 wpm and use unseen distortion exponents (1.8,.6) and (.6,1.8). Same word strings, voices, placements and source bank. Compare coarse versus fine without reference information in selection. Confirm consistent transfer only with ≥3/24 additional correct in each of four cells and report absolute 80% separately. Multiple synthetic rates of the same voice are not independent speakers.

Original warped panels (first timing direction, then reverse) from 252 to 2010 candidate cut combinations with unchanged objective: Rishi 15→21 and 11→20 /24; Tessa 11→21 and 5→16. Independently reproduced all 24 coarse segmentation choices and their saved outputs. Reference-nearest coarse candidate achieved 9/15 Rishi, 4/7 Tessa (scores for the two directions respectively); fine candidate 17/23 and 18/11. In reverse timing, attainable improvements over selected coarse within individual placements total at least 5 jobs Rishi and 3 Tessa (sum of positive witness differences); corresponding first direction no positive witness. Thus candidate density mattered, and recurrence ranking sometimes left usable candidates on the table. Per-placement recurrence ranks and grid feasibility verified in raw log. Contrastive score on coarse grid 10/13 Rishi, 0/5 Tessa; no consistent improvement.

Fresh 187→227-wpm recordings with the alternative warps: coarse→fine Rishi 21→23, 19→22; Tessa 18→20, 12→22. All fine cells ≥80% but only two of four gained ≥3, missing the stricter transfer criterion. Recovered/lost individual outputs were 3/1, 5/2, 2/0, 11/1 respectively. Finer search improved net counts everywhere but cannot be assumed individually monotone; about eightfold candidate enumeration. Same two synthetic voices and word strings, hash-distinct recordings, evaluator-known warp used only to form diagnostic witnesses. External cut_grid.py, verify_cut_grid.py, confirm_grid.py, check_confirm_grid.py and cut-grid/cut-confirm JSON. No target enrollment labels or downstream trajectories entered candidate ranking.

### Choosing a segmentation using a third spoken lesson

On both opened 187→227-wpm distortion panels keep the top fine-grid recurrence candidate and up to three further candidates in rank order, requiring at least one cut to differ by ≥1/8 of its lesson duration from every already retained candidate. No warp reference in proposal or selection. Preview two new sounds (B,A and A,B,A,A at 217 wpm) and have all retained listeners predict their trajectories. Choose the sound with most pairwise disagreements, first on ties; if there is disagreement buy the shown movement and take the earliest-ranked candidate predicting exactly that movement, falling back to the original when none match. Charge .05 per preview and .5 per purchase; base two demonstrations cost 1 for all arms. Compare original recurrence, free preview-majority diagnostic, same-spend withheld and alternative valid paid movement, and evaluator-only best proposed candidate per installation. No target labels or outcomes for proposal, stopping or matching. Require ≥3/24 net newly correct outputs and ≥.20 net reward per four jobs vs original in each voice/direction for robust improvement. Distinguish unproposed, undistinguished and misranked alternatives where a better candidate exists. This is a diagnostic with replayed placements, two synthetic voices and supplied chooser.

All 24 reset deployments purchased the third movement, three changed segmentation. Complete actions /24 per voice and direction (Rishi then Tessa, each 1.8/.6 then .6/1.8): original 23/22/20/22, true confirmation 23/23/20/21, alternative and withheld both 23/22/20/22, preview-majority 23/20/20/16, evaluator-best of four candidates 24/24/21/23. The one added and one lost correct action canceled; 87/96 both before and after. Incremental preview/teaching fees 14.4 over 24 deployments, net −.60 per deployment vs original. Even best possible candidate selection on every placement yields only 92/96, five gross recoverable jobs. After paid selection, four of nine residual job losses are unavailable to a fixed proposed candidate per placement, one is reachable by an equally compatible lower-ranked candidate, four reflect an optimal candidate not surviving the selected true receipt. These comparisons concern total jobs per placement; they do not assert every individual missed job is impossible.

Post hoc menu audit with unchanged tie rule: perfect hindsight choice of which single query to buy could yield 89/96 gross, as could requiring both correct receipts and falling back to original when no survivor. Only two of 24 placements had any one-query action whose predicted benefit measured in hindsight exceeded its .60 fees. Hypothetical clairvoyant buy-or-skip net improvement upper bound for this menu and update rule was .8 total (about .033 per deployment), below the .20 criterion. Disagreement often split weak candidates while supplying little evidence about which competent listener would transfer. No positive economic or causal superiority claim. Pairwise prediction splits and matching, exact baseline cuts and transcripts, and scored path coordinates independently checked. Reproduce via boundary_lesson.py, check_boundary_lesson.py, audit_boundary_menu.py and boundary-lesson JSON in the external dual-role-word archive.

### Constructing a pronunciation request from competing segmentations

Freeze both fine-grid leaders (rank one plus the first candidate differing by at least 1/8 lesson duration in any cut) from the 187-wpm lessons. Test the reversed distortion (.6,1.8) first on both voices. Generate all two- and three-name strings over the demonstrated pair, excluding the two lessons. For each leader synthesize a feature-level prediction for each string by concatenating its own extracted spans, selecting the original position most similar to the requested occurrence (initial, internal, final; ties in lesson order). Decode the imagined practice with both leaders using the installed acoustic scorer. Rank by number of simulated voices in which exactly one listener reads the requested sequence correctly; ties prefer shorter, then construction order. With positive discrimination, pay .5 for one actual 221-wpm rendition of that request; pick the second listener only when it alone reads it correctly, else retain the first. No teacher audio before selection. Compare paying for a random same-menu request (average all alternatives), fixed reverse phrase B,A, never asking, and oracle menu/leader headroom. Evaluate eight fresh five-word command strings, A/B first two names unequal, then ABA/ABB/BAA/BAB; use 231 wpm. Report prediction vs actual discrimination, changes, gross/net return per eight after both initial lessons, and remaining candidate headroom. Require +.25 net over skipping and +.10 over same-spend random per voice before claiming useful construction. The teacher supplies pronunciation of a requested sequence; labels, acoustic handles and two-name generation alphabet are grounded by the earlier demonstration, and feature concatenation is a supplied prediction mechanism. Uniform synth timing is not assumed to reproduce real coarticulation.

Separate use-of-receipt diagnostic frozen before opening primary scores: after paying for the requested pronunciation, retain its audio as new reusable excerpts. Align the requested handles against the selected listener by scoring every feasible segmentation on the existing eighth grid (plus equal cuts), then install these exact cuts via registered connected teaching. All new excerpts shared across positions. Compare selecting alone and assimilating the identical paid audio; include assimilating fixed reverse B,A at matched buy decisions. This isolates whether new target examples can help where the two old listeners cannot. Evaluate on same jobs, no additional fee or teaching. Model fitting uses no job labels.

The constructed request discriminated the two listeners on actual sound in 5/6 Rishi installations (32/60 across the candidate menu), 3/6 Tessa (24/60 menu). All 12 bought a rendition. Selecting only changed the Rishi listener once, in a tie on eventual job accuracy. Full original / selected / evaluator-best-of-two outputs: Rishi 46/46/46 of 48, Tessa 45/45/45. On eight jobs per installation the original net was 6.667/6.50 respectively, chosen/random/fixed each 6.167/6.00 after .5 purchase. No selection gain was attainable even with hindsight: the original listener always equalled or exceeded the other on eventual outputs. Distinguishing candidate interpretations was insufficient.

Retaining excerpts aligned from exactly the same paid utterance recovered both Rishi errors and all three Tessa errors without a lost output, reaching 48/48 per voice (6.5 net on each). Assimilating the fixed reverse utterance reached 48/48 Rishi and 47/48 Tessa. Thus evidence for using the new example exceeds evidence for the invented query policy; the one-output advantage on Tessa is insufficient for a robust selection claim. Retaining the chosen example's break-even fee relative to skipping at this horizon is 2/6=.333 per installation on Rishi and 3/6=.50 on Tessa. The probes are requested known names, and the returned acoustic example is used with that known sequence; physical onsets and final job outcomes are not disclosed to the listener. ### Whether to reuse a familiar name or allocate a fourth referent

Keep waveform A,X,B and the same grounded two-name bank/anchor spans in each pair of worlds. A fourth visible object overlaps A or B exactly in the initial board; X denotes either that familiar object or the fourth, equiprobably. Public known phrase anchors, bare-name dynamics, known object IDs, two developed familiar name bindings, four possible middle referents, and a mechanism to store a new lexical handle or another exemplar under an old handle are supplied. Enumerate all four middle bindings against the first observed path. Two paid re-demonstrations of the same recording are available: move A alone or B alone, with fourth fixed. Rank by expected improvement over four applications times separated hypothesis mass (4 times reduction in modal binding error); choose only if strictly above fee (.5 and overpriced 3). Resolve ties without additional evidence by reusing the familiar label. Hidden world never enters the selector. After observing the path, actually register the new excerpt under the existing handle vs handle 8 in the local recognition bank; decode all old and mixed commands, tracking slot count. Same heard form with a familiar meaning might also be a synonym, so this tests operational reuse vs growth, not the linguistic distinction of synonym vs pronunciation variant. Score joint correct outputs across matched worlds and both overlap contexts, not simply correct allocation. Require true query to produce ≥80% joint mixed paths and ≥95% retention per voice, surpass withholding by ≥20 points and net +.25 per four mixed outputs vs committing early. Equal-fee irrelevant layout, reversed valid receipt, and overpriced abstention controls. Prior cases in the last experiment used already distinct coordinates. This follow-up uses archived audio; geometry and ambiguity are new.

The first public trajectory was identical for the two balanced meanings at every placement. Moving the overlapping familiar object separated them; moving the other familiar object never did. The cost-aware public enumeration bought the separating layout at .5 and abstained at 3 in every placement. After the separating receipt, actual acoustic banks reused an existing handle in 12/24 forks per voice and allocated handle 8 in the other 12, exactly matching the operational criterion. Both-world mixed path accuracy was 40/48 Rishi, 48/48 Tessa. Existing jobs correct in both forks 96/96 per voice. Early familiar commitment, withholding the paid path, moving the irrelevant object, and reversing the receipt all had 0/48 joint successes; the early arm still achieved 40/48 or 48/48 in its familiar-meaning branch. Each pair of worlds reuses identical audio and two overlap contexts; 48 counts are paired decisions, not 48 independent recordings. The selector's prior, construction, deterministic transition model, one handle per known referent preference and action costs are supplied. A separate synonymous handle bound to the same referent may also produce correct behavior; these outputs alone cannot identify a speaker's linguistic distinction between synonym and pronunciation variation. Independently recomputed both-world executable actions and equal initial public paths. External reuse_or_grow.py, check_reuse_or_grow.py and reuse-or-grow-{rishi,tessa}.json.

### Inducing the geometry of a spoken reference from raw coordinates

Remove named spatial relations from the learner. Supply numeric 2D coordinates for each object, distinguishable speaker and addressee coordinates, a generic candidate-object ranking interface and all degree-one/two monomials on the six coordinates. Complete four-convention/two-role-position/three-transform scenes 0/72, 36/72, 72/72; at 128 each convention correct on all 432 transformed pose decisions, including 46/72 scenes where at least one reference selected the new fifth object. Spoken complete sets 240/288 Rishi and 288/288 Tessa at 128, matching the supplied exact menu already after eight demos. Real-valued minimum-L1 ranking achieved only 2/72 complete scenes at 128 despite per-rule scores 364,370,363,363 /432; training-scale finite-margin solutions need not translate or rotate correctly. The hard-margin linear-only control was infeasible in every fit; it has no trained prediction, counted as no complete successes, not a measure of best approximate linear accuracy. Scope is a new board/repeat replay of opened strings, with a trusted repetition service, not spontaneous dialogue.

Across 6144 paired outputs per voice, asking on object disagreement preserved the transcript-disagreement policy's correct counts (6144 Rishi, 6120 Tessa) while reducing calls from 864 each to 359/410. At .25 per call net/output was .98539/.97941 versus .98177/.98486 for the strongest fixed reader (mean), differences +.00362/−.00545, missing the prespecified +.01 in both. Repeating always earned .75. Fees strictly below 112/359=.3120 Rishi and 69/410=.1683 Tessa beat the strongest fixed free reader on this mixture; these are sensitivity calculations on a fixed policy. On the fast-long half the travel reading was already correct throughout; all 57/69 purchased repeats were redundant. On the matched half the repeat corrected 243/337 otherwise wrong travel-based actions. Withholding purchased audio kept charges fixed and reduced total correct to 5901/5783; substituting the other last connector yielded 5931/5862. Tessa's remaining 24 errors were complete acoustic agreement on the same wrong transcript, involving two strings; the independently spoken repeat would have corrected all 24. Rishi example: with recording (2,4,0,3,7,3,1), source library 0 and left grouping, both hearings selected object index 2 on board 7. On board 5 they selected 3 and 1; the purchased repeat selected the correct object 3 and flipping its connector selected 2. Boards, recordings and grouping were paired; repeat choices and availability verified across initial-sound conditions. Outcomes reuse recordings and semantic libraries. The gate was engineered, reward/fees simulated and acoustic reads registered locally. Reproduction: repeat_request_audio.py VOICE 207, travel_fit.py VOICE repeat, repeat_request.py VOICE under mac.sh, then check_request.py and request_pairs.py. Per-branch raw decisions saved externally. No deployment change.

### Estimating when agreement about a spoken command is unreliable

Freeze a cross-voice, cross-form replay on the two opened repetition conditions. For each previously scored board, interpret the registered acoustic service's best candidate at every available grammatical length through the same grounded reader. Measure the excess mean acoustic cost (relative to the winning cost) of the cheapest candidate choosing another object. Fit a small decision rule on source returns: select mean or travel for immediate action, optionally ask on their action disagreement, and optionally ask when the relative gap against the mean action is at or below a threshold (-1 disabled, 0,.01,.025,.05,.10,.20,.40,.80). All eligible choices use the same repeat and .25 fee. Maximize source net, then fewer calls, smaller threshold, simpler policy. Fit on the opposite voice and the complementary half of whole operand orders (alternate in each length in fixture generation order), then aggregate held halves. No source/target sharing of whole commands within a fit; the initial acoustic templates are those of the enrolled test voice. Compare the same source selection with threshold disabled, fixed readers and the prior disagreement rule. Require positive net vs the best fixed and the same selection without gap per voice, and ≥50% recovery of Tessa's 24 consensus errors. Record whether affordable extra questions exist even with hindsight and account for false positives. Previously opened recordings; cross-fit is a diagnostic. No voice, length label, processing condition, correctness, repeat content or board seed is a policy input.

Cross-fit result per 6144: Rishi 6057 correct/26 calls/.98478 net, vs source-selected no-gap .97245 and best fixed .98177. Tessa 5788 correct/no calls/.94206, identical to source-selected no-gap and below mean-only .98486. Rishi had no wrong agreed transcripts at source, and both target Tessa folds disabled the gap. In the opened Tessa consensus subset, retrospectively asking only for <=.01 gaps would have fixed 12/24 errors in 14 calls; .05 would fix all 24 at the expense of 164 calls. The acoustic signal sometimes existed but the transfer policy missed it.

Fresh check frozen before scoring: four new operand orders at each length, lexicographically first unused permutation for each starting operand, excluding archived group/depth teaching and test orders. Cross the last two connector signs. Same graph, ears, trained readers, original paired source histories and fee. Fresh board seeds 93100–93105, initial five/ seven rates 183/273 or feature-time matched at a common geometric mean from 249 wpm, true and alternative repeats at 211. Fit once on all archived outputs of the opposite voice and compare with no-gap fit. Score the separate fixed .01 consensus extension of the original semantic gate as a post-historical hypothesis, with the identical original gate as control. Require positive net and ≥50% of consensus errors recovered on each voice where present, report false repeats and no-headroom cases. The four fresh orders per length and entire fresh board/recording cohort are excluded from policy fitting; both voices still synthetic.

Fresh orders result: learned opposite-voice gate Rishi 5794/6144 with 119 calls (.93819 net) vs best free .93278, but detected 0/260 shared errors. Tessa 6144/6144 with 50 calls (.99797) vs mean alone 6144 correct for free; no shared errors. The fixed .01 consensus extension bought 56 additional calls on Rishi and zero on Tessa, recovering no shared errors. All 260 Rishi misses would respond to a repeat; their relative gaps ranged .01479–.04303. In a post-result source comparison, applying the identical fitting procedure to the same voice's archived data selected .05 Rishi and .01 Tessa, yielding 6144/6144 correct with 751/0 calls, .96944/1 net and 260/260 Rishi shared errors corrected. Pooled data selected .01. This suggests speaker-specific calibration but the comparison was chosen after opening this split.

Confirmation: freeze all fitted policies from the original 32 archived strings (opposite-voice, same-voice, pooled, and best source fixed). Hold out the next lexicographic unused permutation per starting operand, excluding all earlier teaching and tested orders. Fresh 185/275 wpm five/seven initial, independent feature matching from 247 wpm, repeat at 203 wpm and boards 94100–94105. Evaluate same-voice calibration vs opposite-voice and strongest target fixed reader; require at least +.01 per output where shared mistakes exist and ≥50% shared-error recovery. Give full denominators even if the earlier effect disappears. No refitting on either new panel.

Independent confirmation on the second unseen-order set (32 distinct commands per voice, 6144 paired board/convention decisions each): Rishi same-voice selection reached 6059 correct after 1002 repeats, .94539 net vs opposite-voice 5760/239/.92778 and best fixed 5618/0/.91439. It corrected 291/376 (77.4%) wrong consensus decisions across five distinct commands, exceeding both prespecified recovery and net margins. The remaining 85 could also have been corrected by a repeat. Of 1002 calls, 441 corrected an otherwise wrong action and 561 left accuracy unchanged; maximum price to outperform best fixed across this mixture was 441/1002=.4401. The advantage is mixture dependent: compared to the best separate fixed reader within each condition, net differences were −.04793 fast-long and +.06112 time-matched. Tessa same-voice selection used the mean reader for all decisions, achieving 6144 correct without calls, tying best fixed; opposite-voice calibration spent 240 calls for the same accuracy. ### Learning comparative and cardinal group words from judgments

Extend prior quantifier grounding beyond selecting named quantifiers. Supply two grounded binary properties per utterance and a fixed three-word construction. For each quantifier form independently fit a small integer comparison over the four contingency cells (both, restrictor alone, predicate alone, neither). Candidate integer weights −2..2 and bias −3..3, test positive or zero, deduplicate by truth vectors on teaching menu (retain simplest), then choose the simplest consistent candidate. Teacher conventions rotate four meanings across four enrolled forms: strictly more than half, at least half, exactly one member satisfying the predicate, no such member. No distinctness requirement or supplied semantics-to-form mapping. Build a public menu with each cell 0..3 and 1..8 objects, represent each as shuffled per-object anonymous features. Two diagonal property-name combinations taught; both off-diagonal combinations withheld until testing. Buy up to 14 binary judgments per form using largest disagreement among surviving candidates, compare same-budget deterministic random lessons, whole-group counting and exact named-rule baseline. Run open continuous audio at 193 wpm teaching and 227 testing through registered scorer on Rishi and Tessa; exact tokens diagnostic. Four counterfactual conventions use identical recordings. Test restrictor sizes 4,5,8,11,16 and all possible positive counts; compare simultaneous correctness over changing spoken quantifier, changing convention, and adding unrelated predicate-positive and predicate-negative outsiders. Require ≥85% complete sets per voice and report empty groups separately (classical half-or-more is true for zero vs zero). Include a class balancing diagnostic for equality on large groups. Counts, visual property detectors, comparator grammar and teacher truth feedback are supplied. This is semantic induction within that representation.

Primary: open decoding recognized all 8 teaching and 8 held property-combination recordings per voice. Induced comparisons passed 98/98 nonempty complete sets, 6/6 exact-half sets (subset) and 2/2 empty sets per voice. Each set requires all sixteen form/convention decisions on both original and outsider-augmented scenes. Same-budget random teaching passed 36/98; whole-scene counting 0/98; named-rule baseline 98/98 with two judgments per form vs 10–13 for induction. The same semantic fixtures were used across voices. With exact hearing verified, labels from teaching belong to the observed spoken forms; no conclusion on ambiguous acoustic teaching.

Extension frozen before fitting: retain the same comparison space and acquisition budget. Switch to four meanings absent from the four named rules: strictly more than two thirds of the restricted set match, exactly two thirds match (arithmetic convention includes zero/zero), more matching objects inside than outside, and equally many matching objects inside and outside. Train on the formerly held property pairings, freeze before testing on their complement; reuse exact decoded recordings from the primary panel and use fresh teaching order/scene seeds. Test new restrictor sizes 3,6,7,10,15, outsider-positive counts 0,2,5, with and without seven further matching outsiders. Require ≥85% complete sets per voice and ≥85% joint correctness where adding outsiders actually changes the answer; compare frozen four-rule list, a refitted model forced to ignore outsiders, random teaching and exact-word diagnostic. Report original limited-menu identifiability before attributing any failure to recognition. This extension tests flexibility of the supplied comparison space; no additional acoustic claim.

Extension result: each voice passed 276/276 complete nonempty sets, 6/6 empty sets and 720/720 paired decisions on which adding outsiders changed the truth. Each form took 11–14 judgments (191 across the sixteen form/meaning fits). Matched-cost random teaching achieved 246/276 and 720/720 changes, but 0/18 complete exact-two-thirds sets; the outsider-insensitive learner scored 0/276 and the old four-rule list 18/276, neither making any correct paired outsider-sensitive change. Across both studies, the independent verifier recomputed all saved teacher answers from count algebra. Exhausting original menu-consistent candidates yielded 1–7 equivalent parameterizations per true rule; none disagreed on any of 38,416 larger count configurations (each of four cell counts 0–13). Every selected induced meaning also passed all those configurations. The 720 decisions reuse boards across form/convention forks; semantic fixtures are identical across voices. Arithmetic convention for exactly two thirds is equality of three times the numerator to twice the denominator, including zero/zero. Registered synthetic audio recognition ran locally; count induction, lesson choice and evaluation were external replay. Source and scripts under dual-role-word: quantity_audio.py, quantity_ground.py, quantity_test.py, quantity_new.py, quantity_newtest.py, verify_quantity.py with per-voice fits and judgments. No core or default package change.

### Two-way spoken clarification with privately held alternatives

Freeze a three-turn dialogue: sender sees only its private graph and chooses the first true sentence in a shared fixed utterance order; listener has a shuffled three-graph display. Cross both possible private targets per display; both actually produce the identical initial utterance. All three displayed graphs share edge count, third fails the initial assertion. Freeze seeds 104801/105801 for development/test and fixed-question selection on development only. Compare dialogue, best development-fixed question, no question, and true, withheld and inverted spoken replies with charges preserved. Include singleton and semantically indistinguishable distractor controls. Reward 1 for a correct point; charge .25 per question, and .60 on separate no-payback forks. Uniform prior on possible targets; break guess ties by display order. Require ≥85% complete four-branch success per acoustic direction/convention and ≥.15 mean net gain vs immediate guessing on cheap ambiguous trials. Report incremental economic value over the best fixed question separately. All protocols are engineered, local speech is synthetic, and utterance truth conditions come from stored scalar comparison fits.

One-question result: for each sender voice and each convention all 64/64 matched display quartets passed under both answer vocabularies (512/512 branches). Truthful/withheld/inverted reply accuracy 512/256/0 of 512 with identical fees; receiver asked different questions across every display pair. Net .75 vs .625 development-selected fixed question and .50 immediate guess. At .60 the receiver skipped all questions and scored .50. Singleton controls 128/128, no queries; indistinguishable alternatives 128/256, no queries. The supplied uniform model explicitly computes value of a split. The same semantic fixtures run with both acoustic directions. Drawing 64 test pairs took 509 and 2012 proposals in the two conventions, respectively; conditioned matched fixtures, not naturally observed question frequencies.

Two-question follow-up: four graph display, with three possible targets all independently producing identical initial assertion, plus one excluded distractor. Require all three truth signatures distinct, guaranteeing a decision tree of depth at most two with boolean questions. New held-out generation seed 106801, 64 such fixtures per convention, uniform target. Use a generic finite-horizon utility recurrence (stop and point value 1/k; a question charges the price then receives one of its predicted answers). Compare one-step and two-step policies at fees .25, .36, .45; retain actual acoustic turns and .36 withheld-second-reply branch. Predict at .36 no one-step question can repay, but two-step starts, stops after singleton reply and continues on the two-survivor reply, earning .40 per output vs 1/3 immediately. At .45 both stop. Require ≥90% all-three-correct fixture sets and ≥.05 gain at .36 per voice/convention. The reward calculation, uniform prior, depth limit and reliable-answer model are supplied rather than fitted. Check plans against an independent analytic bound and log observed branch sequences.

Two-question confirmation matched the finite-horizon bound on all truthful branches. Per acoustic direction and convention, 64/64 complete sets, 384/384 individual correct at .36 with 640 calls across both answer mappings, net .4000. One-step skipped, 128/384 and net .3333. Each three-target fork began with the same question, stopped after one particular first answer on one branch, and spent a second question on the other two branches. Suppressing just that second reply at the same fee reduced correctness to 256/384. At .25 one- vs two-step yielded .4167/.5833; at .45 both achieved .3333 and skipped. With errorless answers in this balanced fixture the two-step plan beats stopping exactly below a fee of .4 (three correct branches, five calls vs one correct unaided branch); this boundary excludes historical training/physical service costs and is not a general human conversation estimate. Local registered acoustic services plus external semantic/planning replay, with precomputed audio for a finite menu. External dialog_turn_audio.py, dialog_private.py, verify_private.py, dialog_horizon.py and verify_horizon.py in dual-role-word; independently checked ground-truth reply content, branching, expected vs realized utility and acoustic-direction replications. Keep the same three-survivor grammar and original registered acoustic reads. Build actual question/reply transitions for fresh partner sessions. Each partner answers truthfully with probability 1 or .5 (equiprobable types); an error changes the outgoing spoken yes/no form before listener decoding. Public practice history contains eight previously verifiable yes/no answers from that partner. Use one observable feature: ≥7 of eight consistent with the known referents. Supply the first question in seeded public order that splits remaining graphs, honest-reply filtering, and stop/ask actions; stop guesses first surviving object. Learn two-stage action values backwards from uniformly randomized stop/ask trajectories, using only chosen question costs, next public states and terminal reward. Fixed price .36; include learned one-step, history-erased learner, never ask, always continue while ambiguous, and a same-information planner estimating answer accuracy from practice. Require ≥.015 net/output over strongest unconditional routine and learned one-step on each voice, ≥75% joint ask-clean/skip-noisy, and verify first reply changes next request. Paired difference vs never .02485, 95% placement bootstrap [.02236,.02716]. Opposite-history intervention .06307. The same board/reply draws under both voices gave identical decisions, so they are not independent replications. Initial ask/stop learned values after high consistency .3783/.3343, truncated one-step ask .2936. Uniform exploration cost 63620 calls × .36, net 22278.8 across 98304 source trials; skipping has expected net 32768. Source deficit is larger than the observed held gains. No additional source feedback. Freeze new graph seeds 110003/110004 and test noise seeds 110801, matched public history, 128 placements per convention, eight repetitions and three target positions. Refit neither policy on new outcomes. ### Grounding a spoken judgment about what the evidence permits

Teach three anonymous marker sounds on atomic link facts using true-only, false-only and mixed sets of possible observations and a binary judgment per marker/state. Fit each marker's three observed truth outputs independently (no named-modal menu). Teacher conventions rotate must, might, cannot. Then transfer to quantified claims on four-person/four-key graphs using the frozen nested quantifier meanings and learned row-outer convention. Supply the set of possible graphs, binding of atomic sound to one link, a prefix frame and a whole-proposition attachment in stage one. Teach continuous two-word marker+atomic sound at 197 wpm, evaluate four-word marker+two-quantifier clause at 233 wpm. For each clause draw 24 true/false graph pairs with equal edge count, from nontrivial cases; cross both actual completions and mask/reveal so identical accessible evidence can conceal opposite actual facts. Add same-length unanimous-true and unanimous-false alternatives. Require ≥85% complete tests across all markers, all three rotated teaching conventions, mixed and revealed evidence and unanimous controls per voice. Compare using only the first possible graph, the number of alternatives alone, rotated judgments, and exact-word diagnostic. Verify world-order invariance. Hidden actuality never supplied to prediction. This assesses transfer of a learned word over a supplied representation of possibilities, not discovering which worlds remain possible.

Stage two: atomic evidence leaves whole-proposition attachment indistinguishable from applying the modal separately to each row's property before the outer quantifier. Use both as candidate readings of the same utterance. A single compound demonstration on a separate graph pair and the first clause must distinguish them. Evaluate both conventions on the other three clauses, including only decisive pairs in the main endpoint; stratify by modal, report opportunity counts and common controls. Require ≥85% both-convention accuracy and ≥20-point gain over a common-target demonstration. Independent fixture seeds 112901, 113901; synthetic voices and generator are shared across conventions. Report acoustic and semantic results separately.

Primary result: Tessa 96/96 complete sets and 864/864 decisive both-attachment judgments after the compound example (three rotated vocabularies on 288 placements), vs 0 for shared/reversed compound lesson. Rishi 0/96 and 384/864; all twelve compounds heard exactly, but atomic lesson (5,3) was decoded as (4,5,3), leaving one marker entirely ungrounded. Known-slot or exact tokens recovered 96/96 and exact tokens 864/864. First-world-only and rotated whole-marker judgments 0/96 complete; world-count-only cannot pass any set because two equally sized unanimous observations can require opposite answers. All nine held clause × marker-meaning strata had decisive pairs. The atomic support code encodes presence of true and false completions; learning maps those three support states to judgments.

### When one pointed answer teaches the meanings of other spoken names

Generate anonymous candidate pairs first, then sample their meanings. Compare one connected ring of eight ambiguous words with disconnected rings of lengths six and two. On each ring a bijective assignment has two possible orientations; unconstrained assignments independently choose either candidate for every word, permitting synonyms. Both mechanisms expose identical candidate pairs and audio before inquiry. A learner is supplied these two hypotheses, with a mixture weight estimated from the proportion of bijections in 16 settled same-community vocabularies, correcting for accidental bijections under independent choices. No target regime label. Use seed 171501, 32 source-history draws per community (true structural weights .125/.875); randomize word and person identifiers, pair and presentation order. Ground eight anonymous acoustic clusters from 173-wpm ambiguous lessons, score 251-wpm independent renditions on both voices. Provide an eight-word upcoming usage inventory as audio only, one output per word, in shuffled order. Allow one teacher pointer at a price of 1.5 correct outputs, or skip. Use expected accuracy with fair credit for unresolved two-way guesses and a common scoring prior for all policies (true community mixture only in evaluator). Compare learned, forced one-to-one, forced independent, always buy, never buy, and random question. Primary: for the single ring with a bijective public contract, one receipt must resolve all eight words under both orientations on both voices. For the disconnected rings, require learned policy to query the larger ring on ≥80% of rich-history placements and skip ≥80% in the low-regularity community, and outperform best fixed buy/skip by ≥.15 net per eight outputs equally weighting the two communities. Report held uncertainty and losses on synonym exceptions, alternate receipt, costs of source vocabularies and acoustic scope. This tests transfer under supplied structural hypotheses.

Both listeners identified all eight 251-wpm words from the 173-wpm templates. On a single ring under the explicit bijective contract, the eight ambiguous exposures and one further pointer uniquely resolved all eight names under both assignments in every layout (64 layouts per voice). The orientation assumption is decisive: with the same public prefix and independent meanings, the other seven choices remain at probability .5. On disconnected rings, all 32 high-regularity history draws selected a name in the six-word component, and all 32 low-regularity draws skipped. Across the balanced community mix the resulting expected net per eight outputs was 4.594 vs 4.245 always buy under the fitted prior, 4.250 for unconditional bijective inference plus best purchase, 4.000 skip and 3.996 random purchase. Gain over the stronger unconditional control +.344. Mean net by community was 5.188 high and 4 low. Reversing the sole paid pointer in the high condition cost 5.375 correct outputs on average at equal fees. On genuinely nonbijective exceptions inside that community, net fell to 2.960 versus 4 for skipping. Each historical vocabulary costs eight settled associations; 128 prior associations per installation excluded from the target net. The two voices share the exact same simulated histories, not two independent semantic replications.

Evaluator integrated all 256 assignments; target expected reward credits ties at one half. History-only paired bootstrap interval on the gain over max(always buy under the fitted prior, skip) [.344,.358]; the gain over fixed hard-bijection purchase is .344 for every disconnected-ring history pair in this sample. In the single-ring mixture, learned net 5.022 vs 4.750 hard purchase and 4 skip. An independent check recovered each purchase from its analytic gain (.5 times one plus the estimated regularity times the number of *other* names linked by the same orientation, minus the 1.5 fee). For a connected component of size six, asking pays in expectation when the regularity probability exceeds .4. A post hoc calibration check under a forced pointer gave mean Brier loss .247/.060 for a second linked name in the low/high communities, compared with .438/.063 assuming a bijection and .250/.250 assuming independence. Only lexical frequency was estimated; the hypotheses, applicability of the structural prior and exact posterior decision algorithm were supplied. Registered acoustic matching ran locally; target meanings, simulated teaching costs and the eight-output inventory were evaluated in external replay. External lex_scope.py VOICE and lex_scope_check.py under mac.sh reproduce the saved outcomes.

Test a small morphological construction. Teach eight bare names with a single pictured individual per kind. On four-way held-stem sets (both inflections under both independently refitted teaching conventions), prefix/suffix scores were 7/8 and 5/8 for Samantha, 5/8 and 6/8 for Joelle. Thus suffix count recognition alone does not identify a benefit of segmentation. Joint segmentation improved retaining which kind was named with suffixes, but the simple whole-word comparator won a prefix cell.

Each fit received eight bare kind examples and eight inflected kind/count examples from four stems, with the other four stems held out in both inflections. Restricting the evaluator to the nine available candidates and choosing by cue timing alone still yielded 60/56 on power and 56/54 on smooth. Mean original-time error across the cue's three sample positions on the two smooth clocks grew from .096 of the phrase for fixed timing to .188 and .176 for live alignment. Whole-phrase consistency poorly localized the cue when different parts moved in different directions. Neither voice met the combined retention and transfer criteria.

The two voices each contribute 32 fresh locally synthesized utterances; timing variants are feature-space transforms. Freeze the prior classifier and nine alignment candidates. Use mean training acoustics at the two samples on each side of the frozen three-sample window. ### Learning which acoustic regions matter for a retrieval request

Two anonymous request handles are grounded by demonstrations selecting a recording: match both noun identities or match the final ending. Source and held vocabularies are disjoint. Cross four possible first nouns with two second nouns. Each archived pair has a checkerboard final ending; target queries change that ending. For each query offer the matching noun pair and one other phrase that matches the new final ending; foils share either the first or second noun. The same public recordings and menu thus require opposite selections for the two handles. Use both first endings, counterbalance menu order, and evaluate neutral panels where the matchers can agree separately. No word boundaries, noun IDs or ending bits go into acoustic distances. Distance vector: eight equal time bins, each using the cheapest local time offset of −4 to +4 on a 48-sample grid and a squared discrepancy. Fit two simplex-weighted distances by binary pointer loss with .01 quadratic regularization toward uniform, using only clean, .8 and 1.25 power-clock source examples. Controls: shared uniform, fixed first-two-thirds and final-third rules, exchanged fits, and the best source-selected single bin per request. Freeze before testing 207/233 wpm archived/query rates, held nouns and distortions 1, .70, 1.45, ±.12 sine. Require ≥75% both-request success per voice for each foil relation and ≥10 percentage points over the fixed paired region rules overall. Separately report clean and distorted, transfer to equal-ending menus and bootstrap across lexical pairs. No claim about inferring the spoken request itself: handles and demonstrations are supplied.

The primary noun metric favored early samples; both voices passed the shared-second foil requirement but failed shared-first. Opened-panel diagnostic: fit the identical noun metric separately on source menus with the first noun shared and menus with the second noun shared. Supply the test foil class only to this evaluator and compare with the original single noun metric. This tests whether source supervision specific to the distinction suffices. The ending metric and its evidence remain fixed.

Both voices located the final ending on all 160/160 conflict menus and all 160/160 neutral menus per voice. Ending fits concentrated ≥84% of weight in bin seven of eight. On conflict menus the complete two-request score therefore equaled noun accuracy: Samantha 45/80 when the first noun was shared vs 75/80 when the second was shared, Joelle 42/80 vs 74/80. Clean / power / smooth joint counts Samantha 24/32,48/64,48/64; Joelle 25/32,46/64,45/64. Overall learned / fixed paired regions / independently selected single bins: 120/122/119 of 160 Samantha, 116/102/97 Joelle. Paired gain over fixed regions −1.25 points [−13.75,11.25] and +8.75 [−10.625,30], resampling eight noun pairs. Swapping the two fits yielded 0/160 both voices on conflict menus; the request-independent metric necessarily failed joint conflict but gave 160/160 and 158/160 joint neutral. Learned neutral joint 119/160 and 142/160. Primary failed on both voices. A control had an exact acoustic distance tie; the verifier counts tied decisions (absolute margin ≤1e−12) as unresolved and checks reversal on all decisive menus.

When the evaluator supplied which noun differed, source fits used bins five/six for a differing second noun and one/two for a differing first noun. Shared-first accuracy rose from 45 to 63/80 Samantha and 42 to 51/80 Joelle; shared-second was 74/80 and 75/80. This localizes some loss to using one noun metric regardless of what alternatives share; Joelle still had substantial acoustic errors even given that information. Six source and six held stem identities per voice, 16 source query recordings and 32 held, eight additional archive recordings per split. Each of 96 source menus had two task pointers and reuses recordings across foil choices and timing variants. All forty held WAVs were bytewise distinct and disjoint from the 24 source WAVs within voice. Independently recalculated sampled block distances from waveforms, both target pointers from reference identities, and all paired contrasts from saved margins. The acoustic features were obtained locally, and learned retrieval and pointing ran as external numerical replay with supplied handles. Freeze a source-pointer-only model for the noun request. On Joelle, supplying the distinction to the previously fitted source relation-specific metrics raised shared-first accuracy from 45 to 65/80, with shared-second unchanged at 62/80. Canonical 213-wpm forms retain their original eight reference identities. Teach changed-final forms at 203 and 217 wpm in two separately shuffled rounds. Report false writes in ambiguous histories, exact matching gaps, and separately whether the reference or acoustic readout limited performance. All 8/8 cross-round recordings were independently paired correctly in both voices. ### Grounding whether pitch or pause carries a grouping contrast

Freeze two miniature conventions, one groups at the longest preceding gap, the other at the highest-pitched operator relative to that word's enrollment. Use paired three-name teaching queries: first both cues agree (both rank orders), then a conflicting utterance with a distinguishing answer. Test 16 independent four-name placements seed 217412, all four combinations of pitch and pause rank reversal, exact same PCM across conventions. Reuse the prior lexical model and eight isolated TTS sounds; pitch-shift only operator words by −4/0/+4 semitones (two-level training ±4), using resampling and tempo compensation, preserve sample counts and normalize RMS. Receiver estimates voiced fundamental from normalized time-domain autocorrelation, relative to isolated same-word enrollment. No true word identity, renderer pitch setting or timed boundaries given to receiver. Require ≥13/16 complete crossed sets per voice and ≥20-point conflicting-cue gain over either fixed cue. Separately score lexical identity, inferred gap/pitch ranks and semantic performance with oracle tokens vs oracle prosody. Controlled resynthesis, possible timbral artifacts and presegmented source audio are limitations; reported generalization concerns cue use, not naturally produced intonation.

Primary failed before semantic fitting: both hypothesis pools emptied. Neither voice decoded a complete held token string (0/64), despite correct gap ordering on 64/64. At 183 wpm both pitch-shifted operators in the very first teaching question were heard as name tokens. Frozen-pool oracle-at-test controls are also zero because a later oracle cannot restore a lost fit. Separate repair: add four pitch-shifted isolated operator enrollments at 173 wpm (both signs × both operators), no new names or source answers. Retain the failed arm, refit same teaching design and reserve fresh four-name placements seed 217413, at 211 wpm. Add diagnostic refits using exact tokens during teaching and testing with measured pitch/gaps, or true prosodic ranks with actual token readings. No further held-out tuning.

With four additional isolated enrollments per voice, both heard all 64 new recordings' words and recovered all 64 pitch rank orders. Correlated teaching retained longest-gap and highest-pitch as possible in BOTH communities. One conflicting answered example per community selected its intended cue. Frozen listening on the repair cohort: 16/16 complete sets, 128/128 branches per voice, including 64/64 conflicting-cue branches versus 32/64 for each fixed cue. On identical repair-cohort audio the original bank identified 0/64 full strings, but a refit using exact word identities with measured pitch and gaps recovered 128/128. This locates the original binding failure in lexical recognition under synthetic pitch variation. Pitch-shifted operator arrays have the same sample count at each pitch; normalized pitch is computed from the enrolled identity. The manipulated waveform may carry timbre artifacts; the cue score itself uses estimated fundamental, and this controlled design does not demonstrate natural intonation comprehension. The original 16 placements required 162 draws. Independent checks verified shared observations across conventions and endpoint denominators.
