For the intervention, exchange just the power labels among the two values with acoustics fixed and verify recovered power flips while room is retained. No word boundaries, transcript, or true duration in the reader. Test split speakers receive personal teaching; split names describe source files, not a zero-shot speaker test.

Test room-first, exact on unseen/24, familiar/72, all-four panels/24: linear 19/60/19, warped 19/63/19, previous fixed 19/61/19. Test power-first: linear 17/58/10, warped 18/63/17, previous fixed 17/60/11. Warping met both absolute thresholds for both constructions; superiority criterion passed only for power-first. Seven extra power-first panels over linear came from two speakers (+3 and +4); other four tied. Validation room-first (denominators 20/60/20) linear 10/36/5, warped 12/44/8, fixed 11/39/5; power-first linear 11/45/9, warped 15/51/13, fixed 12/46/8. Same six test and same five validation speakers across constructions; split cohorts disjoint. Independent readback checked all label decisions against stored distances, every balanced panel and the held-cell/training exclusion. All power-label intervention checks passed, a label-channel verification only.

Post-primary timing intervention: double the duration of each spectral frame in the first half or in the second half of each original test recording while preserving frame values/order. Require a correct answer to the original AND both edited hearings, 96 decisions per construction. Room-first linear 64/96 vs warped 80/96, power-first 32/96 vs 78/96. Original-only counts 79 vs 82 and 75 vs 81. Reuses 24 distinct test waveforms per construction across held-cell fits; feature-space intervention, not human re-recordings. Only source regions came from the archived eight speakers; warping is a supplied timing algorithm, not a learned grammar. Local registered spectral features and fixed-region comparator, external warping and decision readout. Reproduce fluent_warp.py valid/test room/state and fluent_warp_stress.py via mac.sh. Per-template costs and decisions saved outside the repository. No production reader changed.

### Recognizing a construction when the speaker mixes two ways of giving a command

Freeze a mixed session using the saved official validation and test recordings. Hold the same room/power combination out of BOTH forms. Six teaching clips give two renditions per observed outcome; supply the prior that there are two constructions and one example per outcome per construction. Group six recordings without form labels by minimizing within-group symmetric whole-utterance warped distance. Name/order groups by which assignment maximizes their three-example acoustic contrasts at the two previously source-learned pairs of regions. At test pick the group of the single nearest whole recording. Inputs are spectral frames and training outcome pairs; neither transcript, filename nor test outcomes may influence grouping. Infer field labels by the earlier per-group warped reader. Compare supplied grouping alone, supplied grouping and routing, and a duration-only partition/router under the same assignment method. Randomize training order and check permutation stability. Require ≥90% correct live form assignments and ≥75% correct joint meanings on jointly withheld cells in both validation and test, and within five percentage points of named grouping/routing on all test commands. Use identical recordings to isolate removing the cue; previously opened panels. Include a new, uniformly time-normalized input control if raw duration alone succeeds.

An initial check stopped before scoring when duration-only partition ties depended on presentation order. Equal group costs (rounded to twelve decimals) now break ties by a canonical partition signature of the public spectral contents. Verified the same named partitions under reversed input order for every live fit. On validation acoustic grouping correctly recovered both named teaching groups in 20/20 fits, routed 155/160 commands, answered both fields in 120/160, and 26/40 withheld combinations. Test: 24/24 fits, 188/192 routed correctly, 159/192 meanings correct, 35/48 withheld (72.9%). Supplied groups without supplied live routing gave identical outcomes. Fully supplied routing gave 122/160 and 163/192 meanings, including 27/40 and 37/48 withheld. Duration grouping/routing gave 127/160 and 146/192 correct routes, 107/160 and 140/192 meanings, 23/40 and 33/48 withheld. Both routing criteria and within-five-points test criterion passed; withheld mastery missed on both splits, including validation with oracle routing. Grouping got six annotated-outcome but construction-unlabelled teaching utterances per installation, with a supplied balanced two-construction prior. These findings do not establish induction of the number of constructions.

Diagnostic: time-normalize every reference and query to 80 frames for grouping and routing; preserve the trained region assignment procedure. Route accuracy 156/160 validation and 188/192 test; using mean spectra of those same normalized frames gave 114/160 and 145/192. The ordered acoustic comparison retains discrimination at equal length. Meaning readout stayed outside this diagnostic. The six test speakers share 48 distinct query recordings across 24 correlated teaching forks; validation has five speakers and 40 distinct query recordings. Local external replay fluent_mixed.py valid/test and fluent_mixed_check.py via mac.sh. Per-decision routes, outcomes and controls saved locally; known-route outputs checked against every previously saved warped answer. No change to core or deployed reader.

### Transferring two competing room names across spoken constructions

Freeze a three-room balanced hearing test. For each direction teach three on commands, one per room, in one form and two kitchen commands (on/off) in the receiving form; no bedroom or washroom example in the receiving form. Test one new utterance for every receiving-form room × state. Include all eligible official validation/test speakers (5/5 validation, 7/6 test, for receiving room-first/state-first). Use only the word “washroom” for the new location. Compare a lexical bank of time-normalized spectral patches at the previous source-selected room position in each form, a fixed broad 40% edge, and a bank that translates donor patches by the difference between the two kitchen-on anchor patches. Primary method is unshifted source-selected regions with same-form kitchen examples included. Predict power from the two receiving-form kitchen examples by the previous warped reader. Explicitly supply construction identity to isolate word transfer. Test relabelling the two transferred room memories (power and query held fixed), and the advantage available to an evaluator given only the two disputed rooms. Require ≥75% on BOTH individual room and joint decisions on transferred-room trials separately by direction, ≥75% on kitchen room controls, and ≥50% complete four-command transferred-room panels on both validation and test. Every eligible speaker contributes a single panel per direction. No source-driven adjustment after seeing either split.

Separate follow-up after inspecting both opened cohorts: fit paired windows across the two command forms using only bedroom and kitchen, without any washroom audio, from eight earlier source speakers. For every region pair compare each on/off presentation with the two room candidates spoken in the other form; use number correct then summed relative nearest-room margins averaged across source speakers to select one pair. Freeze all 16×16 windows. Compare this alignment to the original within-form regions and broad edges on up to the first eight eligible train-split speakers in each direction outside prior_ids, all previously used window-study cohorts, and the cross-form source. Preregister independent ≥75% transferred-room accuracy and +10 points over broad edges in each direction. Report opened validation/test separately if replayed. Broad task now tests a third word outside the acoustic region-selection vocabulary.

Primary transferred-room / complete meaning: validation room-first 6/20 and 6/20, state-first 6/20 and 6/20; test room-first 9/28 and 7/28, state-first 7/24 and 7/24. Correct test kitchen rooms 14/14 and 12/12, power alone on transferred rooms 25/28 and 22/24. Zero complete primary panels throughout. Broad 40% windows improved joint test to 16/28 and 13/24 (zero and two complete panels). With only the two transferred rooms offered, broad room scores reached 26/28 and 21/24. Enforcing a shared shift from the kitchen-on correspondence gave zero transferred-room hits in every split/direction. The alternate memory-label check recomputed selections from saved distances and switched exactly the two associated names while retaining kitchen and the separate power readout; this verifies dependence on supplied teaching labels. Diagnostic with broad windows and only the three donor-form exemplars in competition: 23/28 and 18/24 transferred-room hits but only 5/14 and 11/12 correct kitchen controls on test, versus 17/28 and 13/24 transferred-room hits with all five exemplars. Same-form distractors affect identification. This diagnostic changes both template count and form coverage.

Cross-form fit on 64 source recordings from eight speakers chose room-first frames 0–20%, state-first 60–80% (formerly 70–90%). Fresh train-split speakers after exclusions: room-first eight speakers, learned-pair room/joint 17/32 and 17/32 vs broad 18/32 and 18/32; state-first three eligible speakers, learned 7/12 and 7/12 vs broad 8/12 and 7/12. Forced two-room trained comparison reached 26/32 and 10/12. All kitchen room controls correct with trained pair (16/16, 6/6); zero complete four-command panels. No superiority or mastery threshold passed. Cross-form training improved on the narrow within-form patches (6/32 and 4/12 room hits), but no gain relative to broad edges. Verify using fluent_carry.py valid/test 0/1, fluent_carry_fit.py, fluent_carry_fresh.py train 0/1 via mac.sh; raw outcomes, costs, source grid and clip identities in dual-role-word. Spectral envelopes registered locally; comparisons and interventions external. Speaker-level installations and conditional power scores do not imply unrestricted vocabulary learning. No deployed model change.

### Calibrating cross-construction evidence with a changed familiar room

Freeze before fitting. Compare the broad 40% region with a local search over word durations of 20%, 30%, 40%, or 50% of either recording anchored to the same outer edge. Take the minimum scaled squared envelope distance across width pairs. Separately calibrate both readers by multiplying same-construction distances by a source-chosen factor in {1,1.25,1.5,2,3,4,8}. Select factor on equally weighted familiar-room and transferred-room accuracy, ties nearest one. Source uses only bedroom/kitchen, first eight sorted train speakers with two recordings of all four meanings in both forms, alternating the familiar room, training on donor-on and familiar receiver-on/off and evaluating distinct second receiver recordings. Target uses five examples and all six balanced commands, repeating the prior kitchen-anchor task then a new washroom-anchor task with bedroom and kitchen never demonstrated in the receiving form. Evaluate validation and test separately, both directions; hold rendered state fixed across ablations and charge acoustic or classification errors. Primary is local-search plus calibration. Require ≥75% transferred rooms, ≥75% familiar rooms and ≥10 percentage points in overall room accuracy above uncalibrated broad patches per test direction with the changed anchor. Keep source selection blind to target measures. Raw source/target word timings unavailable.

Separate repair test after primary measurement. Simulate asking for the same instruction in the donor wording. Supply a real other-form utterance by that participant with the same intended room and state; for “on” use a distinct take from the donor-on teaching clip, for “off” use first available. This is evaluator-routed prerecorded clarification, not interactive human behavior. Exclude entire speaker/direction panels if any of the six replies are unavailable or overlap a teaching/query recording. Listen to the reply with the existing local-width donor-only bank, retain the original power readout for a room-only clarification. Charge .15 correct-room units per question across every live output. Fit a threshold on the two-room source from {never, .1,.25,.5,1,always} using (second-best minus best) / second-best cost across distinct room labels from the calibrated primary; maximize correct rooms less fees on complete source panels, ties fewer requests. Compare selective, never, always and within-panel spend-matched uniform expected reward. Require +.03 net per decision versus the strongest comparison for EACH changed-anchor test direction. Treat a zero-question threshold as a substantive result.

Source selected multipliers 2 for broad windows and 1.5 for local-width search (103 and 109 correct of 128 source trials vs 88 and 99 with multiplier 1). Test with kitchen familiar: primary transferred/familiar room correct 24/28 and 13/14 room-first, 19/24 and 11/12 state-first. With washroom familiar, primary 21/28 and 13/14 room-first vs uncalibrated broad 14/28 and 14/14; overall 34/42 vs 28/42, meeting the three room-first tests. State-first primary 8/20 and 10/10 vs broad 8/20 and 10/10, missing transfer and gain. Seven of ten bedroom recordings in this latter panel selected washroom. Changed-anchor validation 15/20 and 10/10 room-first; 3/12 and 5/6 state-first. These are room decisions, conditional on supplied construction. No timing annotations or isolation of the phonetic cause.

Rephrasing: source threshold .25, 119/128 room hits after 49 purchases (111.65 net). Changed-anchor test complete panels: room-first never/selective/always 31/36, 29/36, 28/36 hits, with 0/18/36 calls and net 31/26.3/22.6; spend-matched random expected 26.63. State-first 14/24, 20/24, 22/24 with 0/12/24 calls; net 14/18.2/18.4 vs random expected 16.53. Selected state-first replies corrected six and broke none; room-first corrected one and broke three. Validation room-first 19/24,17/24,13/24 with 0/14/24 calls; state-first 8/18,10/18,9/18 with 0/14/18 calls. Selective failed the strongest-control economic criterion. Verified SHA-256 separation of each changed-anchor reply from its query and five teaching recordings. Excluding incomplete panels changes denominators relative to the original study. No human was asked live, and the evaluator supplies the matching intended command in an alternate construction. Reproduce fluent_calibrate.py fit/valid/test and fluent_rephrase.py via mac.sh in dual-role-word. Frozen source grids, per-command predictions, costs and receipt identities saved externally. No production change.

### Deciding how strongly to revise a room judgment after a rephrasing

Freeze the prior margin-.25 purchases and fee .15. Reconstruct per-room acoustic distances from both hearings. On a paid trial minimize log first distance + weight × log second distance for each room. Select weight from 0,.25,.5,1,2,4,reply-only using correct paid source decisions in each direction, ties closest to equal weight (then smaller); fit only the archived two-room/eight-speaker source. Compare equal weighting, retaining first, blindly taking reply, and always asking with equal weighting. Report corrected vs broken first judgments, complete deployment return including skipped jobs, and a diagnostic paid pointer intervention that exchanges reply recordings across rooms at fixed speaker, power, wording, price and first evidence. This alternative is a deliberately conflicting utterance. Require fewer paid errors than both keep and replace combined across the two changed-washroom directions, net superiority ≥.03 per output to best fixed purchase strategy in each direction, report separately on opened validation/test. Independently run a new three-room cohort using first eight eligible train speakers per direction outside every earlier train-split study's source/target IDs, or all available if fewer. Do not change fit or acquisition after evaluating the cohorts.

The preregistered unused-speaker complete-panel cohort had zero eligible speakers in both directions. Separate, explicitly incomplete-coverage check: retain the same speaker exclusions, learned rules, five teaching clips and washroom anchor. Take every unused eligible train-split speaker with those five clips; score each available room/state probe only if its query is distinct from all teaching clips and its reply distinct from both. Use first legal recordings in sorted path order. Report per-direction exposure, which rooms/states are represented, conditional decisions and speaker counts. Missing individual cells preclude the balanced deployment or six-command mastery claim.

On source paid trials the room-first rule selected reply-only (22/22; equal fusion 20, keep 13); state-first selected equal fusion (21/27 vs 20 keep). On the three-room test paid room-first trials keep/take/equal/fitted got 14/12/14/12 of 18, and paid state-first 4/10/10/10 of 12. Fitted therefore tied blind replacement on the 30 paid trials, while fixed equal fusion achieved 24/30 vs fitted 22/30. Test room-first fitted corrected one first decision and broke three, state-first corrected six and broke none. Whole deployment room-first 29/36 minus 2.70 fees = 26.30 vs best fixed return 31; state-first 20/24 minus 1.80 = 18.20 vs 18.40. Validation fitted paid correct 7/14 and 9/14; complete net 14.9 vs best fixed 19, and 7.9 vs 8. Validation/test criteria failed. At fixed fee and timing, substituting a conflicting other-room recording changed fitted choices in 9/14 and 10/14 paid validation cases and 12/18 and 10/12 on test; this identifies receipt dependence, not correctness under conflicting speech. Verified both extreme fusion weights reproduce the stored first/reply choices.

Incomplete-panel independent check: 15 distinct new speakers overall. Room-first 40 available trials from 15 speakers, 22 purchases, first/take/equal/fitted 32/33/33/33 correct; fitted net 29.7 vs 32 for never. State-first 30 from 12 speakers, 20 purchases, first/take/equal/fitted 18/20/22/22; net 19 vs 18 for never. With state-first, 24 of 30 were off commands, only three queries named the familiar washroom; availability is informative and this is not a replication on balanced deployments. Verified per-speaker query uniqueness, distinct query/reply content hashes, and per-room minima against both original readings. Selective fusion gave modest independent state-first gains but no general superiority to fixed equal weighting. Local reproduction: fluent_integrate.py fit/valid/test/fresh and fluent_integrate_partial.py via mac.sh; score vectors, paid decisions and receipt identities archived externally. No core or deployed expert changes.

### Learning whether a paid spoken reply is clear enough to revise the first hearing

Freeze the prior purchases and fee. For every paid original, fork its identical WAV into clean and 0 dB additive white noise (RMS over entire clip); only the reply changes. Use deterministic noise from WAV digest. Also test held corruption type at the same SNR (low-pass noise, causal eight-sample average). Receiver observes only waveform-derived distances and dynamic range (90th / 10th percentile of 20-ms RMS in dB); no SNR flag or target label. Jointly select one dynamic-range threshold from quartiles of source observations and two reply weights in {0,.25,1,4,reply-only} by source paid-fork accuracy, ties prefer equal weights then proximity to one. Compare constant weight selected on identical source, fixed equal, keep and reply. Report paid correctness separately for both wording directions, clean-vs-degraded matched switches, denominators, and source-speaker vs official split. Require ≥2 additional correct pooled paid forks over the better constant/equal on both validation and test, no more than one clean loss versus equal per split, and a positive gain on the held noise type. This evaluates revision after buying; acquisition unchanged.

The source fit (49 paid calls × two receipts) chose to keep the original below 24.74 dB measured dynamic range and use the reply alone above it. The best source-constant reply weight was .25. On validation clean/white matched forks the learned rule got 32/56, fixed .25 got 34/56 and equal fusion got 32/56. On test the same counts were 40/60, 35/60 and 38/60. Clean test alone was 22/30 vs 24/30 equal, exceeding the allowed clean loss. Smoothed-noise test alone: learned 18/30, constant 16/30 and equal 14/30; validation 16/28, 14/28 and 15/28. The clean+white validation and clean-loss gates failed. Conditions reuse the same recorded reply and purchases; added noise is engineered, not natural recording variation. Reproduce fluent_quality.py fit/valid/test via mac.sh in dual-role-word. Saved settings, candidate decisions and per-utterance quality externally. No deployed policy change.

### Finding a spoken power distinction inside unfamiliar English commands

Teach each eligible FSC speaker with two “Lights on” and two “Lights off” recordings, supplying binary outcomes only. For every teaching waveform align its spectral frames against the other three utterances. Select the contiguous 35% of active frames with the largest mean different-outcome distance minus same-outcome distance. Spot the chosen fragments anywhere in each entire probe by sliding a time-normalized matcher at .65/1/1.5 of its teaching duration, every two frames including last start. Predict by closest example. Compare same matcher using full teaching utterance or fixed final 35%, and contrast fragments restricted to the final probe position. Same training scale across arms. Test four paired carriers: “turn [on/off] the lights”, “switch [on/off] the lights”, “turn the lights [on/off]”, “switch the lights [on/off]”. Include every eligible speaker, first sorted path per complete on/off pair, equal count within each observed pair. Separate validation and test; no tuning. Require both opposite commands right on ≥70% of eligible pairs and ≥10 percentage points above full-utterance spotting on each split, report internal vs final position separately. No test form, transcript, polarity or word position passed to classifier. This tests a binary distinction learned from contrasting utterances; a single explanation for the meaning of arbitrary words is not implied.

Before examining interventions, freeze a post-primary feature-level check on originally joint-correct opposite pairs. Exchange the winner's selected query interval between the two actual recordings from the same speaker and wording, interpolating donor frames to preserve receiver length. Exchange the farthest disjoint interval of identical length in each recording as a matched control. Exclude pairs lacking a disjoint interval. Rerun the complete free-position contrast search. Count a paired reversal only if BOTH instructions change to the donor output. This tests dependence of the classifier on local sound; true human word boundaries and perceptual effects of resynthesis remain unknown.

Validation (six speakers/24 opposite-command pairs): contrast 15/24 joint and 37/48 individual, tail 15/24 and 37/48, full spotting 10/24 and 34/48, end-only 13/24 and 33/48. Internal vs final contrast 4/12 vs 11/12 joint. Test (seven speakers/28 pairs): contrast 22/28 and 50/56, tail 20/28 and 47/56, whole 17/28 and 45/56, end-only 15/28 and 42/56. Internal vs final contrast 10/14 vs 12/14. Ten-point gain over whole on both splits; 70% absolute passed test but missed validation. Limited evidence that choosing the contrast beats always using the tail of these particular short teaching commands. Confirmed unique probe WAVs, disjoint enrollment and saved decisions from distances. Wording provided only to assemble matched evaluator pairs; enrolled word/command identity here means a supplied on/off action outcome. Frozen settings and all distances/regions in external fluent_spot.py valid/test.

Feature swap on eligible initially correct pairs: 13/15 validation and 17/20 test reversed BOTH judgments when exchanging the selected spans; no paired reversals from the equal-length disjoint control on either split. Individual flips 28/30 vs 0/30 and 37/40 vs 1/40. Two initially correct test pairs lacked a disjoint control span. Additional waveform intervention: map selected feature indices to PCM using speech-envelope active-frame offset and 160-sample hop, interpolate the opposite segment to the receiver's length and blend its edges over 5 ms. Fresh envelope extraction and full search gave paired reversals in 4/15 validation and 9/20 test vs zero for controls, individual flips 15/30 vs zero and 28/40 vs two. Stronger feature-splice results cannot substitute for physical waveform results. No human verified what the edited recordings sounded like; a raw splice can change pitch or cross a phoneme boundary. Local registered envelopes, external selection and search. Reproduce fluent_spot_swap.py and fluent_spot_pcm.py through mac.sh. No deployed reader changes.

### Contrasting word positions during teaching

Freeze before scoring. Match teaching cost at four utterances: repeated short form (two per power state, “lights STATE”) versus one short and one internal-position command (“turn STATE the lights”) per state. In each teaching clip enumerate local fragments of shared length 35% of the shortest teaching utterance at two-frame steps. For each training fragment compute the nearest fragment of the other same-outcome clip and nearest fragment of either opposite-outcome clip; select the one maximizing the normalized margin (negative minus positive distance divided by their sum). No teacher-supplied word position. Search the full probe as before. Compare recurrent fragment versus tail with identical width and varied teaching, and recurrence versus repeated-only teaching. Independently score four excluded wordings (“switch STATE the washroom lights”, “turn STATE the kitchen lights”, “switch the bedroom lights STATE”, “turn the washroom lights STATE”), both members of each pair correctly. Require ≥70% complete pairs plus ≥10 points over both controls on validation and test. Matched contrasts use only complete speaker/wording pairs; no new source fitting from either split. Inspect teaching-only recovery by evaluator and retain acoustic-distance traces. Speech recognition remains conditional on the supplied binary action labels.

After the primary, freeze a separate teaching-content comparison: change only the second teaching pair from “turn STATE the lights” to “turn STATE the lamp”, keeping “lights STATE”, four examples, the learning/search code and probe recordings fixed. Balance the three arms by requiring availability of all teaching phrases. Score an independent train-split cohort, first twelve eligible sorted speakers disjoint from official validation/test (not necessarily unseen in earlier unrelated studies); previously opened official splits are regressions. Require the lamp pair to gain ≥10 percentage points of complete pairs over BOTH varied-lights and repeat-only on the new cohort, and no loss over varied-lights on either opened split. Different command recordings can differ in pronunciation as well as noun, so this is an intervention on teaching examples rather than a phoneme-isolated causal attribution.

Primary complete pairs on validation: repeat fragment 13/23, repeat tail 16, varied fragment 11, varied tail 10. Test: repeat fragment 17/27, repeat tail 16, varied fragment 19, varied tail 7. Varied fragment passed 70% on test only and improved on repeat by two pairs (7.4 points), below the ten-point criterion. Its 19 test successes included nine internal-position pairs versus one for varied tail. The independent speaker cohort follow-up gave lamp 19/47 versus varied-lights 14 and repeat 20. Internal-position successes on precisely the same internal pairs were 11, 5 and 4, respectively, so performance on final-position commands fell as internal transfer improved. Lamp on opened validation reached 15/23 versus varied-lights 11 and repeat 13; on opened test 15/27 versus 19 and 17. Neither study demonstrated the specified reliable gain. Four labeled teaching recordings per arm per speaker. These are paired recordings from the same person saying each opposite command, not evidence for arbitrary grammatical position.

A concurrent duplicate fetch of a shared teaching file interrupted the first follow-up before scoring; deduplicated fetch paths and reran. Verified disjoint speaker splits, identical probe WAVs across arms, both labels present in every counted pair, four distinct teaching files disjoint from each query, and predictions recovered from saved winning distances/locations. Local reproduction: fluent_motif.py valid/test, fluent_contrast_noun.py train/valid/test, fluent_motif_check.py via mac.sh. Registered spectral envelopes with external fragment selection and sequence evaluation. No deployed reader or core changes.

### Retaining both spoken power readers and selecting by acoustic context

Freeze existing repeat and lamp motif banks (six distinct labeled recordings per target speaker in total). At test compute the two distance margins and an acoustic context vector: mean spectral frames in four equal temporal quarters, divided by coefficient scale from the six teaching clips. Source: 12 train speakers' saved probe outcomes. Predict which reader is more likely to be right by mean correctness difference among the 11 nearest normalized context vectors from source, with a tie falling back to the more confident reader (relative distance margin). No test phrase identity, word position, outcome, or same-speaker source neighbor is available. Compare both single readers, margin choice, and equal addition of signed log distance ratios; all have access to the same saved receipts. Report a per-command hindsight ceiling. Evaluate unchanged on original official validation/test recordings and independently on excluded carriers “switch STATE the lights in the bedroom”, “turn STATE the lights in the bedroom”, “turn the bedroom lights STATE”, “turn the kitchen lights STATE” (only actual paired forms). Prespecify ≥2 more complete opposite pairs than the strongest fixed single or fusion arm per cohort and no loss over repeat on final-position pairs. Track internal-position gains independently; mark unavailable pairs and correlated tests. Never fabricate a missing spoken alternative.

On the previously studied validation panels (23 pairs) repeat/lamp/equal fusion/context got 13/15/17/14 complete pairs; on original test (27), 17/15/17/17. On newly excluded wording pairs, validation (17) scored 8/8/7/7; test (21) scored 14/12/16/13. Fusion and larger absolute margin gave identical outputs, as expected for the sign of two summed binary log odds. Novel test internal/final: repeat 7/7 successes out of 14/7 pairs, lamp 9/3, fusion 10/6, context 9/4. Thus the context selector failed its superiority and retention criteria. Even simple fusion lost one previously covered final-position pair while gaining three internal pairs. On novel validation the same fusion gain did not replicate. The kitchen-final carrier had no complete pair on either split (only the on command exists in this inventory); results concern three novel phrasings. Novel probe WAVs differ from the original four evaluation carriers, using the same six validation/seven test participants and enrollment clips.

With evaluator access to the correct answer only when the readers disagree, recoverable complete pairs were 20/23 and 23/27 original validation/test, 11/17 and 17/21 novel validation/test. On novel test context selected the correct reader in 5/9 disagreements vs 8/9 for fusion (verify from saved individual decisions); headroom above fusion only one complete pair, so the prespecified two-pair superiority there is unattainable by selecting these two readers alone. Separate source arrays, ranking, score differences and all test decisions can be recomputed from fluent_retain.py valid/test old/new via mac.sh with prior archives. Registered spectral envelopes and external selector. No production change.

### Learning a local acoustic detector from whole human command outcomes

Freeze a speaker-independent binary detector before fitting. Select the first 24 sorted official train speakers with complete opposing commands in four source wordings (“lights STATE”, “turn STATE the lights”, “lamp STATE”, “switch STATE the lamp”), or all eligible if fewer. Use first path per speaker/wording/outcome. Identical-split acoustic controls: local temporal convolutions with max evidence per output, same network with mean pooling, and a framewise max detector without temporal context. Use the package's 13 spectral features, source feature scaling, two 32-channel ReLU convolutions (width 5, then width 5 dilation 3), two output scores. Mask padding at every hidden layer. Adam .002, 32 epochs, batches of 16, seed 85192, no target fitting or model selection. Freeze before opening evaluation. Tests use official validation/test speakers, no personal examples; balanced pairs for each available wording including former four room commands plus “switch STATE the lights in the kitchen”, “turn the lights STATE in the kitchen”, “turn STATE the washroom lights”. Require ≥75% complete pairs on EACH split and at least 5 points over strongest pooling/framewise control for a mechanism gain. Separate accuracy and paired correctness; report coverage, source cost, and physical feature/model size. Corpus text used only to arrange matched recordings and exclude entire test wordings from source. No transcript, timestamps, locations or true order passed to model. Not a zero-label vocabulary learner.

Before reading held scores, freeze a localization check for the local detector. On originally correct opposite pairs, choose a 17-feature-frame interval (the convolution's receptive field) independently per utterance by the largest drop in its predicted-class margin when that interval is replaced with the clip mean; stride four frames plus the final start. Compare exchanging the chosen PCM intervals between the two original recordings to exchanging their farthest disjoint equal-length intervals. Both have matched editing steps. No human labels guide interval selection. Report eligible denominators, individual flips and doubled reversals separately; a waveform intervention does not establish a human phonetic boundary.

192 source recordings (24 speakers, eight balanced commands each); three deterministic CPU fits took 2.70/2.38/1.64 s for local/mean/framewise, excluding download and feature preparation. The local expert has 7,330 parameters (29,320 float32 parameter bytes); the saved three-model checkpoint including scale and source file identities is 86,839 bytes. Registered envelope uses 13 coefficient values per frame (104 bytes as float64; converted to 52 bytes in float32 for training). On nine validation speakers: 13/54 complete pairs (61/108 commands) local, 16 (66) mean and 8 (55) framewise. Nine test speakers: 18/62 (77/124) local, 15 (76) mean and 14 (71) framewise. Both absolute criteria failed, as did the comparative gain on validation. No trained detector installed.

Frozen-model attribution: 192/192 exact on original fitting waveforms. Other takes of taught wordings from source speakers: 33/61 complete pairs (93/122 individual). New wordings with those same speakers: 27/155 (177/310). For official test speakers, taught wordings yielded 9/37 (44/74) and new wordings 18/62 (77/124). ### Does request recognition need the order of acoustic frames?

Known-panel diagnostic, frozen before collecting diagnostic outputs. Reverse the four contiguous quarters as blocks, preserving all frames and their order within each block; separately permute all frames with a filename-seeded permutation. Order audit results: reversing quarter blocks preserved 27/28 and 31/32 construction choices. Shuffling individual frames preserved 21/28 and 27/32; construction accuracy fell to 20/28 and 25/32. Omitted cells in order volume up/down, temperature up/down: forward counts [3,2,6,2]/7 and [3,6,4,5]/9, reverse [3,4,1,2]/7 and [2,4,0,6]/9. Always returning the absent pair achieves 100% novel, 0% familiar and 25% overall; copying a teaching example gets zero novel by construction. Local listener missed every primary threshold. Strong novel setting identification transfers in this constrained panel; applying direction across constructions remains the dominant loss. Absolute accuracy on recordings is over matched forks, not independent language exposures. Local fluent_setting_change.py valid/test through mac.sh; query decisions and support IDs saved externally. No production change.

### Does the same audible direction transfer from volume to temperature?

Use the eight first-take commands from the setting grid. Supply four volume commands, both up/down in both construction orders, then test four unmodified temperature commands; independently reverse the device roles. Give the listener only one query at a time. Compare whole recording, the previously frozen contrast-selected spans (within-carrier opposite plus other-carrier same/opposite), and a diagnostic supplied acoustic region using 40% beginning/end of trimmed teaching and query audio depending on construction (beginning includes “turn” for preposed direction). No target labels or boundaries in the production conditions. Matched opposite-direction same-speaker same-device splice intervenes on beginning vs end of each query; expected region flips with construction. Require ≥75% both directions correct per order/transfer direction/cohort, +10 points over whole-recording on complete order pairs in each cohort, and ≥20-point gain in donor following for expected vs other splice region in each order. Report individually paired uncertainty and exact all-four results. Where available inspect independent same-device repetitions as a separate diagnostic. No new fit or target tuning.

Both directions correct per speaker (preposed, final): volume→temperature 4/7,1/7 validation and 3/9,2/9 test; temperature→volume 1/7,2/7 and 4/9,2/9. All four target commands correct respectively 0/7 and 1/7, 2/9 and 2/9. Relative to whole reference pairs, average span gain −3.6 points validation [−25.0,17.9], +5.6 test [−16.7,33.3]. Same-device distinct repetitions gave 8/21 and 14/29 complete pairs. Giving rough direction regions in support and probe on test gave 6/9 and 8/9 on preposed transfer (volume→temperature and reverse) but only 4/9 and 1/9 final. In all eight crossed cells, opposite-state donor following was more frequent for the expected region; differences in volume→temperature / reverse order preposed,final: validation 2/14,5/14 and 3/14,5/14; test 6/18,5/18 and 6/18,3/18. Thus regional directionality shifted with construction, but the predicted size missed in two cells and reliable intact comprehension failed. An edited response is not proof of isolating a word or understanding its meaning. Local fluent_direction_transfer.py valid/test through mac.sh; saved query and intervention outcomes. No production change.

### Spectral resolution as a bottleneck for “up” and “down”

The registered speech envelope already uses 32 mel bands and retains cepstral coefficients 1–13. On the unchanged four-command direction lesson compare those 13 components against all 31 non-DC components of the same log-mel spectrum. Same waveform trimming, frame rate, mel filters, span search and subsequence matcher. Scale both candidates by per-coordinate SD on the four teaching clips only (floor .1). Include a block-balanced arm with equal total squared-distance weights on the low 13 and added 18 components. Primary added-detail arm is 31 uniformly weighted components. Predict ≥10 points more both-directions-correct pairs than the matched 13-component reader in both cohorts with positive paired lower bounds; separately require ≥75% absolute in every order/transfer direction to claim stable grounding. Analyze independent same-device takes separately. No feature weights or thresholds fitted on test. External front-end diagnostic, no core/package modification.

Across devices, with both directions required per person/order/source-device, 13→31 components gave 10→6/28 validation (−14.3 points, paired speaker 95% [−35.7,3.6]) and 10→14/36 test (+11.1 [−11.1,33.3]). Equal weighting of the two component groups gave 8/28 and 14/36. Full-detail counts by source volume/temperature and preposed/final order: [1,1,2,2]/7 and [2,4,3,5]/9; none reached 75%. Same-device second takes 8→9/21 and 11→8/29. Exploratory crossed diagnostic retaining low-detail selected spans and changing only matching detail gave 7/28 and 16/36 across devices; high-detail spans scored with low detail gave 8/28 and 5/36. The test improvement appears in matching fixed spans but did not replicate on validation. Existing 13 coefficients reproduced on all waveforms to 1e-5; crossed run reproduced each diagonal decision. No evidence that discarded spectral components alone account for the direction failures. Local fluent_direction_spectrum.py and fluent_direction_spectrum_cross.py valid/test through mac.sh, recorded per-query predictions externally. No production change.

### Recognition with independently recorded isolated “up” and “down”

No independent word-time annotation located for the existing fluent commands. Use a separate, controlled diagnostic on TensorFlow mini Speech Commands (official archive MD5 4b8a67bae2973844e84fa7ac988d1a44). Require two takes of both direction words plus four different other words by the same speaker. Split eligible speakers by alternating SHA256-sorted identifiers. Teach first take per state, test second. Construct three-token streams from energy-trimmed isolated human recordings with 20 ms joins: shared flank words per state pair, two other flank words on test, three balanced query target positions, teaching target central. Score full versus known target clip independently on support/query, frozen acoustic scale and subsequence distance; no use of filenames or labels as inference features. Check target removal leaves identical audio within each up/down pair. Primary known-support/known-query ≥80% of speakers correct on both new recordings in each cohort; ≥15-point improvement over whole-stream matching in each cohort for the exact-both metric, paired bootstrap by speaker. Inspect position and which side needs localization. This supplies clip boundaries only in constructed streams; it cannot certify boundaries or recognition in naturally coarticulated sentences.

69 eligible speakers before signal checks; preserved cohort assignments and excluded two in cohort 1: same trimmed “up” waveform under different filenames and a 480-sample trim yielding insufficient acoustic frames. Both independent words correct with supplied teaching and query clip: 30/35 and 19/32, separately up/down 32/35 and 33/35, 26/32 and 23/32. Whole-stream in both stages at start/mid/end: 6/23/8 of 35 and 4/17/4 of 32. Known teaching clip alone: 27/28/27 and 18/18/17; known query clip alone: 21 and 14 in every position. Matched gains with both boundaries over whole-stream averaged across positions +50.5 points [40.0,61.0] and +33.3 [20.8,45.8]. Thus boundary support substantially helped both cohorts, especially in the lesson, but the 80% reliable-repeat criterion failed in cohort 1. Twenty-ms gaps, same-speaker distractors, identical deleted-target controls and distinct energy-trimmed waveforms verified. No annotation was generated for the original fluent recordings; independent isolated Speech Commands takes and constructed streams answer a narrower causal question. Reproduce fluent_isolated_direction.py 0/1 via mac.sh using mini_speech_commands.zip; no production change.

### Finding the contrasting sound from two teaching streams

Rotate lesson target position start/middle/end and cross all three query positions. Align opposite-labelled streams by global dynamic time warping of the archived spectral envelopes, then choose the contiguous interval of greatest cumulative above-mean aligned squared distance in each member. No word cuts, seam indices, position or transcript to the selector. Compare to complete streams, fixed middle third, and known isolated teaching clip with full query. Report positive prediction if both fresh direction tokens correct; meaningful ≥15-point gain over whole and fixed middle in both cohorts. Score selected frame midpoint inside target clip using construction times, requiring ≥80% in each cohort. Separately rerun on speakers with distinct second takes of both lesson flank words so the two teaching streams no longer share exact flank audio. No change to query audio or old eligibility; count independent speakers. Evidence pertains to constructed streams.

Identical flank recordings: localized midpoint inside the target on 210/210 and 192/192 teaching streams. Both fresh directions correct on 235/315 and 152/288 matched teaching/query-position pairs vs whole 139 and 90, middle third 70 and 64, known teaching clip 246 and 159. Independent flank takes: midpoints 80/102 and 87/114; both-direction outcomes 65/153 and 73/171 vs whole 47 and 68, middle third 31 and 41, known clip 117 and 105. Thus the two onset/offset constructions with exactly shared context passed the gain and localization criteria across the two cohorts; independent takes missed both 15-point whole-stream gains and both 80% localization gates. These positions reuse 35/32 or 17/19 speakers. The matched contrast heuristic neither learns English generally nor establishes spontaneous coarticulated-word discovery. Local fluent_find_contrast.py 0/1 through mac.sh.

### Learning a repeatable word comparison without hearing the target words

Freeze the existing two target cohorts and use only isolated clip boundaries in this experiment. Train an acoustic comparison from scratch on six other Speech Commands words (go, stop, yes, no, left, right). Exclude all target speaker IDs and up/down recordings. Use up to 128 hash-ordered eligible source speakers, then 24 distinct audit speakers, each with two distinct takes of each of two randomly assigned available words. Support and query roles swap each epoch. Normalize using only fit recordings. Same two-convolution max-pooled normalized embedding, cosine prototype likelihood ×10, Adam .002, seed 85221, 32 epochs, eight speakers per step. Compare frozen learned, untrained same encoder and existing direct matching with identical two target labels. Main: ≥10 points gain over direct on complete up/down pairs and ≥80% absolute in each cohort, with speaker-level paired intervals. Separately check same-word-vocabulary fresh-speaker audit and individual word errors. This diagnostic presupposes isolated tokens; natural sentence segmentation remains open.

With 512 distinct fit recordings and 128 people, learned comparison distinguished both directions of the sampled source word pair for 127/128 fit people. On 24 disjoint source-vocabulary speakers, learned/raw/seeded-random scored 19/20/18 complete pairs of 24. With independently spoken isolated up/down from entirely different speakers, cohort 0 learned 22/35 vs direct 30/35 and random 24/35; cohort 1 learned 18/32 vs direct 19/32 and random 21/32. Within-speaker differences vs direct −22.9 points [−40.0,−8.5] and −3.1 [−25.0,18.8]. Learned recovered 1 and lost 9 direct successes in cohort 0; recovered 6 and lost 7 in cohort 1. Confirmed all six named source words were present, no up/down fit examples, no fit/test waveform hash overlap, and exact previous direct predictions. No evidence for cheaper or better novel-word acquisition using this global max-pooled comparison. This does not test localized temporal alignment learned from such examples. Reproduce isolated_metric_transfer.py train/audit/0/1 through mac.sh. Weights and decisions archived locally, no production change.

### Learning which aligned acoustic differences matter

Use the previous six-word 128-speaker fit, 24-speaker audit and entirely untrained up/down cohorts. Compute a global monotone minimum squared-distance path between each isolated teaching token and query after fixed source-only channel scaling. Average aligned squared channel error in four relative teaching-token quarters (52 components). Fit nonnegative importance values by balanced two-choice logistic loss on source only, both take assignments, logit multiplier 5, mean quadratic penalty .05 toward unit weights. Compare equal weights on the identical path, equal-weight linear time normalization, previous direct subsequence matching and previous whole-vector learned comparator. No known word identity beyond the two teaching labels. Prespecify ≥10-point speaker-paired gain over direct and ≥5 over equal path in both target cohorts with positive lower bounds to attribute transfer to learned importance. Separately test effect of reversing frame order in the query only. Keep all examples, deterministic tie policy, and exact-pair vs individual denominators; no target fit.

The fitted mean importance per successive quarter was .81, 1.32, 1.38 and 1.02. Source-vocabulary audit on new speakers: equal and learned global alignment each got both words right on 21/24 vs 20/24 direct. For unheard up/down complete pairs, cohort 0 linear/equal/learned/reversed/direct/previous global embedding = 29/28/27/23/30/22 of 35, cohort 1 = 21/21/20/13/19/18 of 32. Learned-minus-equal paired effects −2.9 [−11.4,+5.7] and −3.1 [−12.5,+6.2] points. Learned-minus-direct −8.6 [−22.9,+5.7] and +3.1 [−6.2,+12.5]. Reversing query frames cost 4 and 7 complete pairs, but is an artificial temporal perturbation. Individual target readings correct with learned weights 62/70 and 51/64. No learned advantage, despite better observed pair counts than max pooling. This fixed-quarter weighting does not learn boundaries or discover a phoneme. External isolated_ordered_metric.py train/audit/0/1 via mac.sh; fitted weights and per-query outputs archived, no production change.

### Can isolated spoken directions be found inside natural commands?

Freeze one isolated up/down pair from each of the first 32 SHA256-ordered eligible Speech Commands speakers outside the previous 67 isolated-test speakers. No fluent labels for template selection. For each whole command, compare both isolated templates to its entire envelope with the established subsequence distance, then combine equal-speaker signed cost differences by median. Compare nearest exemplar and prior four-example personal span reader; separately calibrate only the decision threshold using an up/down command pair from the same speaker on the other setting (fixed “turn the SETTING up/down” phrasing). Do not use query position or setting to search. Target both state readings correct ≥75% per order, device and cohort, ≥10 points improved over personal span in both cohorts. Report direct isolated-word positive control on previously excluded speakers and paired uncertainty. This asks about human cross-corpus transfer of familiar lexical items, distinct from learning two unfamiliar labels. Feature scale remains the existing acoustic matcher’s scale.

The 32-speaker median got both directions correct in 5/28 fluent validation pairs and 4/36 test pairs. The earlier personal span reader got 8/28 and 11/36. Speaker-paired differences were −10.7 points [−28.6,+7.1] and −19.4 [−41.7,0.0]. Calibrating the threshold on two labelled commands from the same speaker using the other setting yielded 9/28 and 11/36. Neither primary criterion passed. Even for isolated words in the source corpus, the frozen threshold got both words right for only 10/35 and 4/32 unseen speakers. With paired labels available solely for diagnosis, the score ranked down above up in 34/35 and 22/32 isolated pairs and 18/28 and 29/36 fluent pairs. A threshold biased toward up accounts for some failures, while incorrect rankings also limit what threshold calibration can recover. External isolated_to_fluent.py and isolated-to-fluent-{0,1,valid,test}.json contain the local measurements.

Retrospective threshold audit on these same outputs. Use the median of labelled pair midpoints from disjoint calibration speakers and freeze one threshold across all target voices, settings and positions. On isolated cohort 1, calibration using cohort 0 lifted complete pairs from 4/32 to 13/32. On fluent test, calibration using validation lifted 4/36 to 11/36 without any target-speaker labels. Exhaustive evaluator-only threshold sweeps establish hard ceilings for the saved scores under this decision rule. The best common threshold after seeing all test labels gives 15/32 isolated and 14/36 fluent. Even allowing a different hindsight threshold per voice gives 24/36 fluent, below the original 75% target. Of 36 fluent pairs, 7 have reversed/tied scores and a further 5 cannot be simultaneously separated by one threshold per speaker. This localizes the residual to the scores and their dependence on recording context. These reused cohorts provide diagnostic evidence only. Reproduce with python3 bridge_threshold_audit.py in the external study archive.

### Acoustic word models pooled across teaching voices

On the archived 32-speaker isolated dictionary, learn one average four-part spectral shape per word. Use 20 log-spaced bands on 25 ms frames, subtract each frame's mean log energy, and scale features using source variation. Search for either word over windows of three source-derived durations, comparing the closest window for each word. Fit no thresholds on target voices. Compare against collapsing the four temporal parts to one and against the archived template matcher. Reuse the established isolated and fluent panels for development evidence. Look for ≥10 points complete-pair gain over the template matcher on both fluent panels and ≥75% complete on isolated words in both groups.

Using the four-part shape, both isolated words were correct on 17/35 and 18/32 voices, compared with 14/35 and 13/32 for a single spectral average. A further hash-selected cohort of 64 speakers outside both panels and the teaching bank, with duplicate feature sequences excluded, gave 30/64 vs 28/64. The four-part reader recognized 93/128 individual words there. On complete fluent pairs the four-part model scored 6/28 and 8/36 versus 7/28 and 10/36 for a single average. Earlier uncalibrated template matching got 5/28 and 4/36. The prespecified gains and isolated-word criterion failed. Temporal detail showed a small numerical benefit on isolated words across groups and none on the two fluent panels. Both acoustic representation and finding a matching span remain open. External pooled_spectral_word.py reproduces the per-recording outputs in pooled-spectral-word.json.

### Learning correlated variation across voices

Keep the four-part descriptor, 32 labelled teaching pairs, duration search, and separately minimized word costs fixed. Estimate the within-word covariance of standardized source residuals, shrink halfway to the identity, and whiten distances with it. The diagonal distance is the matched control. Primary exploratory test on the next 64 eligible speakers after the previous 64 in the fixed hash ordering: ≥10 points paired gain on complete isolated pairs, positive lower speaker-bootstrap 95% bound. Separately test ≥10 points gain on each of the two already-open fluent panels. Report all panels.

On the new 64 speakers, both words were correct for 43 vs 35, +12.5 points with paired bootstrap 95% interval [0,+25]. The point estimate passed the practical margin, while the lower bound missed the strict positive requirement. Individual words were 106/128 vs 98/128. On the three prior isolated panels the paired counts were 24 vs 17 of 35, 18 vs 18 of 32, and 38 vs 30 of 64. For fluent speech the counts were 2 vs 6 of 28 and 11 vs 8 of 36. The same covariance estimate can improve isolated recognition and still make searching a sentence worse. Verified finite transformed distances with explicit NumPy contraction and warnings treated as errors. Per-recording costs and decisions are in spectral-covariance-word.json, reproducible with spectral_covariance_word.py in the external archive.

### Known-interval diagnosis on recorded words in constructed streams

The Fluent Speech Commands CSV has utterance transcriptions without word times. Use a controlled feature-stream splice of recorded words to supply exact frame intervals. For each archived isolated target, place its frames before, between and after two fixed same-speaker distractors. Freeze the 32-voice four-part covariance reader. Compare exact interval, true length with unknown start, ordinary three-duration search, and distractors alone on the same frames. Include an exhaustive start for true-length search to ensure it contains the exact interval. Denominators are voices within each position, clustered by voice across positions. This does not establish a segmentation result on intact fluent speech.

Across initial, medial and final positions, blind complete-pair counts were 11/15/11 of 35 and 9/16/10 of 32. Length alone gave 16/19/15 and 15/16/12. Exact intervals gave 24/35 and 18/32 at every position, reproducing the isolated reader. The exact-minus-blind gain averaged over positions was +33.3 [19.0,48.6] and +19.8 [4.2,35.4] percentage points (10,000 speaker bootstrap samples). Deleted-target decisions were identical within every pair and got zero complete pairs. This establishes a location penalty under constructed distractors while leaving an appreciable isolated recognition error. All positions reuse each voice's target tokens. External known_interval_word.py and known-interval-word.json.

### Locating a changed sound using an unlabelled contrast

Give each query a same-speaker recording of the opposite direction with the same wording and setting. Pair membership is supplied, and each item is named independently. Align the two by relative time, choose the source median word-length interval with the largest mean framewise spectral difference, and name that interval with the frozen covariance reader. Test known-interval streams and intact commands separately. Score midpoint inside the true word on constructed streams only. On natural commands compare identical processing with a same-direction, different-setting companion and the archived blind reader. Require ≥10-point complete-pair improvement over both on both fluent panels. This is an assisted two-recording task. Query order, labels and true positions are excluded from locating/naming.

Relative-time matching located the target midpoint on 148/210 and 139/192 constructed items. It named both words in 48/105 and 45/96 placements, with three placements per voice. On intact commands it got 9/28 and 9/36 complete vs 7/28 and 7/36 with the control companion. Unequal speaking rates could make unchanged material look different under relative-time matching. As a separate developmental diagnostic, replace the linear alignment with a global minimum-error monotone frame alignment, fixed .5 cost for horizontal/vertical steps; average the residual for each query frame along the path. Preserve window width, reader and cohorts. Predict improvement in constructed midpoint capture and measure whether that carries to intact speech.

Elastic alignment raised midpoint capture to 182/210 and 161/192, with 57/105 and 44/96 complete placements. Complete fluent pairs were 4/28 and 10/36 vs 7/28 and 8/36 with the control companion. The archived covariance reader searching independently got 2/28 and 11/36. Neither alignment met the transfer criterion. Verified word locations in artificial sequences can improve while intact recognition fails; the intact recordings do not permit an exact localization verdict. External paired_word_region.py and paired_word_alignment.py save per-item decisions.

### Learning direction from balanced whole-command demonstrations

Use every locally cached training-speaker command containing up or down for which the same speaker also recorded the opposite direction with otherwise identical text. Take the first filename per form. Use text only to construct pairs and direction feedback. Train a ridge classifier over acoustic exemplars drawn from training only: 128 randomly sampled four-part windows, convert distances into radial similarities, retain each exemplar's highest similarity anywhere in a command. Fix width 24 frames, stride 4, seed 871, median source squared distance as bandwidth and ridge penalty 1 on standardized features. Compare a whole-utterance version with identical exemplar count and penalty. Score the two previously opened fluent cohorts and both positions separately. Require 75% complete pairs per cohort and a ten-point advantage over the whole control. This is supervised direction learning, with no word boundaries supplied.

The balanced local fit contained 336 commands from 25 speakers. File hashes and speaker identifiers were disjoint across training and evaluation. On validation, local exemplar search got 10/28 complete pairs (6/14 early, 4/14 final) vs 2/28 whole. On test it got 15/36 (7/18 early, 8/18 final) vs 7/36 whole. Individual local readings were 37/56 and 51/72. The local search improved on its matched whole-command control but fell short of the 75% complete-pair criterion. The 25-voice fluent supervision differs from the earlier 32-voice isolated dictionary, so gains across those studies cannot be attributed solely to segmentation. External whole_command_direction.py and whole-command-direction.json store the reproducible experiment and scores.

### Does the local listener follow the spoken direction region?

Freeze the preceding acoustic listener and reproduce each archived score before intervention. In each same-speaker, same-setting, same-order pair, replace either half of the trimmed acoustic frames with the corresponding half of the opposite-direction command, linearly resampled to the recipient's half length. Self-replacement must reproduce the original. Compare opposite-direction decisions after replacing the expected half versus the other half, scoring early and final word orders independently. Require ≥15 percentage points excess donor following in every cohort/order cell, with positive speaker-bootstrap lower bounds. Repeat on the originally both-correct pairs for interpretation. These edits have exact feature coordinates and coarse linguistic boundaries; they do not isolate a word or produce an intact natural utterance.

Opposite-direction choices after replacing the expected vs other half were 20 vs 10 of 28 early and 20 vs 9 of 28 final in validation, and 25 vs 11 of 36 early and 23 vs 10 of 36 final in test. Speaker-bootstrap lower 95% bounds on these four differences were +14.3, +14.3, +16.7, +5.6 points, so every primary cell passed. On the originally both-correct pairs, counts were 11 vs 4 of 12, 7 vs 1 of 8, 10 vs 2 of 14, and 10 vs 4 of 16. An additional control used a separately recorded take with either direction wherever both existed. Across those same 100 recipients, exchanging the expected half produced opposite answers on 62 with opposite-direction donors vs 32 with same-direction donors; exchanging the other half gave 37 vs 31. This supports dependence on position-appropriate acoustic evidence; coarticulation, prosody and splice effects still limit word-level attribution. All archived pre-edit scores reproduced. External whole_direction_halves.py and whole_direction_repeat_halves.py retain individual decisions.

### Two spoken command components with a missing combination

Use locally recorded fluent commands for heat/volume crossed with up/down, in short and “turn DIRECTION the DEVICE” forms. Balance training within each speaker and construction. First fit all four intents, then rotate the omitted intent and remove both phrasings of it from all training, including acoustic exemplar selection. Fix the preceding local embedding. Compare independent ridge outputs for device and direction with an explicit additive prototype control which constructs the missing acoustic prototype from the three observed corners. Use equal prior distance for all prototypes. Report both-components-correct on the omitted commands, both components separately, and complete four-command groups under full training. Aim for ≥75% joint accuracy on omitted commands in each previously opened cohort. The two output factors and four legal combinations are supplied.

The full ridge listener got 39/56 and 49/60 joint. With one combination omitted, joint fell to 16/56 and 25/60, with direction alone 22/56 and 30/60. Follow-up diagnosis on the same open panels: fit each output using only the two observed cells in which that attribute varies while its counterpart is constant. Use the original three-cell anchors and equal priors. This discards unmatched labelled examples for that head and tests whether the training correlation is harmful. Score all four omissions without selecting a favorable omission.

Full teaching used 128 commands from 16 speakers; each missing-cell model used 96. The additive prototype control got 28/56 and 23/60 on omitted cells. Matched two-cell training for each output lifted joint ridge success to 24/56 and 37/60 (direction 31/56 and 38/60, device 45/56 and 53/60). Held-out speakers were disjoint from source, with one recording per eligible speaker, form and intent. On test the matched reader was correct on all four omissions for 2/15 speaker/form groups across four separately fitted models. Neither cohort achieved the joint target. This supports a specific difficulty in inferring independent directions from correlated teaching examples; it does not establish general compositional speech understanding. External spoken_command_corner.py and spoken_command_matched.py save every decision.

### Natural English vowel discrimination before IPA teaching

Hillenbrand et al. hVd recordings via the Santiago Barreda archive, SHA256 2560548591e3a726c88549b6dc9d226995616c26874d601c69fee8b9eee9d730. Stratified hash split by talker group: 36 development, 68 teaching, 35 reserved. Development-only cyclic cross-speaker ABX, two balanced queries per contrast and speaker. Frozen untaught representation averages log spectral bands over high-energy frames. An initial duplicate frequency edge produced nonfinite distances; discarded that run, deduplicated edges and reproduced with finite checks and runtime warnings fatal. Correct out of 72 per pair: hid/heed 69, head/had 44, hood/who'd 58, heed/who'd 68. Corpus categories construct trials only. The shared consonant frame and recording setup leave context transfer open. Script, split and individual decisions saved in the external phonetic-foundation archive.

For the same four development ABX contrasts, estimate voice-specific mean spectra from up to four other recordings per voice, selected by hash from available tokens outside all six tested vowel categories. Subtract the mean from each token before calculating distance. Compare zero adaptation and a mismatched voice's mean. Stress-test every ordered pair of distinct development voices alongside the original cycle. Aim for ≥10 points improvement on head/had over both controls without >3 points lost on either previously strong contrast. The evaluator curates an off-target listening set; no category names enter distance calculations.

Across all 1,260 ordered pairs of the same 36 voices (2,520 decisions per contrast), raw → own-voice centered counts were hid/heed 2197→2254, head/had 1376→1392, hood/who'd 1816→2034, heed/who'd 2356→2429. Mismatched centering yielded 1944, 1325, 1611, 2115 respectively. On the original cycle own-voice counts were 66, 40, 59, 70 of 72. Head/had improved only 0.6 points over raw on all pairs; the proposed mechanism fails the primary gate. Shared talkers and recordings make pair decisions dependent. No reserved speakers were opened. Reproduce via vowel_speaker_history.py in the phonetic-foundation archive.

Test three successive equal-count spectral averages against the whole mean, crossing energy-selected frames with evaluator-only annotated nucleus intervals. All ordered pairs of distinct development voices, no voice adaptation. Require a ≥10-point gain on head/had using energy-based windows, and check whether reversing the query thirds removes any gain. Keep the reserve sealed.

Of 2,520 head/had decisions on 36 shared development voices, whole/thirds/reversed-thirds gave 1376/1485/1227 with energy selection and 1361/1474/1280 with annotated intervals. Ordered thirds gained 4.3 points on the ordinary pipeline, below the 10-point target. Supplying the annotated nucleus did not close the gap. On the three remaining contrasts ordinary thirds gave 2212 (hid/heed), 1852 (hood/who'd) and 2357 (heed/who'd). Individual comparisons archived in vowel-thirds.json with vowel_thirds.py. These results localize a limitation of this descriptor on this shared consonant frame.

Diagnostic: use corpus-measured log F1 and F2 at 20%, 50%, 80% of vowel duration. Compare midpoint alone, all three positions, and subtraction of same-voice average log F1/F2 from the four previously fixed off-target recordings. Exclude voices with missing required measurements from all three arms per contrast. If head/had gains ≥10 points over the acoustic thirds baseline on matched comparisons, prioritize autonomous resonance tracking. These measurements are privileged and never enter production inference.

For head/had the matched baseline, midpoint, three positions, and voice-centered three positions got 1399/1265/1607/1723 correct of 2380, a +13.6-point centered gain. For hid/heed corresponding counts were 2087/2198/2187/2037 of 2380, hood/who'd 1648/1582/1742/1946 of 2244, and heed/who'd 2089/2158/2165/2207 of 2244. Missing measurements reduced coverage to 34–35 voices per contrast. Centering had mixed effects. These development results motivate testing a waveform-based resonance tracker; they are not listener performance. See formant_reference.py and formant-reference.json in the external archive.

Waveform resonance feasibility check: fix pre-emphasis .97, order-18 autocorrelation LPC on 25 ms Hamming windows at each of three relative positions in the energy-selected voiced frames. Take the lowest two positive-frequency poles between 180 and 4000 Hz with bandwidth below 500 Hz; use median over adjacent frames. Report missing tokens and compare the automatic centered and raw estimates with the matched spectrum control. Reference tracks enter only evaluation. Retain ≥10-point head/had gain as the development target.

The automatic tracker returned all 360 development tokens. On 358 with complete reference tracks, median absolute deviations pooled across three time points were 10 Hz for F1 and 27 Hz for F2 (approximate sampling positions, not identical frame times). On 2520 comparisons per contrast, the centered tracker vs the previous three-part spectrum got head/had 1695 vs 1485, hid/heed 2089 vs 2212, hood/who'd 1993 vs 1852, heed/who'd 2368 vs 2357. Head/had gained 8.3 points, below the 10-point target. Local scripts and tracks archived; no reserved recordings or IPA teaching used.

Duration cue experiment on the existing development contrasts: estimate log span from first to last high-energy frame. Subtract median log span of the four prior recordings per voice. Compare duration only, centered resonances only, and their equal-weight squared log distances (each cue family averaged internally). Perturb query duration alone by factors .8 and 1.25 in feature space, keeping calibration history fixed. Success means ≥10-point improvement on head/had over resonances at natural timing and improvement remaining in both stress conditions. This simulates an unannounced timing shift only.

Natural head/had counts from 2520 shared-speaker comparisons: resonance 1695, duration 1823, combined 1889. Query-duration ×.8 and ×1.25 dropped combined counts to 1547 and 1669, both below the fixed resonance score. Combined natural counts for hid/heed, hood/who'd and heed/who'd were 1884, 1807, 2306, all worse than resonance alone. Natural head/had gain +7.7 points missed its margin. Duration is informative here but unconditional equal weighting fails to generalize. External duration_cue.py reproduces duration-cue.json.

Freeze first reserved-voice naming test: use the existing untaught LPC tracker and high-energy duration without speaker calibration. Fit balanced binary shrinkage LDA on teaching speakers only for each of the four fixed contrasts, using all available complete teaching pairs. Shrink standardized pooled within-category covariance halfway toward identity. Compare six resonance coordinates with the same six plus duration. Count missing estimates as incorrect; use all available reserved tokens. A supplied contrast menu and lexical vowel categories define a supervised restricted-choice task. Threshold is 90% separately on every contrast. Also score simultaneous six-category naming with identical settings. Reserve results are opened once for this specification.

All 68 teaching and 35 reserved speakers had complete estimates. With duration vs without: hid/heed 67 vs 66, head/had 64 vs 63, hood/who'd 61 vs 56, heed/who'd 70 vs 70, all out of 70. Six-category naming was 184 vs 177 of 210. Three binary menus met 90%, hood/who'd missed. Training used 408 distinct labelled tokens in the six-way arm. Natural English hVd context only, supplied lexical targets, no claim of narrow IPA transcription, zero-shot discovery or vocabulary teaching savings. Archive reserved_naming.py and reserved-naming.json.

Freeze a new English cross-corpus transfer probe before scoring: use the six-category source reader exactly as fitted (with and without duration), test every FSDD recording of 3, 6, 2 against broad expected vowel categories iy, ih, uw. No target labels for fitting or calibration. Full six-way menu primary, also report the externally supplied three-category menu. Convert 8 kHz PCM to 16 kHz by fixed bandlimited interpolation. Report results by word and voice; these are expected lexical vowels rather than independently annotated phonetic realizations. Target ≥85% on each word in the full menu. Transfer crosses corpus, recording bandwidth and consonants simultaneously.

Frozen six-way reader with duration: two 122/300, three 113/300, six 226/300, total 461/900. Resonance alone: 149, 186, 133, total 468/900. Restricted to the three anticipated vowels the totals were 514/900 and 507/900 respectively. Full-menu with-duration counts per speaker in lexicographic order were 95/47/52/102/75/90 of 150. The 85% per-word target failed. These repeated recordings cover six voices; no zero-shot lexical meaning claim. FSDD revision 26eb9aaf76e81b692f806f9140c2d2777410d7a1. Reproduce with digit_transfer.py and inspect digit-transfer.json in the phonetic-foundation archive.

Bandwidth fork: low-pass the original 16 kHz tokens with an 81-tap windowed sinc, decimate to 8 kHz, then use the frozen digits interpolation back to 16 kHz. Cross original/matched teaching with original/matched reserved words and identical 900 digit recordings. Primary measure is six-way recognition with duration. Require a ≥10-point digit gain to call matching materially helpful. Compare identical vowel-class subsets separately from all six source classes.

Source-trained wide reader: 184/210 native vs 167/210 degraded; restricting evaluation to the three digit vowel classes but retaining all six options, 95 vs 92 of 105. Narrow-trained reader: 167 native vs 158 degraded of 210 (88 vs 82 of 105). Identical digit test wide vs narrow training: 461 vs 530/900 (+7.7 points), improvements on two 122→139, three 113→138, six 226→253. All 900 wide predictions reproduced exactly. Matching helped on digits, missed the 10-point margin, and reduced recognition on simulated narrow source words. Changing the bandwidth alone on the corresponding source vowel subset caused only a 2.9-point drop. External bandwidth_fork.py and bandwidth-fork.json.

Grounding feasibility replay on the already-open English digits: use three anonymous objects and identical recorded lessons and queries in two constructed communities. In one, three words denote distinct objects; in the other the disputed word denotes the anchor object, while the third word stays distinct. Rotate the disputed word and use each voice as teacher for every different test voice. First two pointing lessons (anchor and unrelated) are identical; the third is the disputed word, with only its pointer changed. Query on independently hash-ordered takes, one per word per voice. Score both-community correctness on the disputed word and complete three-word sets in both communities. Require 80% on both; include a basic mean spectrum nearest-demo learner. This is a bounded closed-set replay with supplied menus, synthetic meanings, and natural English audio; target examples include consonants too.

Across 90 ordered teacher–query–rotation cases from six reused speakers, the categorical vowel reader correctly followed the changed pointer in both worlds on 23/90 disputed-word cases and got both complete three-word sets on 3/90. Mean-spectrum nearest example got 36/90 and 3/90. Four of six teachers already produced duplicate category readings for different lesson words, precluding perfect downstream separation from those discrete outputs alone. This is a failure of this hard-category interface in this replay; no complete spoken-language or kernel transfer claim. Raw decisions in grounded-digit-replay.json.

Replay identical community histories with the frozen six squared class distances, subtracting the per-token mean distance and comparing the vectors by Euclidean distance. Compare hard label, soft evidence and average spectrum. Use ranks (0,1) of the established hash ordering for reproduction and all 24 remaining disjoint pairs (2,3) through (48,49) for replication across takes of the same six speakers. Keep the 80% primary gate; score complete sets separately. No target fitting.

On original recordings the six scores gave 48/90 disputed and 9/90 complete vs hard 23/90 and 3/90. On remaining recordings six scores gave 952/2160 disputed and 111/2160 complete vs hard 513 and 45, average spectrum 875 and 48. Cases heavily reuse speakers, and rotations repeat the complete triplet decision. Extra continuous evidence survives hard classification, but exact-triplet performance remains poor and both gates failed. Local digit_scores.py and grounded_scores.py reproduce scores and outcomes.

Freeze an ordered whole-word comparison on the same opened digit replay: trim to first/last frame above 1% peak power, retain all intervening frames, describe four consecutive quarters using 16 log spectral bands per frame centered over bands. Compare ordered vs time-averaged profiles on exactly the same frames, reverse only query quarters, and compare middle two vs outer two quarters. Keep demonstrations, tie handling and 80% disputed/complete gates unchanged. These are time intervals, without annotated consonant boundaries.

Across the 2160 recurring-speaker cases, ordered quarters gave 1188 disputed /342 complete vs mean 900/57, reversed query 715/6, inner quarters 1074/210 and outer quarters 1206/399. On initial 90 cases ordered 51/18 vs mean 41/3. Sequence is informative, especially near the edges of these three words, but the primary gate fails.
