Complete-set outcomes repeat over rotations; these are developmental cases, not independent deployments. Raw file grounded-ordered.json from grounded_ordered.py.

Fresh lexical panel: all 35 triples among the seven FSDD digits outside 2/3/6, all six known query voices, two successive disjoint query blocks of ten takes each. Freeze ordered four-quarter descriptor vs identical collapsed mean. Supply 1, 2 or 4 examples per word, from one different speaker or as many distinct non-query voices in cyclic order. Use nearest individual demonstration and evaluate complete three-word sets (equivalent to complete sets under both supplied pointer conventions for unique matches). Require 85% on both blocks; report unresolved thresholds. Count all 3k demonstrations. No source fitting or target tuning.

Out of 2100 complete-set cases per block, ordered hearing with 3/6/12 demonstrations from distinct voices gave 569/877/1195 and 605/850/1154, respectively. With all 12 from one voice it gave 841/887; four voices with time-collapsed profiles gave 700/730. Neither block reached 85%, so no time-to-mastery or teaching-saving claim. The six target voices and recordings are reused across triples; the seven lexical items were new to this grounding replay. No human semantics or separately learned phones were supplied to the matcher. External fresh_seven_grounding.py and fresh-seven-grounding.json.

Controlled tone probe before fitting: 96 seeded synthetic installations, each with fresh reference and query voice parameters, independently drawn baseline pitch, duration, amplitude and vowel-like resonances. Contrast a six-semitone rise vs fall with identical endpoints in reverse order. Estimate pitch from waveform periodicity and compare centered early/middle/late log estimates; controls collapse pitch to its mean or reverse the query. Both query directions must be recognized. Map the two teacher utterances to distinct vs shared objects in matched worlds, permuting object identities by installation. Require ≥90% individual cross-voice recognition and ≥80% joint correct objects for both sounds in both worlds. This supplies pitch as an acoustic primitive and a curated contrast, without a learned tone inventory.

Contour reader scored 192/192 individual queries and 96/96 complete two-community installations. Mean pitch scored 96/192 and 0/96 complete, reversing the query thirds gave 0/192 and 0/96. Same-object worlds alone are trivial; the joint criterion also requires correctly distinguishing both directions. This is a direct two-demo nearest-example mapping using supplied pairing, no active inquiry, natural tonal-language result or kernel deployment. External controlled_tone.py and controlled-tone.json.

Synthetic connected-tone feasibility: freeze 96 new seeds with a half-second-or-shorter rise/fall inserted among two level syllables, target order and sign crossed. Paired worlds reuse identical syllable durations and noise; in stress world randomly offset each syllable's pitch register by up to three semitones. No pauses or supplied boundaries. Recover pitch frames and choose the 240 ms window with greatest absolute median-log-pitch change from first to last third. Require midpoint inside target and correct direction jointly on ≥90% in each condition. Score equal-window zero-evidence control on matched all-level streams. Generator coordinates used only for scoring.

Joint location/direction fell to 49/96 with a common register and 33/96 with offsets (located: 50,34; sign correct: 51,42). Among correctly located windows sign was correct on 49/50 and 33/34. Matched level controls scored 1 and 17 chance joint coincidences against the removed target. No abstention threshold was fitted. This selects a 21-frame window (250 ms waveform support, correcting the approximate 240 ms description above); midpoint scoring does not verify complete boundaries. The first divergence on these constructed streams is choosing the window. External connected_tone.py and connected-tone.json.

Connected-tone follow-up on 96 fresh simulated voices. For a fixed 25-frame window compute median log pitch in five blocks, and take the weakest of four signed changes in the proposed direction. Require all four steps to exceed 0.20 semitone, else abstain. Compare endpoint score on the same fresh waveforms. Gate: ≥90% joint correct midpoint and direction and ≤5% false detections on all-level sequences in both register conditions. No target timings or syllable count enter the listener.

On the 96 new installations the consistency rule correctly located and named 96/96 contours at each register setting, versus 41/96 and 24/96 using the earlier endpoint rule. It abstained on all 96 matched level sequences in each setting. The paired settings use the same voices. Both gates passed in this synthetic generator, whose level carriers and monotonic six-semitone contours favor this prior. This does not establish learned boundaries, shallow or nonmonotonic tone recognition, or natural speech. Reproduce with tone_consistency.py and inspect tone-consistency.json in the external study archive.

Natural tone transfer pilot: use every syllable in the pinned Mandarin tone trainer audio subset with tone 2 and tone 4 for both FV1 and MV1. Preserve the frozen synthetic consistency threshold, treat abstentions/too-short/untrackable tokens as misses. Decode mono 8 kHz; trim outer silence using first/last 10 ms block exceeding 1% maximum block energy. Primary 90% per tone per speaker. No target fitting. This is isolated citation-form audio, no connected-speech localization labels.

Tone Perfect (Michigan State University) audio distributed in jacqueline-1929/mandarin_tone_trainer revision 8477f953d4c2665d2e2d9db95f02da7d178da84a. Eleven matched syllables × two voices × two tones. FV1 rising/falling 11/11 each; MV1 rising 11/11, falling 2/11. Nine abstentions for MV1 falling: six trimmed clips shorter than required window and three with insufficient monotonic evidence. Overall 35/44, all emitted judgments correct, one of four cells missed the gate. Natural citation-form pilot only. Raw decisions natural-tone-pilot.json and script natural_tone_pilot.py.

Freeze fallback: try the 25-frame rule first, then 15 frames (five blocks of three) only on abstention, same minimum 0.2 semitone per step. Retest old 44 clips and separately take the first eight alphabetically eligible *new syllables* per tone 1/2/4 with both existing speakers. Tone 1 is a lexical high-level control: count emitted rise/fall as false for the lexical task, irrespective of the phonetic contour. Require ≥90% correct in each new direction/voice cell and ≤5% directional emissions per voice on tone 1. Same sources/voices, disjoint syllables.

On the opened pilot, baseline→fallback MV1 falling 2→10/11, other three cells 11→11/11. On eight new syllables per category, FV1 rise/fall 8/8 each; MV1 rise 5/8 and fall 4/8 vs 2/8 baseline fall. Both rules abstained on all 16 new lexical tone-1 recordings. Fresh direction accuracy 25/32 vs 23/32 baseline. The larger pilot recovery did not replicate in magnitude and two voice/contrast gates failed. Same two speakers; small denominators. External natural_tone_short.py and natural-tone-short.json.

Saved the 56-second tone listening replay from the seeded two-community and connected-tone trials. It re-runs the recorded classifier and location decision, presents the same test waveform under changed teaching pointers and replays a baseline localization failure. All audible examples are controlled synthesis. The last card reports the natural Mandarin result without redistributing corpus audio. Verified both stream durations and full movie decode. External listening_replay.py regenerates it.

Packaged sustained-tone in nca-sound-foundations 0.4.0. Built and installed a wheel into a separate target directory, launched a fresh Python process, discovered the package entry point and invoked three typed requests through Kernel/Workspace. Falling and rising 400 ms sweeps returned correct direction and in-range midpoint; level returned None. Single-call times 14.27/7.89/7.27 ms, including planning but excluding process startup/install. Six package tests passed. This verifies serving, not broader language transfer.

Installed-consumer pilot: cache actual typed kernel calls for each of the 44 opened matched Mandarin clips, using sustained-tone and the installed fine-direction control. For each ordered distinct syllable pair and opposite voices, provide two lessons with object pointers, then evaluate both query tones in a contrastive and a merger community. A categorical lookup skips missing evidence, abstains on conflicting associations, and sees only kernel receipts plus lesson pointers. Require 80% joint success over both communities and both query tokens. This is an engineered object convention over real sound and a previously opened panel.

Installed sustained-tone jointly solved 100/110 cross-syllable assignments in each teacher direction (200/220 overall) vs fine-direction 3/110 in each (6/220). All 220 assignments reuse 44 clips from 11 syllables and two speakers. Measured 44 unique calls per expert; p95 9.95 ms sustained vs 0.96 ms earlier, excluding decoding and install. Combined Python consumer peak RSS 258064384 bytes. The consumer learned only the mapping from two receipts to pointers; the acoustic contrast and lesson pair were supplied. No natural referent identification or teaching-efficiency claim. Raw installed-mandarin-grounding.json and installed_mandarin_grounding.py.

Controlled aspiration foundation: 128 new seeded cross-voice ABX installations. Synthesize brief noisy release, a short (10–25 ms) or long (55–85 ms) aperiodic interval, then a voiced resonant vowel. Independently vary pitch, resonance, amplitude, leading silence, vowel duration and noise realization. Match voiced-onset time relative to detected acoustic release, using periodicity only, with generator timestamps excluded. Cross ordinary timing with equal total post-release duration within each pair. Compare total duration. Require ≥90% individual ABX in both conditions and median absolute interval error ≤12 ms. This assesses positive voice onset time in constructed pseudowords only.

Across 128 installations per condition, release-to-periodicity matching got 256/256 short/long judgments in each condition. Median absolute timing errors were 8.875 ms ordinary, 8.75 ms equal duration. Active total-length control got 141/256 and 90/256 (ties count as misses). Both gates passed for separated positive-lag ranges under synthesis; no natural speech, negative VOT, place recognition or IPA naming tested. Script aspiration_abx.py saves aspiration-abx.json.

Natural aspiration pilot: the pinned subset has just one same-rime, same-tone stop pair, da4/ta4 (two voices). Freeze the synthetic detector and nearest-reference ABX in both teacher directions. Score expected within-voice ordering separately, plus whole active duration control. No independently annotated VOT or broader natural generalisation claim from four clips.

Detector estimates (ms) for da4/ta4 were 12/16 (FV1) and 22/116 (MV1). The expected ordering held within each voice; in each transfer direction both query clips matched the same reference (1/2 correct, neither complete pair). Active duration also yielded 1/2 each. Without annotated boundaries these values do not establish actual articulation timings, especially the apparent 4 ms contrast. Reproduce with natural_aspiration.py. More natural matched contrasts and reference boundaries are needed.

Independent English timing audit, AutoVOT tutorialExample/test: use all positive manually labeled VOT intervals. Give detector a coarse externally supplied search region from the nearest stop phone (closure start through 120 ms after phone end); this is a cued diagnostic. Select nearest stop to VOT midpoint on evaluator only. Compare its predicted release and voicing offsets with manual endpoints, and rerun periodicity search starting exactly at manual release. Count missing estimates. Freeze ≤12 ms median absolute duration error and report voiced/voiceless lists separately. No fitting or AutoVOT classifier use.

All 58 intervals returned estimates. In voiced (26), median absolute release/voicing/duration errors were 40.0/115.8/76.5 ms; supplying manual release reduced duration error to 10.0 ms. In voiceless (32), errors were 50.0/8.0/50.0 ms; manual release reduced duration error to 7.0 ms. Coarse-only failed both margins; release-conditioned passed both. Diagnostic supports prioritizing release localization on these English fixtures. It cannot explain any specific Mandarin clip. AutoVOT git revision 7901092b870cde2d2e8a985deca9d01baffcecfc. Raw per-interval results and annotated_aspiration.py in external archive.

Release localization follow-up: fixed first-difference energy contrast over adjacent 8 ms blocks. Maximize log ratio with a floor of 0.1% peak first-difference energy, within the same externally supplied search region. Compare absolute release and duration errors with the previous onset rule and a coarse phone-end timing control. Run on opened tutorial test and independently on the tutorial train directory without fitting. Report missing detections and coverage within 12 ms, counting misses as failures.

Correction superseding the previous 58-interval report: AutoVOT's tutorial test files use a window tier named vot for decoding; it cannot serve as manual release/voicing ground truth. The prior 40/50 ms release errors and apparent oracle gain on those files do not establish release accuracy. The manual training annotations provide 150 usable intervals. On those (no fit), the burst rule localized release with median absolute errors 1.1 ms voiced and 0.5 ms voiceless vs 93.8 and 89.6 ms with first energy. Duration errors were 6.8 and 7.9 ms; 58/75 and 47/75 within 12 ms. First-energy duration error on voiced stops was deceptively small (2.1 ms) despite both endpoints being misplaced. Evaluation uses externally cued windows and one corpus. Files release_flux.py and release-flux-train.json preserve results; test results retained as window diagnostics only.

Uncued target-release retrieval on the same 150 manual AutoVOT intervals. Rank bursts over the entire decoded waveform using the fixed 8 ms first-difference energy contrast. Suppress a 40 ms radius after each pick and keep five. Compare top-1/3/5 coverage within 12 ms against equally spaced midpoints (separate grids per budget). No annotations, target identity, or transcript in proposal generation. Require ≥80% first-choice and ≥90% five-candidate target coverage separately per group. Additional candidate events can be genuine releases unmarked on the target tier; this cannot measure all-stop precision.

Whole-utterance coverage within 12 ms: top 1/3/5 retrieved 7/24/31 of 75 voiced and 6/27/39 of 75 voiceless targets. Equal-grid counts were 1/1/2 and 0/0/0. Both first-choice and five-candidate gates failed. This contrasts with strong timing given an external local window; no independent-speaker or precision claim. Reproduce with uncued_bursts.py train; per-utterance predictions in uncued-bursts.json.

Context ranker on whole-utterance burst candidates: keep up to 20 peaks with existing 40 ms suppression; score top 1/5 and candidate ceiling within 12 ms. Fit a balanced ridge discriminator (unit penalty on standardized features) using burst score, short-time energy and first-difference energy before/after, and post-burst periodicity. Compare burst-only ordering. Hold out entire numbered utterance groups together across their repetitions via fixed modulo-five folds. No absolute utterance time, filename, phone annotations or target category enter the model. This supervised development test uses previously opened annotations.

Context vs burst-only top-1: 29 vs 7 of 75 voiced, 53 vs 6 of 75 voiceless. Top-5: 44 vs 31 voiced, 66 vs 39 voiceless. All 110 reachable references were in the contextual top five; 40/150 were absent even from the 20-candidate pool (31 voiced, 9 voiceless). Neither group reached the top-1 gate. Verified with explicit numerical contractions under warnings-as-errors. No evidence here for independent-speaker transfer. External ranked_release_context.py train.

Equal-budget suppression test: change only the candidate suppression radius from 40 ms to 12 ms, refit the same ranker under identical folds and 20 proposals, compare top-1/5/20 coverage and per-interval candidate recovery/loss against the archived run. Require ≥8 additional voiced candidates without any net voiceless loss to pursue this setting.

Short-radius candidate coverage rose from 44 to 68/75 voiced (+24 recovered, zero lost) and 66 to 71/75 voiceless (+7 recovered, two lost). Contextual first-choice correct rose 29→44 and 53→60 respectively; top-five captured all 139 reachable targets. The suppression hypothesis passed its development gate. Eleven remaining intervals lack a proposal. These are previously opened annotated fixtures; no fresh-speaker validation. Script ranked_release_short_radius.py train.

Place feasibility audit: all 150 matched AutoVOT train targets are P/B under the supplied phone tier, so that panel cannot evaluate place. In the existing Mandarin subset the complete unaspirated same-rime/same-tone pairs are ba3/da3 and duo3/guo3 for both speakers. No complete aspirated pair. Evaluate them all in both teacher directions. Freeze energy onset (first 2 ms block above 0.9% peak energy); compare normalized eight-band log spectra on the following 24 ms vs a 24 ms midpoint control, by nearest example. Treat ties or unavailable inputs as misses. No target fitting. A pilot success requires both directions correct for each place pair and teacher.

Initial spectrum matched 6/8 natural place queries vs 4/8 midpoint; initial succeeded on both pairs with FV1 as teacher and collapsed to one answer for each pair with MV1 as teacher. Four complete cross-voice pair tests, two passed vs zero midpoint. No annotated release boundaries or independent lexical replication; thus onset-region evidence only. Raw mandarin-stop-place.json and mandarin_stop_place.py reproduce the pilot.

Mandarin manner pilot prediction, before scoring. Across all five FV1 inventory matches for x/j with identical written remainder and tone, test the existing first-24-ms spectrum and midpoint control with the two previous voices. Predict higher accuracy at onset. Each direction uses the other voice as its only reference. Report missing recordings and pair-level failures.

All 20 recordings available. Early/middle correct by matched pair (four decisions each): xi1–ji1 1/3, xi3–ji3 2/1, xiao4–jiao4 2/4, xin1–jin1 2/4, xin4–jin4 2/2. Totals 9/20 and 14/20. The prediction failed. One static spectrum gives no temporal release profile; the midpoint advantage cannot identify which cue drove it. Two voices, reciprocal comparisons; no population inference or expert change. Local reproduction: python3 mandarin_manner.py in the phonetic-foundation research archive.

Exploratory follow-up on the same 20 x/j clips. Test four successive 24-ms spectral frames starting 12 ms apart, with adjacent frame log-energy changes, against a collapsed time-average of the same spectra. Both use nearest reference and cross voice. Predict that retaining time improves discrimination. These clips are open development evidence.

Ordered frames plus energy changes scored 8/20; time-averaged spectra scored 9/20. Both reversed all four xi1/ji1 decisions. Sequential windows at this alignment and simple nearest-reference comparison did not fix the pilot. No fresh named speaker present in this pinned subset for xin1. Leave the installed expert unchanged. Raw predictions and reproduction in external mandarin-manner-time.json and mandarin_manner_time.py.

Onset diagnostic on open x/j clips. On xi1_FV1 the 8-kHz energy trigger fired at 240.2 ms, while three consecutive native-rate 10-ms frames exceeded 1% of peak 4–15-kHz power starting at 20 ms. For ji1_MV1 the values were 90 and 0 ms. This is a signal landmark, not a human-annotated boundary. Replacing only the trigger yielded 10/20 ordered and 11/20 averaged (previously 8 and 9); on xi1/ji1 both went from 0/4 to 2/4. Alignment affects errors but this substitution still leaves accuracy near chance. Source audio is 44.1 kHz; all the tested classifiers discard energy above 4 kHz even with the revised trigger. Reproduction: onset_audit.py and mandarin_realign.py in the external archive.

Bandwidth ablation on the 20 open Mandarin x/j recordings. Fix native decode, same high-band trigger, four 24-ms windows, 12-ms stride, 500-Hz spectral bins. Compare separately centered and dimension-normalized 0–4 and 4–12 kHz shape blocks and their equal-weight concatenation. Predict adding the upper block improves both voice directions. Disclose each changed decision. Development diagnostic only.

Bandwidth scores with FV1 / MV1 as reference respectively: low 5/10 and 6/10, high 8/10 and 8/10, both 5/10 and 8/10. Prediction of improvement in both directions failed. Adding high to low corrected MV1-reference ji1, ji3, xin4 and FV1-reference xiao4; it broke jiao4 in both directions. High alone was best here, below the 90% target; choosing it now would require independent confirmation. No change to installed reader.

Freeze Mandarin bandwidth extractor SHA256 00c10743e69ff1e6a3eac0ae083e4bb548898d31d621b064a1d24ac372afa2ad. Secondary context-transfer screen: use all previously unscored x/j syllable-tone forms recorded by both named voices. Compare the nearest of the opposite voice's original ten exemplars, no matching by rhyme or tone. Report recall per initial, macro-average, and counts per speaker; unmatched contexts and scarce j forms limit attribution. No speaker novelty claim.

On ten additional forms spoken by each voice, frozen high band scored FV1 j 1/1, x 7/9 and MV1 j 0/1, x 8/9: 16/20 raw, 66.7% macro recall. Low scored 7/20, 41.7% macro recall; combined scored 16/20, 88.9% macro recall. Always predicting x scores 18/20 raw, 50% macro recall. Neither superiority on balanced novel contexts nor novel-speaker mastery is demonstrated. Only jiao1 supplied new j examples. No package promotion.

Freeze balanced x/j screen: FV2 MV2 FV3 MV3; original ten forms plus j/x with ian2 ing1 iong3 iao2. Pool both original voices as nearest references. Primary high band, secondary low and both. Score each stratum per speaker.

All 72 files scored. Frozen high band: familiar forms 28/40, new forms 20/32. Per-voice totals FV2 14/18, MV2 10/18, FV3 13/18, MV3 11/18. Low 45/72, combined 49/72. Thus upper-band advantage over low was only three decisions across four voices. Below 90% target. Audio from Level Up Mandarin's attributed Tone Perfect service; predictions in mandarin-four-voices.json. No core or expert change.

Duration diagnostic: from first sustained 4–15 kHz activity to first sustained low-band vowel energy (100–1500 Hz above 10% of its peak for three 10-ms frames). Fit class medians on the 20 original FV1/MV1 clips. Predict nearest median on the 72 now-open recordings. Confirm separately without refitting on j/x matched with ie2, ia3, iang2, ue4 in all four other voices (32 clips). Missing landmarks count as misses.

Original-reference medians j 110 ms and x 200 ms. Landmark duration classified 72/72 previously opened clips plus 32/32 reserved forms (8/8 each voice). Fresh j range 60–130 ms; x 210–300 ms. Post-hoc matched whole-recording-length control scored 51/72 and 20/32. A supervised, analyst-specified acoustic measurement succeeds in this single corpus; production discovery, cross-corpus robustness and downstream teaching benefit remain separate. External scripts mandarin_duration_landmark.py and mandarin_duration_whole.py.

Rate stress test: fixed 110/200-ms original reference medians; FFmpeg atempo 0.75 and 1.5 on the same 32 reserved-form recordings. Report per-class recall and all changed decisions. Predict slowing disproportionately hurts j and acceleration hurts x. Synthetic interventions, no refitting.

Slowed: j 16/16, x 16/16. Accelerated: j 16/16, x 14/16. Only xiang2 MV2 (150 ms) and MV3 (140 ms) crossed the 155-ms boundary, both into j. Slow-j prediction failed; fast-x prediction supported on these examples. Digital time stretching tests waveform sensitivity, not natural changes of speaking style.

Exploratory grounded selection. Supply three octave-scale band onsets (100–1500, 1500–4000, 4000–15000 Hz) each at 1% and 10% of its peak; offer six absolute onsets, fifteen pairwise differences, file duration. Select by cross-voice source accuracy, ties by listed order. Compare opposite arbitrary pointing conventions. Test separately on fresh balanced ian4 and un1 forms across FV2/MV2/FV3/MV3; no test-dependent choice. Acoustic operations supplied; offline selector.

Both mappings selected candidate 12 (high-band 1%-onset minus low-band 1%-onset). Cross-voice source validation 19/20. On the same 16 previously unused recordings, each mapping pointed correctly 16/16. Reversing all source pointers reversed all 16 answers. These are one set of paired tests and two artificial mappings. Selection used labelled examples, 22 supplied features and a human-designed search space. Direct Python analysis; no new kernel capability established.

Registered wideband onset service in sound foundations 0.5.0. Built wheel, installed separately, discovered entry point from a fresh process; kernel_manner_selection.py measured six landmarks per waveform through actual invocation. Paired grounded choices exactly matched offline JSON, both 16/16 with reversed pointers. Selection/difference composition still runs in the external evaluation. Package tests 6 passed.

Freeze teaching-cost pilot. Artificial two-referent Mandarin-initial convention. FV2/MV2 give identical cumulative 2/4/8 examples to retained cue 12, reset equal-prior cue selector (leave-one-out error when possible, ties by order), and whole-length control. Opposite object mapping to source. Target class medians fit anew in all arms. FV3/MV3 each supply a balanced fresh block at every checkpoint, two new rimes/tones per block. Threshold 85% on each speaker block; report restricted grid and prior 20 labels. No natural-language transfer claim.

Retained / reset / whole length correct (each out of eight): at two labels 8/8/4, at four labels 7/8/6, at eight labels 8/8/6. Both retained and reset reached criterion on the two first fresh speaker blocks after two examples, the earliest tested level. No measured marginal teaching saving; retained used 20 prior labels. Reset chose feature zero, absolute low-band onset, under the prespecified tie order. This control can exploit leading silence; test onset-shift robustness separately before attributing portable phonetic knowledge. No change to installed package.

Frozen two-label delay test, all 24 existing probe recordings, same waveform with 0, 87 and 250 ms leading silence. Compare cue 12, absolute low onset, and low onset minus earliest of six band onsets; identical median fitter and training audio. Predict loss only for absolute cue; 87 ms also changes frame alignment.

Of 24 unique probes, absolute cue scored 24/24 with no padding and 12/24 at either delay. Retained and simple relative control each scored 24/24 in all three paired conditions with identical two labels. Relative timing is sufficient for this robustness benefit; no retained-policy advantage over the cheap aligned baseline. These are repeated synthetic forks of isolated speech.

Prefix intervention: prepend same-speaker ji1 or xi1 to each of 24 prior probes; each prefix crosses both target classes. Compare unchanged two-label cue on whole clip, evaluator join, and blind split at lowest 30-ms energy in the middle half. Predict join restores isolated decisions. File margins retained; constructed two-syllable sequences.

Whole sequence 24/48; known join 48/48; lowest-energy split 48/48. Across same 24 target tokens with two crossed prefixes, the supplied two-syllable structure and preserved file-edge pauses suffice for the simple splitter. This isolates a selection-of-region failure without establishing continuous-speech segmentation.

Freeze tight-splice intervention on prior 48 sequences. Trim each recording to first/last 10-ms frame above 1% peak broadband power, overlap by 10 ms with linear crossfade. Use first mixed target sample as reference boundary. Score prior midpoint-valley splitter, whole and true boundary unchanged; report localization within ±30 ms independently of classification. Trim can remove quiet target evidence; true boundary arm tests that.

Tight splice: whole 24/48, known boundary 48/48, valley 42/48. Valley median absolute boundary error 10 ms; within 30 ms 37/48, all 37 correct. Of 11 farther splits, 5 were correct. Thus classification alone would overstate localization. Reused target recordings and supplied two-token structure; no natural coarticulation. Predictions in grounded-manner-tight.json.

Natural sentence-final feasibility screen. In 40 pinned phrase transcriptions, four end in x/j (25858 jiu, 26450 xie, 25931 xia, 26348 xin). No word boundaries. Apply original two-example cue to last syllable sought by a blind minimum-energy 30-ms split between 100 and 500 ms before final active frame (1% utterance peak). Report all four predictions; this single-j fixture cannot validate mastery or localization.

Natural phrase screen: 2/4, j 1/1 and x 1/3; always x 3/4. Correct jiu and xin, missed xie and xia. No timestamp labels, so cannot assign errors to split or cue. Pinyin used only for eligibility and scoring. Kernel natural_phrase_final.py, raw natural-phrase-final.json.

Evaluator-only suffix sweep on all four open natural phrases: every 10-ms start from 500 to 100 ms before the last active frame inclusive. Fixed references; count correct windows separately per utterance and longest consecutive run. A positive oracle result establishes reachability only, not a valid phonetic boundary.

Correct windows out of 41: jiu 41, xia 0, xin 4 (one consecutive run), xie 0. Even a label-informed choice among these 41 starts cannot improve the original 2/4 sentence score. Does not rule out other boundaries, windows, landmark definitions or per-speaker calibration. Sweep trials reuse four utterances.

Independent duration diagnostic from first 10 test rows of changelinglab/thchs30-segment, speaker D11. Strip duration marks; exclude aspirates. Forced-alignment intervals (metadata, not manual or acoustic model output by Elisa): tɕ 12 tokens median 80 ms, 30–100; ɕ 20 tokens median 90 ms, 30–160. Applying 155-ms isolated-landmark threshold to those different interval definitions gives 12/12 vs 1/20. Evidence of duration overlap in connected read speech; no waveform discrimination/localization claim. Audit thchs_duration_audit.py and thchs-duration-audit.json external.

Freeze aligned-start acoustic screen on same 32 THCHS tokens. Supply MFA start and next 300 ms regardless of phone end; use installed kernel's high onset (1%) and low onset (10%), comparing low minus high to 155 ms. Score non-detection as error. Original 16 kHz corpus limits available high band to 8 kHz. Report one-speaker recall.

Aligned-start waveform screen: tɕ 12/12, median acoustic interval 60 ms; ɕ 0/20, one non-detection, median 90 ms among 19 detected. Balanced recall 50%. This 300-ms crop measures first band onsets within the clip (including subsequent speech); it is not a phone duration estimate or a test of autonomous localization.

Freeze paired bandwidth intervention on the 32 previously reserved isolated forms. Original waveform, or FFmpeg resample to 16 kHz then back to 44.1 kHz. Apply identical installed onsets and 155-ms cutoff. Report detection and both recalls; source-side bandwidth alone predicts the connected-speech collapse only if x recall drops substantially.

Native and 16-kHz round trip both yielded 16/16 j and 16/16 x, zero missing, identical group medians 100 and 260 ms respectively. This matched manipulation cannot reproduce the connected-speech failure. Corpus/speaker/style and supplied crop differ; no unique causal attribution to coarticulation.

Freeze connected-speech calibration transfer: midpoint of D11 class medians 75 ms, compared with 155 ms on 10 consecutive official test utterances starting at offset 1000. Verify speaker disjointness. Same externally aligned 300-ms crop, missing cue counted wrong. Report per-class recall and balanced accuracy.

Offset 1000 cohort was D6, 15 tokens each. D11-calibrated cutoff 25/30 (15/15 j, 10/15 x) vs original 17/30 (15/15, 2/15). Eight additional x correct, one x missing; calibrated balanced accuracy 83.3%, below 90%. Supervised calibration used 32 D11 labels, alignment supplied in both corpora arms. No autonomous localization or teaching savings inferred.

Freeze third-speaker evaluation: ten test rows at offset 2000, verify disjoint speaker. Same 75-ms D11 threshold, 300-ms crops at aligned start and ±20 ms. Include 155-ms cutoff at nominal start. Report both classes for all offsets, misses counted wrong.

The prespecified block crossed a speaker boundary (D21 and D7). Retained both. Aligned cutoff 75 scored 11/12 D21, 10/20 D7 (j 6/6 and 5/7; x 5/6 and 5/13). Pooled 21/32 vs 12/32 at 155 ms. Earlier crops 21/32, later crops 20/32. Strong between-speaker heterogeneity; no broad transfer or independent boundary-finding claim.

Exhaustive evaluator-only within-speaker cutoff bound on the 94 existing nominal-start connected tokens. Maximize mean recall over both classes, every observed interval threshold plus all-x; missing remains a miss. Fixed 75 ms vs best hindsight balanced accuracy: D11 90.0/90.0%, D21 91.7/91.7%, D6 83.3/83.3%, D7 54.9/67.0%. Even omniscient threshold selection cannot reach 90% on two panels. Narrow conclusion: more speaker-specific cutoff tuning cannot repair this fixed scalar decision rule on these crops; test complementary waveform evidence on disjoint material. Reproduce with thchs_cutoff_bound.py.

Freeze timing vs timing plus band rise: source all prior 30 sentences. Source-standardized nearest class mean (each arm drops incomplete training vectors, missing test predictions count as misses). Rise is registered high-band 10%-minus-1% onset. Test first disjoint speaker block in fixed offset sequence 1500, 500, 2300, 750 (10 sentences per block, reject previously seen speakers before accessing labels). Report per-class recall and paired flips.

All four candidate test blocks contained a prior speaker. Before scoring, change independent cohort to first ten validation rows, contingent on speaker disjointness; retain source and estimator.

Validation rows cover five disjoint speakers; 40 tokens. Duration 9/12 j and 26/28 x (83.9% balanced); duration+rise 8/12 and 26/28 (79.8% balanced). Zero repaired and one spoiled decision. This rise statistic adds no observed benefit. External thchs_rise.py/results; externally supplied starts remain a diagnostic.

Open-set diagnostic before scoring: same source and opened validation sentences as rise test, add IPA s, ʂ, ts, ʈʂ, tɕʰ distractors. Nearest source median by phone using installed timing interval; second arm adds eight log-energy bands (1 kHz each, first 40 ms, mean-centered) with source standardization and equal block weight. Pool distractor outputs as other. No detection abstains (wrong for target). Report target recall, distractor false accepts and denominators. Forced boundaries, supervised reference only.

With five known distractor classes competing, timing identified j 0/12 and x 3/28 while falsely accepting 8/80 distractors. Adding spectrum raised exact target hits to 4/12 and 4/28, and false accepts to 16/80. All candidate starts provided. Prior binary discrimination substantially overstates target identification in this seven-class reference.

Error audit suggests place evidence: 16/28 x classified s by timing+onset spectrum. Predict later spectral shape helps in opened seven-way diagnostic. Hold 8 bands and dimensionality fixed; move 40-ms window from 0 to +40ms. Keep same class centers procedure, source/eval split. Evaluate exact target hits and false accepts, as well as x→s errors. Later window may include vowel context.

Window shift failed: x→s 16/28 at both placements. Exact j/x 0/12 and 6/28 late vs 4/12 and 4/28 early. Other→target 20/80 vs 16/80. Of 32 original target errors, only one was an x↔j swap; remaining 31 were assigned to other phones. Do not advance later-window prototype.

Binary place diagnostic on opened validation material: compare timing vs spectral-only standardized nearest source-class medians. Pair held s and ɕ within speaker, interval difference at most 20 ms, greedy smallest difference first without reuse, deterministic ordering. Count jointly correct pairs and unmatched tokens. No tuning.

Timing recognized 4/5 s and 9/28 ɕ (56.1% balanced); spectral shape 1/5 and 18/28 (42.1%). Only three same-speaker timing-matched pairs qualified. Neither arm got both members right on any pair. Insufficient matched pairs for population inference; more common-class successes do not establish place discrimination.

Validation rows 100–199: 60 disjoint s/ɕ pairs available by same speaker, zero by same speaker and following phone (tone and length stripped). Freeze all 60 pairs, taking first n per class in row order per speaker. Reuse previously frozen 40-ms shape and timing readers. Score both arms without tuning. Following context remains uncontrolled.

Balanced evaluation: timing 62/120 (s 40, ɕ 22), shape 69/120 (s 32, ɕ 37). Of 37 further matched pairs within 20ms, timing solved both on 0 and shape on 6. Fresh utterances; speaker overlap with previously opened validation is possible. Shape conveys limited complementary evidence, far below mastery.

Context diagnostic on previously opened source and balanced validation tokens. Use aligned 20-ms target midpoint vs 20-ms window 10–30 ms after target end, same 8 spectral bands and source-standardized class median rule independently fitted. Restrict both arms to clips supporting both windows, report denominators. Predictions concern labels recoverable in each region; aligned regions diagnostic only.

All 120 probes qualified. Mid-consonant spectrum 70/120 (s 42, ɕ 28); post-consonant spectrum 76/120 (s 35, ɕ 41). Context alone is informative in these aligned clips. This does not identify how much of any other reader's decisions used context, nor exclude imperfect forced boundaries.

Paired feature intervention on the opened balanced diagnostic: concatenate both eight-band windows with equal per-coordinate source standardization, nearest source class median. Pair same-speaker opposite consonants in utterance/start order. Hold target window fixed and exchange context. Negative control: same-label context swap within speaker where at least two examples exist. Compare on identical eligible subsets. Artificial feature swaps; no claim of natural acoustics.

Joint reader 76/120 with original features, 44/120 after opposite-context swap, 36 changed answers. On 102 supporting both controls: 63 original, 39 opposite, 63 same-label; opposite flipped 28 (26 harmed, 2 helped), same-label flipped 26 (13 each direction). Thus class-linked context has directional influence beyond generic perturbation; evidence limited to supplied windows and artificial swaps.

Selective context replay: cost 0.05 per following window, reward 1 correct; margin absolute difference in first-window standardized distances. Choose buy cutoff by source leave-speaker-out mean class-balanced net reward, ties fewer purchases. Compare never, always, selective and evaluator oracle choosing only helpful continuations on same opened 120 probes. Offline feasibility only.

120 probes: never 70 correct, net 70; always and source-selected gate 76 correct after 120 reads, net 70. Hindsight 38 beneficial reads, 108 correct, net 106.1. Context corrected 38 and spoiled 32; the tested margin gate captured no economic advantage. Historical model-fitting and service costs excluded; modeled marginal net only.

Exploratory context-value predictor: fixed standardized ridge regression (penalty 10, intercept unpenalized), eight early spectrum bins plus early margin, train on leave-speaker-out change in correctness for 70 source tokens with equal class weight. Buy if predicted gain exceeds .05. No target fitting. Compare fixed controls and matched random expected reward on 120 opened probes; cluster-bootstrap paired differences by speaker.

Regression bought 106/120, correct 79, marginal net 73.70 vs 70 each fixed control and 70 expected under uniform random 106 buys. Paired mean +0.0308 per token; speaker bootstrap percentile 95% intervals vs never [-.054,.115], vs always [-.008,.086]. Direction promising but uncertain on open data. Recomputed with finite checks and warnings-as-errors. No installed policy change.

Freeze original ridge coefficients and 0.05 fee for validation rows 300–399, first n per class/speaker as before. Verify utterance disjointness against previous windows. Fixed baselines, exact expected matched-random and speaker bootstrap. Previously unseen utterances, no requirement for new speakers.

Fresh 118 tokens: selective 94 reads, 64 correct, net 59.30. Never 75 correct/net 75; always 67 correct, net 61.10; matched random expected net 63.93. Selective minus never −0.133/token, speaker-bootstrap interval [−.199,−.064], vs always [−.066,+.037]. Prior pilot advantage failed to replicate. Do not install gate.

Frozen-policy failure audit. On fresh tokens the 94 bought contexts helped 19 and harmed 30 (predicted mean pre-fee gain +.365, observed −.117); 24 skipped would have helped 10, harmed 7 (predicted −.197, observed +.125). Pairwise score ordering helpful over harmful: 0.475 fresh vs 0.524 development, ties half credit, unchanged decisions excluded. This identifies both calibration and ranking failure. Counterfactuals evaluator-only. No policy change.

Retrospective speaker-experience replay: all 120 earlier block tokens are paid commissioning at .05 with correct referent supplied after action. Use only these settled receipts. Future 118-token block, same fee. Compare speaker-specific mean gain shrunk by four pooled pseudo-observations with pooled mean gain, never and always. No future feedback during scoring. Known identity supplied. Separate history cost and full-deployment net.

Speaker history available on 60/118 later tokens. Speaker policy bought 44, correct 76, net 73.8; pooled and never 75/118 net 75; always net 61.1. Earlier commissioning net 70 including fees (same numeric net as acting immediately throughout history), so totals 143.8 vs 145 for never. One extra correct decision cost 2.20 units. Retrospective cut, artificial guaranteed label feedback, no separate teacher fee modeled. No economic gain.

Ordered word-teaching replay on open English digits 2,3,6. Compare source vowel-score vector and four-window spectrum with identical nearest-demonstration rule. One teaching voice, one different testing voice, 1,2,4,8 examples per word. Two disjoint 5-per-word probe blocks per checkpoint from hash ranks 8–47. Criterion >=85% per block in both; unreached counted explicitly. Same-language diagnostic, not held-out-language evidence.

30 directed pairs from six voices. Spectrum reached criterion in 5 pairs after 3 labels, 4 more after 6, 21 unreached through 24. Vowel scores reached in 1 after 3, 1 after 6, 1 after 24, 27 unreached. Historical vowel transfer representation did not buy target teaching savings. Overlapping voices across pairs and three-word menu constrain inference.

Word evidence fusion on open digit curves: concatenate raw blocks scaled by median nonzero pairwise demonstration distance separately at each checkpoint. Equal and quarter-strength vowel distances (multiply coordinates by 1 or 0.5); no probe scaling. Compare prior spectrum counts and pair-level reached/lost; exploratory only.

Equal-weight reached 9/30 directed pairs (one added, one lost); quarter-weight reached 12/30 (3 added, none lost) vs spectrum 9/30. With three demonstrations: quarter-weight 8/30 vs spectrum 5/30. Same open English digits, reused voices and two exploratory weights; no held-out-language teaching-savings claim.

First multilingual contrast pilot. Fit nearest median of high/low spectral energy ratio for exact IPA s vs m using only English rows 4500–4503 and 5000–5003. Frozen evaluation on all previously downloaded Belarusian, Catalan, French and Swahili rows. Take central 20 ms of intervals >=20 ms, supplied alignment, no test-language input; separate class denominators. This two-phone supervised diagnostic does not score autonomous discovery.

English 7 m and 29 s calibration tokens. Without refitting: Belarusian 9/9, Catalan 57/61, French 13/14, Swahili 13/13. Across targets 39/39 m and 53/58 s. This is one broad contrast at supplied intervals, forced IPA labels, small cohorts, evaluator prototype. No other phones offered.

Freeze whole-sentence s detector: same 20-ms spectral ratio every 10 ms. Energy floor of −40 dB relative to sentence peak, three consecutive qualifying frames. Choose ratio threshold from integers −4…8 by English event F1. Evaluate four other languages, one-to-one greedy descending IoU ≥0.3, exact IPA s. Report misses, spurious events, timing on matches. Previously opened utterances; target labels for scoring only.

Threshold 3 selected on eight English sentences. Across 24 other-language sentences: 38 matches of 58 annotated events, 72 detections, 34 false alarms and 20 misses. Median absolute onset error 30 ms among matches. Belarusian 6/17 predicted vs 6 annotated, Catalan 23/37 vs 39, French 6/11 vs 9, Swahili 3/7 vs 4. Reproducible offline waveform prototype; MFA reference boundaries.

Frozen multilingual s timeline error audit: 30/34 false detections had zero overlap with exact reference s; 16/20 misses had zero overlap with any prediction. Largest-overlap labels: spn 10, ʃ and f 4 each, sʲ, tsʲ, t 3 each, ts and s 2 each, ʒ, d͡z, i 1 each. Keep spn unclassified; do not infer underlying sound. Exact vs secondary-articulation scoring must be explicit. External cv_detection_errors.py.

Fresh whole-sentence comparison: test offsets 20,220,6020,6520, eight rows each. Fixed threshold 3, earlier frame/energy/overlap rules unchanged. Exact s vs union {s,sʲ}; no subclass predictor. Verify disjoint utterances. Break out per-language counts before interpreting broader criterion.

Fresh 32 sentences, 60 detections. Exact matches 23/58 annotations (precision 38.3%, recall 39.7%); union 24/60 (both 40%). Only Belarusian added sʲ intervals, one extra match among two added references. Catalan 5/28 detected vs Swahili 6/6, small cohorts. Broader scoring does not explain most errors. No diacritic naming claim.

Exploratory leave-language-out s detection on open 32-sentence second panel. Train on first panel excluding each target language, compare English-only identical model. Eight centered log-energy bands, class-balanced linear discriminant with half diagonal covariance shrinkage, select intercept on source event F1 over fixed offsets. Same gating and event scorer. Report recall and precision; source data budgets unequal.

English-only spectral classifier 41 matches/90 predictions/58 references (precision .456 recall .707 F1 .554); multilingual leave-target-out 35/74/58 (.473, .603, .530). Prior English ratio 23/60/58 (.383,.397,.390). Spectral shape improves observed F1, multilingual pooling did not beat English-only; open-panel estimates require fresh confirmation. No installation.

Confirmatory replay on eight new rows at each offset 40,240,6040,6540. Same sources, model, hyperparameters, threshold selection and scoring. Compare pooled event F1 plus language counts to fixed two-band threshold 3. Block overlap checked by utterance ID.

Fresh 32-sentence block: exact s 67 references. Ratio 36 matches/86 predicted, English spectrum 45/104, multilingual spectrum 40/83. Pooled event F1 .471/.526/.533. Direction replicated, size modest and rankings of spectral arms reversed. Belarusian English spectrum 4 matches in 30 proposals; Swahili 4/13 references. No broad mastery.

Nasal localization transfer: fix identical eight-band detector, hyperparameters, threshold search, training clips, and event scorer from s study. Fit separate exact m and n models, target language excluded. Score on prior 32 held-out sentences; these phone-specific endpoints new, recordings already opened. Independent detectors may overlap.

Multilingual m 14/188 proposals vs 37 references, n 18/113 vs 76. English-only m 7/180 and n 5/22 with same reference totals. For multilingual n the Catalan scanner issued zero detections despite 26 annotations. Eight-band success on s does not generalize across manner/place. No detector promotion.

Combined m/n target diagnostic on opened 32-sentence panel: pool these two exact IPA reference labels for training and event matching, retain one reference event per annotated segment. Same inputs, fitting and source threshold selection; no target tuning. Report matched m and n separately.

Multilingual m/n detector: 29 matched of 113 references and 140 predictions (9/37 m, 20/76 n); 111 false alarms. Per language matches/references: be 12/17, ca 2/33, fr 0/4, sw 15/59. English-only matched 25/113 with 136 predictions. Removing place-identification requirement still leaves substantial localization failure. No installation.

Fixed-score nasal persistence replay, 32 open sentences. Minimum 3/2/1 active frames yielded 29/31/33 matches and 140/182/259 predictions (113 reference events). Single-frame arm retained all 29 original hits, rescued four, added 115 false alarms. Of 84 original misses, 70 had zero positive-duration overlap with any single-frame prediction. Timing persistence alone is not the main bottleneck; score and energy gates were both held fixed. External cv_nasal_persistence.py.

Frame audit rebuilt frozen cross-language nasal scores on 113 reference spans. All 70 with zero candidate overlap contained at least one energy-eligible frame, and none contained any above-threshold score even before energy gating. Counts by be/ca/fr/sw: 4/27/4/35. Removing energy gate alone recovers zero of those spans. Separating calibration from inadequate score ranking requires a threshold-vs-false-alarm curve.

Diagnostic held-out threshold-offset sweep on the opened nasal panel, fixed three-frame persistence. Source cutoff: 29/113 hits, 111 false alarms, F1 .229. Offset −0.5: 39 hits, 238 false alarms, F1 .200. Offset +0.5: 20 hits, 55 false alarms, F1 .213. Among nine tested common offsets from −2 through +2 none improved pooled event F1. Not an exhaustive threshold or feature bound. No promotion.

Freeze static eight-band vs same frame plus two eight-band differences to frames ±30 ms. Same leave-target-language-out training, source event-F1 threshold selection, frame gates and score. Fresh test offsets 60,260,6060,6560 (8 sentences each). Added lookahead 30 ms; test paired F1 by sentence within language.

Actual sample offsets gave 8 Belarusian, 8 Catalan and 16 Swahili utterances, no French. All 32 scored. Static 47/221 detections, change 49/237 detections, 112 references; F1 .282 and .281. Paired sentence bootstrap 95% delta [−.036,.035]. Swahili gained five hits; Catalan lost three. No overall gain on this panel. No installed change.

Freeze equal-dimensional nasal spectral comparison on fresh test offsets 80,280,5980,6580 (8 rows each). Bin upper edges 250,500,750,1000,1500,2000,4000,8000 Hz versus eight equal-width bins. Unchanged frame rate, source-only thresholds and pooled target-language-excluded fitting. Compare pooled event F1.

Equal bands: 13 matches of 80 predictions, 114 references. Low-focused bands: 29 matches of 135 predictions. F1 .134 vs .233. All four languages gained hits, but only 1/47 Swahili nasals found. Evidence for frequency allocation on this panel, not reliable localization. Offline prototype.

Duration and speaker audit of low-frequency panel: Swahili 47 annotations, median 60 ms, all eight sentences from one speaker. 0/41 events at least 40 ms detected, 1/6 shorter. No annotation in any language shorter than 12 ms (duration-only necessary floor for IoU .3 and minimum predicted span 40 ms). Speaker counts be/ca/fr/sw 1/4/4/1. Previous panel differences should not be generalized to language effects. External cv_nasal_duration_audit.py.

Frozen low-focused nasal detector, all four earlier eight-row blocks per offset group (128 distinct sentence rows). Reference-aligned hits/predictions/references and speaker counts: Belarusian 49/235/83 (7), Catalan 48/171/120 (16), French 17/112/36 (8), Swahili 79/387/207 (5). Swahili speaker hits/ref 1/47,14/15,14/53,24/40,26/52. Single-speaker result did not generalize; high false alarm burden persists across all five. Retrospective, unequal speaker exposure.

Nasal false-alarm audit on frozen 128-utterance replay: 56/712 unmatched predictions touched an exact m/n reference; 656 had no overlap. Largest-overlap reference i 81, u 63, spn 53, no interval 43; other nasal labels include ŋ 12 and nʲ 11. Raw event counts depend on phone prevalence and are not per-phone false-positive rates. Full spans in cv-nasal-false-alarms.json.

Before scoring interval diagnostic: equal counts of m,n,i,u within every eligible evaluation speaker, first eligible tokens in sorted recording/time order. Use midpoint 20ms if fully contained. Train four class medians on original first-panel recordings excluding target language; nearest standardized median. Report family-level AND exact phone decisions. All evaluation recordings previously open. No classifier access to target language as an acoustic feature.

25 eligible speakers, 540 tokens. Family decisions 368/540, exact label 270/540. Per-language family/exact counts be 68/50 of 112, ca 62/40 of 88, fr 12/11 of 20, sw 226/169 of 320. Each speaker equally represented per class; token totals differ across speakers/languages. Offline supervised diagnostic with approximate alignments.

Four-phone uncertainty diagnostic on opened 540 probes. Confidence = normalized distance margin between first and second nearest source median. Calibrate with leave-one-source-language-out predictions, threshold source median margin, no target lookup. Compare retained vs deferred accuracy and report accepted label counts; no probability calibration claim.

Accepted 302/540, 179/302 exact (59.3%), deferred 91/238 exact (38.2%); full accuracy 270/540. Accepted true m 22/52, n 17/63, i 72/96, u 68/91. Confidence separated aggregate outcomes but favored vowels and left most accepted nasal decisions wrong. No installed confidence guarantee.

Four-phone second-read replay. Retain prior uncertainty purchases unchanged. Give second reader the mean centered spectral shape across first, midpoint, last 20-ms windows within supplied interval. Fit medians on identical source cohorts. Compare gated/always/never/uniform matched spend, 0.05 fee, all 540 previously opened tokens. No target tuning.

Second-read gate purchased 238, 263 correct, net 251.10; never 270 correct/net; always 258 correct net 231.0; uniform matched spend expected correct 264.71, net 252.81. Uncertain subset 91→84; confident subset 179→174. Low confidence flagged errors but did not establish that the particular extra measurement could fix them.

Ordered-window replay on same 540 tokens: concatenate 3×8 centered spectral values. Train source medians on chronological windows only; reverse evaluation order as matched intervention. Preserve prior midpoint uncertainty gate. Compare unconditional and selective counts. No tuning.

Ordered 275/540, reversed 264/540, earlier averaged 258/540, midpoint 270/540. Applying ordered rereads only to 238 prior uncertain examples raised 91 to 94 there (273 total), costing 11.90 for three extra correct; marginal break-even 3/238=.0126. These paired development results alone cannot support adoption.

Fresh ordered-window replication: freeze offsets 100, 300, 5960, 6600, eight clips each. Exclude previously read utterances. Retain the four classes, speaker balancing, source medians, uncertainty rule and reversed-window control; report all outcomes.

Fresh replication: 128 balanced annotated tokens. Midpoint 65, ordered 63, reverse 65. Of 73 flagged for a paid reread, both readers got 32 correct. No replicated improvement. Midpoint by language: Belarusian 15/28, Catalan 15/24, French 6/12, Swahili 29/64.

Localization diagnostic on the same 32 recordings: use the nearest source median for each queried phone independently, scanning 20-ms windows every 10 ms. Score the top point conditional on presence against the fraction of scan points covered by that phone; separately count absent queries. No threshold or target annotation during scanning.

Whole-recording scan hit 8/98 present queries (8.2%, uniform-time expectation 3.68%); m 4/22, n 1/27, i 2/27, u 1/22. All 30 absent queries received a location because the scan has no rejection criterion. This is a point-localization diagnostic using corpus alignments, not interval discovery or kernel deployment.

Matched localization diagnostic: source-language frame-supervised ridge detector versus saved nearest-median scan. Use ±30 ms context, absolute and relative spectral energy, ridge 0.1, class-balanced least squares. Hold out last two recordings per source panel for calibration; threshold at pooled 90th percentile of absent-query utterance maxima from other languages. Score unchanged 32-recording panel; report before/after rejection.

Supervised detector localized 28/98 before rejection (m 8/22, n 4/27, i 13/27, u 3/22), versus 8/98 source medians. After rejection: 47 accepted, 6 correct localizations, 9/30 absent-query false alarms. Forty queries had no eligible absent calibration recording and therefore always abstained, including all i queries. No production change. Recomputed matrix products via explicit einsum to verify numerical results. Fresh independent replication required.

Replication: freeze 8 recordings each at offsets 120,320,5940,6620. Keep source fitting, fixed ridge and median baseline unchanged. Add all nontraining cv-test panels to absent-query calibration, excluding target language. Evaluate the 90th percentile cutoff and unconditional locations.

Fresh replication: ridge vs median correctly located 22 vs 9 of 93 present queries; be 3 vs 3 /23, ca 10 vs 3 /25, fr 1 vs 2 /18, sw 8 vs 1 /27. Expanded calibration supplied 5–43 negatives per target-language/phone cell. Accepted 26/128, including 8 correct locations, 14 wrong locations on present queries and 4/35 absent-query alarms. Results support a pooled gain with substantial language heterogeneity.

Matched error replay reproduced all 128 original rows exactly. Of 14 accepted wrong locations on present queries, 1 was within 20 ms of a target interval, 13 were over 100 ms away, median gap 1.02 s. Five peaks lay in corpus spn intervals, nine in intervals with other phone labels. This motivates testing ranking against competing acoustic events rather than adjusting boundary tolerance.

Rank audit on unchanged replication recordings. Greedy peaks at least 100 ms apart; exact circular-shift null preserves peak spacing per recording and query. Among 93 present searches, top 1/3/5 included an annotated occurrence on 22/41/58 (shifted expectations 3.36/9.62/15.28). Of 14 confident misses, 7 included a hit by rank five, 7 did not. All 128 prior decisions reproduced. Candidate coverage is an evaluator-only ceiling for reranking.

Fresh supplied-pair search: 8 clips at offsets 140,340,5920,6640. Enumerate all 12 distinct ordered pairs of m,n,i,u per clip. Choose best summed scores separated by 10–200 ms in forward or reverse time; compare independent maxima. Evaluator requires both points inside one consecutive annotated pair in requested order. No annotations for candidate selection.

Fresh pair results: 43 present clip/query pairs across 19 of 32 recordings, out of 384 attempted. Forward search put both points in the same annotated pair 2/43, independent peaks 0/43. First point correct for that pair 5/43 forward vs 2/43 with reversed timing. Forced-choice diagnostic only, with requested phone identities supplied. This does not establish usable word recognition.

Evaluator-only anchoring audit on 56 adjacent occurrences from the 43 positive clip/queries. Supply midpoint of the first phone and score a point 10–200 ms later. All second phones intersected the window. Correct acoustic channel 35/56, wrong channel averaged 23.33/56, uniform timing expectation 23.52/56, fixed 80-ms offset 44/56. Timing control outperformed acoustic maximization. No target fit or operational capability claim.

Frozen anchored follow-up on 8 clips at offsets 160,360,5900,6660: standardize acoustic score within the 10–200 ms window then subtract half squared distance from 80 ms in units of 30 ms. Compare with 80 ms and audio alone, report paired changes. First midpoint supplied.

Anchored fresh results: combined 43/58, fixed 42/58, acoustic 32/58. Three fixed misses repaired and two fixed hits lost. Exploratory >80 ms first-phone subset: two gained, two lost over 34 occurrences. No convincing incremental benefit over timing.

Next-phone identity on existing timing panel, opposite-family adjacent pairs only so first-phone identity cannot directly eliminate a choice. Supply binary family. Balanced accuracy fixed 80 ms vs annotated second midpoint: m/n 61.4% vs 39.9% (m 6/7 vs 3/7; n 10/27 both), i/u 73.3% vs 86.7% (i 10/15 vs 11/15; u 4/5 vs 5/5). Small pooled diagnostic, no word meanings or automatic family prediction tested.

Freeze nasal transition diagnostic on offsets 180,380,5880,6680. Compare standardized nearest class means using midpoint alone versus midpoint plus onset/offset spectral changes at ±15 ms. Source training excludes target language and target speaker; test intervals supplied. Report balanced accuracy per language.

Nasal transition diagnostic: 123 scorable tokens, pooled balanced accuracy 64.1% midpoint vs 65.0% augmented. Catalan 58.1→68.5 (68), French 62.5→66.7 (18), Swahili 70.6→51.6 (37). Three languages contributed eligible tokens. No consistent advantage; preserve midpoint as control.

Post-hoc coverage audit: paired one m with one n before the same member of a/e/i/o/u within language, deterministic utterance/time order without reuse. 14/123 tokens matched; midpoint and transitions both 10/14. Requiring same speaker left 8 tokens, both 5/8 (Catalan 1/2, Swahili 4/6, French none). Sparse overlap cannot identify whether following vowel caused the original reversal.

Expanded retrospective local archive matching: exact speaker, language and following a/e/i/o/u, unique utterance/onset, deterministic pairs without reuse. Train outside target language and speaker; 61 pairs. Midpoint vs transition counts: Belarusian 31 vs 29 /46 (10 speakers), Catalan 15 vs 18 /26 (10), French 1 vs 1 /2 (1), Swahili 24 vs 24 /48 (6). Total 71 vs 72 /122. This reuses historical audio, supplies boundaries, and has sparse French support.

Retrospective broad supervised label reference: fixed 14-way ae i o u m n p t k s f l r menu, source means from other languages and disjoint speaker IDs, supplied midpoint. 270/741 correct (Catalan 149/427, French 44/152, Swahili 77/162). i 84/101, s 59/82, t 2/73, l 2/62, r 0/13. Corpus-label comparison only; all target tokens restricted to these labels and >=20 ms.

Precision audit on the frozen 14-label midpoint outputs: i 84/161 predictions correct (Catalan 33/52, French 9/39, Swahili 42/70); s 59/67 (41/41, 15/22, 3/4). High i recall masked substantial substitution errors. Restricted inventory and supplied acoustic location still apply.

Grounding feasibility, archived CV metadata only: 320 unique utterances across 5 languages. Case-folded alphabetic transcript tokens recurring across >=3 speaker IDs: 122 language/word types (ca 56, fr 29, sw 23, be 11, en 3). Zero one-word recordings under that rule. Phone times exist but word spans and referents are absent. Transcript-based counts are evaluator-only and do not establish audible s, semantic grounding or independent word comprehension.

English digit diagnostic: train 14 class means outside English, compute s-versus-closest-other distance margin on 20-ms frames of full digit audio. Append its maximum per quarter, scaled to RMS of baseline per example as a second equally weighted distance block. Reuse 2/3/6 target splits, nearest-example rule and independent probe blocks. Compare spectrum-only threshold crossings; target recordings previously studied.

Spectrum reached >=13/15 on both fresh blocks in 9/30 ordered voice pairs (5 at 3 lessons, 4 at 6); spectrum plus frozen s cue in 6/30 (2 at 3, 4 at 12). Remaining 21 vs 24 unreached by 24 lessons. No teaching savings established; target is known English digit corpus, not new-language deployment.

Paired English digit replay: among 3600 decisions (repeated recordings across teaching-voice forks), source s cue corrected 377 baseline errors and spoiled 422 correct outputs. Hindsight upper bound 2556/3600, spectrum 2179, always augmented 2134. Selective augmentation below a relative nearest-class distance margin, threshold chosen using the four other speakers for each held pair, got 2168. This retrospective cross-validation detects disagreement but yields no reliable selection gain.

Cross-speaker word-pair gate: from four other voices, use augmentation only where the unordered top-two baseline word IDs historically gained. Selected 971/3600 times, scored 2121 vs global margin 2168 and baseline 2179; mastered 8/30 vs 9/30 baseline by 24 lessons. Known-word retrospective, no new-language transfer claim.

Retrospective Mandarin 30-form one-example diagnostic: all forms shared by FV2/FV3/MV2/MV3, 120 whole clips, 12 ordered teaching/test voice pairs. Same energy trim and four temporal-bin means, nearest teaching example. Eight raw centered spectral bands 145/360 correct; distance to 14 non-Mandarin supervised phone centers 103/360. Filename labels for target classes/evaluation only, no supplied phone boundaries. One example per form, artificial form IDs and previously studied recordings; no natural semantic or teaching-efficiency claim.

Mandarin pitch diagnostic: freeze four equal time bins of median log2 autocorrelation pitch, center per clip and convert to semitones. Append to raw spectral vector unweighted. Matched time-reversed test contour control; report full-form, syllable and tone scores separately on previous panel.

Whole-form/syllable/tone correct of 360: raw 145/172/219, plus pitch 170/188/273, reverse query pitch 113/139/188. Retrospective cue diagnostic on same four speakers, 120 clips. Confirm separately before promoting.

Freeze FV1↔MV1 follow-up: include every shared tone-labelled form absent as a form from the prior 30-way evaluation. Same single-example nearest-reference classifier and pitch settings; both directions, unchanged reversed-contour diagnostic. Previously archived voices, independent of preceding four-voice panel only.

61 disjoint forms, 122 recordings, two other voices. Raw vs pitch vs reversed correct: whole forms 26/33/17; segmental syllable 38/41/32; tone 55/71/42, all /122. Whole-form gain in both directions (+4,+3). Archives previously used elsewhere; limited speaker coverage.

Retrospective tone-minimal two-label task: eight same-syllable tone pairs × twelve ordered voice pairs. One teaching recording per arbitrary object ID, nearest example. Both objects correct: raw 40/96, spectrum plus chronological pitch 57/96, reversed query contour 26/96. Individual outputs 136/192, 153/192, 120/192. Repeated recordings and assigned referents; not natural lexical semantics or multi-dose learning curves.

Mandarin teaching-dose diagnostic: eight two-object menus, one recording per form per teacher, 12 ordered choices of two teachers from four; remaining two voices are separate 16-item test blocks. At least 14/16 required on both. Raw nearest example: 0/12 at 16 lessons, 0/12 at 32. Raw plus pitch: 1/12 at 16, 4/12 at 32, 4/12 ever. Paired arms; overlapping splits and same probe clips across doses, so no independent longitudinal or percentage savings claim.

Six-voice dose follow-up: use all complete same-base tone pairs in current local six-voice intersection. Each permutation assigns two ordered teachers and two disjoint probe voices per dose. Freeze nearest reference and 85% threshold per probe voice. Report split counts descriptively; permutations reuse recordings.

Four complete tone pairs across six voices (48 unique recordings). Blocks each contain 8 choices, pass >=7 twice. Over 720 overlapping assignments, spectrum passed 0 at either dose; plus pitch passed 12 at 8 lessons, 152 at 16, 164 ever. No assignment passed at both doses on four independent probe voices. Percentage teaching savings remain unidentified.

Pitch-only ablation, retrospective four tone-minimal object menus. All previous raw/combined block counts reproduced exactly. Four centered pitch bins alone achieved 85.8%/90.2% individual accuracy at 8/16 lessons and 372/720, 464/720 two-voice passes, 236 passing both doses; combined 73.3%/80.8%, 12/152 passes, zero both. Supplied tone-only contrasts make this a specialized control, not a general vocabulary policy.

Crossed assigned conventions, identical Mandarin audio and balanced binary objects: two 2×2 syllable/tone grids. Eight pointed lessons across two speakers. Select raw spectrum or pitch-only nearest-example representation by predicting each teaching speaker from the other, tie to raw. Across overlapping six-voice splits, tone rule 437/480 vs raw 285 and pitch 437; syllable rule 329/480 vs raw 336 and pitch 314. Same-audio cases requiring an object change: both forks correct 164/240 (68.3%), below 80% target. No installed-runtime or natural semantics claim.

Crossed-cue ablation: add existing ordered onset representation (8 kHz, four frames and energy differences) as third teacher-validated option, with original options winning ties. Fixed onset syllable 304/480 vs whole spectrum 336. Adaptive tone 430/480, syllable 326/480, matched switches 152/240 vs prior 164/240. No gain on archived six-voice panel.

Crossed-cue panel: add existing 44.1-kHz high-band onset to low-band onset delay (10-ms grid) as optional third representation; nearest matched demonstration, ties count wrong. Fixed duration on syllables 405/480 vs spectrum 336; adaptive syllable 391/480 and tone 437/480. Same-audio switches both correct 187/240 vs 164/240 with two readers, 5 short of 192. Archived exploratory panel; no independent replication.

Frozen four-voice transfer: all archived FV2/FV3/MV2/MV3 j/x pairs with same rhyme and two common tones, excluding every syllable base in the prior crossed tasks. Score the original two-reader and duration-augmented variants with identical histories. Shared speakers; independent syllables only.

Transfer on two new grids (jian/xian and jiao/xiao, tones 2/4): matched history switches 38/48 with duration vs 29/48 without. Adaptive syllable correctness 91/96 vs 75/96; tone 82/96 both. Fixed duration 96/96 syllable. 38/48 is 79.2%, below 80%; shared speakers, 32 recordings, assigned meanings.

Freeze Mandarin c/s contrast on cao and can rhymes, tones 2/4, four previous FV2/FV3/MV2/MV3 voices. Apply identical two- and three-reader selectors. Report coverage if clips unavailable.

All 32 c/s recordings available. Two- and three-reader selectors both 35/48 on same-recording paired switches (72.9%); adaptive tone both 88/96, syllable 67 vs 65/96. Fixed duration syllable only 49/96. Prior j/x duration gain did not replicate across this contrast; no retuning.

Development c/s six-bin relative log high-band contour: fixed syllable 85/96, adaptive 77/96, tone 88/96, joint 40/48. Freeze unchanged for cai/sai and cang/sang tones 1/4 with same four voices; count complete grids only.

Fresh 32 clips: added contour vs identical selector without it, joint history switches 44/48 vs 31/48, syllable 92/96 vs 65/96, tone 92/96 both. Fixed contour 93/96 syllable. New rhymes and tones, same four voices, repeated splits, experimental assigned meanings; not yet validated in installed runtime.

Freeze speaker transfer: same 8 cai/sai/cang/sang forms, same 6 teaching pairs of FV2/FV3/MV2/MV3, evaluate FV1/MV1 only with unchanged cue-enabled and disabled rules. Both target voices new to this c/s study, previously used elsewhere.

New c/s voices: joint switch criterion 31/48 with contour vs 23/48 disabled; FV1 19 vs 15 /24, MV1 12 vs 8 /24. Syllable 74 vs 57 /96, tone 85/96 both. Six overlapping teacher pairs on 16 unique test recordings. Gain travels to both speakers, 80% absolute target does not.

Installed 0.5.0 BandOnsets information audit: synthetic matched waveforms with rising/falling 6-kHz amplitude, common 2.2-kHz component, then 500-Hz onset at 60 ms, returned identical six timestamps (60,60,0,0,0,0). Six-point centered high-band contours differed by Euclidean distance 3.028. Existing timestamp receipt cannot reconstruct the c/s contour; this was a direct installed primitive check.

Sound foundations 0.6.0: installed fresh wheel, discovered contour operation and replayed 48 natural waveforms through the kernel. All contours matched offline reference (unavailable handled by caller), all 192 saved decision rows byte-identical, joint 31/48. Seven package tests passed. Other measurements and choice still external.

Fresh-process local contour benchmark (48 recordings, sequential): imports/discovery/kernel installation 858.9 ms, first kernel request 2.55 ms; remaining 47 median/p95 0.50/0.64 ms. File decode with a new ffmpeg subprocess per recording median/p95 23.86/26.51 ms, total 24.33/27.17 ms. Peak parent RSS 250.14 MiB (whole Python process); valid contour on 47/48. No audio capture, real-time deadline, or chooser cost measured.

Installed kernel prefix audit: reveal waveform at 50-ms increments from file start plus final partial block. Of 47 full-clip valid contours, first nonempty receipt agreed with final to absolute 1e-8 on 10. Median/p95 first receipt 100/250 ms; earliest prefix with all subsequent receipts agreeing 250/300 ms. One full-clip unavailable result stayed unavailable throughout. Stability is hindsight-defined; no live stopping rule or behavioral effect claimed.

Frozen choice prefix replay: 88/192 decisions selected the contour (16 test files); full teaching exemplars retained, reference zero fallback on absent contour. First available 54/88 correct, 38 choices differ from full. At fixed deadlines 150/200/250/300 ms: 32/58/62/68 correct, 56/32/6/0 differ. All 88 full decisions reproduced. This tests selected contour branch only, no end-to-end action deadline or unseen replication.

Freeze prefix replication on cu/su and cuo/suo tones 1/4, four teaching voices and two probe voices as before, deadlines 150–300 ms, zero fallback and selected branch unchanged. Report unavailable clips and selection counts.

Acquired all 48 cu/su/cuo/suo clips. On 48 contour-selected decisions from 16 test files, correct counts first/150/200/250/300/full: 24/24/24/30/46/48. Two disagreements persisted at 300 ms, so perfect deadline parity did not replicate. Across all branches, matched convention pairs both correct 31/48. Branch selection substantially changes denominators.

cu/su/cuo/suo matched diagnosis: all 192 saved decisions reproduced. Evaluator-selected pitch for tone and contour for consonant achieves 44/48 joint vs learned selection 31/48. Syllable histories with tied best teaching accuracy: 5/12 histories, 27/40 adaptive vs 40/40 contour; unique best 53/56 vs 56/56. Tone histories tied 12/16 vs 16/16 pitch, unique 65/80 vs 71/80. Ties describe observed teaching scores, not fundamental unidentifiability.

Diagnostic lesson replay on opened cu/su panel: eight previews available across two spare voices, select largest 0-vs-1 vote disagreement among tied readers, request one pointer only if disagreement. Probe voices FV1/MV1 disjoint. 7/24 histories asked. Baseline/true/flipped/random-equal-question totals 157/165/158/162.625 of 192, random exact expectation. Gain concentrated in syllable histories 80 to 88; tone 77 to 77. Fixed inquiry heuristic; no preview or training costs deducted.

Freeze diagnostic-lesson replication: cen/sen and ceng/seng, tones 1/4 where all clips are available. Skip previews for unique winning reader; otherwise eight previews per tied history. No replacement for unavailable grid. Gross value one per correct held-out object, exact random-question control.

All 48 listed clips obtained and decoded. On 24 fresh teaching histories (two grids, six teacher pairs, two conventions), one tied and bought 1 pointer after 8 previews. Across 192 later decisions: wait 176, true 179, flipped 176, random matched expectation 177.125. All three gains from one tone history. Observed break-even vs wait for this panel only: pointer fee + 8 preview fees <3 correct-output units, excluding other costs.

Unresolved public history on cen/sen and ceng/seng: two diagonal forms taught by two voices, off-diagonal target sounds require opposite pointers under equally weighted conventions. Best-reader vote fraction tested only as confidence proxy. On 48 probes mean absolute deviation from 0.5 was 0.3194, 28 unanimous, expected Brier 0.4005 vs 0.25 neutral. Identical receipts by construction; repeated teacher forks, evaluator supplies balanced convention prior.

Matched clarification-transfer diagnostic on opened cen/sen and ceng/seng: same diagonal history, supply one off-diagonal lesson in third voice, intervene on its binary pointer and test the OTHER untaught form in a separate voice. Frozen tied-reader selection yields both convention answers correct 32/96 forks; 32/44 if tied readers predicted both possible lesson replies, 0/52 otherwise. All 32 output changes were correctly directed. Externally supplied lesson; overlapping forks.

Retrospective one-error tolerance vs top-ties only. Keep readers within one correct prediction of best across four teacher tests, prefer higher historical score among compatible readers. Both possible replies represented 96/96 vs 44/96; joint opposite-form transfer 72/96 vs 32/96. Established probes 362/384 for both (2 newly wrong, 2 newly correct). Repeated forks; no independent confirmation or claim of zero interference.

Freeze one-error retention replication on cong/song and cou/sou tones 1/4 across the same six corpus voices. Exclude previously cached files from novel-recording count. Keep both arms, lesson forks and established probes unchanged.

Confirmation: 48 clips including 46 newly downloaded, six familiar voices. Retaining runners raised joint correction transfer 14→39 /96 and reply coverage 18→56 /96. Established correctness fell 311→300 /384. Positive direction replicated, absolute 80% transfer failed; costs to retention appeared on these forms.

Evaluator-only attribution reproduced all prior rows. Of 57 runner-up policy failures, 33 lacked a viable kept reader for at least one pointer although the full four-reader set supported both transfers; 3 could be solved by choosing differently within the kept set; 21 lacked a compatible lesson-to-target transfer for at least one pointer even in full library. Full-library receipt-consistent oracle 75/96 (<77 required). Per-probe hindsight, not an achievable learned score.
