Installed and run from a clean process (21:00). The recurrent listener's convolutions (with their normalisation folded in), recurrent passes and 64-unit layer were written out as float16 arrays and run in NumPy inside a new package, `nca-phonetics`, with two registered operations: listen (waveform to frames) and compare (two heard stretches to their unlikeness). The NumPy frames differ from the fitted network's by at most 0.0004. In an environment built from wheels of the core and the package alone, the third-vocabulary test was rerun with every clip heard by a request to the kernel: 26.0 against 17.0 examples in Welsh and 13.5 against 8.5 in Ukrainian, the same counts as from the research scripts. Two fresh processes per language returned identical frames (same digest) and identical counts. A clip of about 0.4 s takes 6.0 ms at the median and 8.9 ms at the 95th percentile through the kernel; the process peaks at 372 MB with the core loaded. The registered comparison agrees with the batched one on forty pairs per language. The package's ten tests pass in that environment.

### The same four syllables under two conventions, in Spanish and Italian. Statement (21:03)

Idea. Four syllables that cross two distinctions, say pa, ba, ta, da, can belong to a language where the first distinction changes what is meant (pa and ta point one way, ba and da the other) or to one where the second does (pa and ba against ta and da). The audio is the same; only the pointing differs. A learner that has heard both distinctions should follow whichever the pointing uses, and one that hears only one of them will fail in one of the two languages. This is the goal's decisive experiment on natural speech; neither listener has heard Spanish or Italian.

Protocol. A token is the stretch from the consonant's start to the vowel's end by the corpus alignment, both phones at least 30 ms, heard inside its utterance. Six sets of four syllables for each language, fixed by how many speakers say them, before any scoring:

| Set | First distinction | Second distinction | Spanish | Italian |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | voicing | place | pa ba / ta da | pa ba / ka ɡa |
| 2 | voicing | vowel | pa ba / pi bi | pa ba / pi bi |
| 3 | place | vowel | ma na / mo no | ma na / mo no |
| 4 | manner | vowel | ta sa / te se | ta sa / te se |
| 5 | manner | vowel | na la / ne le | na la / ne le |
| 6 | vowel height | vowel backness | ti te / tu to | ti te / tu to |

Speakers are halved by a fixed hash into those who teach and those who test. The probes are up to 40 tokens a syllable from testing speakers, at most two from one speaker, the same for every history. A history holds eight tokens of each syllable from teaching speakers, from different speakers where there are enough; twenty histories a set; the first n of each syllable (n = 1, 2, 4, 8) are the examples at that count. The two conventions get the same history and differ only in which of two things each example points to. The reader is the one from the word test with one view: likeness from warped distances scaled by the history's median, made positive semi-definite, ridge 0.1. Arms: the frequency bands, and the recurrent listener's 64-unit layer (what the installed expert returns). A set passes at a count when both conventions reach 80% of probes, mean over histories.

Predictions, with eight examples a syllable:
1. The listener passes in at least seven of the twelve sets (chance 0.5).
2. The bands pass in at most three (0.7).
3. On the convention carried by a consonant, the listener is at least 10 points above the bands in at least ten of the twelve sets (0.7).
4. No set carried by voicing passes in both languages (0.5): voicing was the weakest family in Italian.

Outcome (21:09). Share of probes answered as the convention requires, mean over twenty histories and the four syllables, with 8 examples a syllable (and with 4 in brackets); first convention / second convention:

| Set | Spanish, bands | Spanish, listener | Italian, bands | Italian, listener |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| voicing x place | 0.769 / 0.764 | 0.855 / 0.909 (0.821 / 0.888) | 0.754 / 0.795 | 0.857 / 0.983 (0.808 / 0.981) |
| voicing x vowel | 0.717 / 0.971 | 0.861 / 0.991 (0.838 / 0.989) | 0.775 / 0.909 | 0.873 / 0.988 (0.823 / 0.985) |
| place x vowel | 0.624 / 0.717 | 0.882 / 0.891 (0.868 / 0.867) | 0.599 / 0.713 | 0.926 / 0.892 (0.901 / 0.867) |
| manner (t, s) x vowel | 0.728 / 0.739 | 0.957 / 0.907 (0.952 / 0.874) | 0.756 / 0.749 | 0.958 / 0.856 (0.943 / 0.853) |
| manner (n, l) x vowel | 0.716 / 0.762 | 0.824 / 0.885 (0.799 / 0.883) | 0.743 / 0.788 | 0.887 / 0.889 (0.868 / 0.855) |
| height x backness | 0.676 / 0.836 | 0.873 / 0.928 (0.860 / 0.920) | 0.703 / 0.842 | 0.884 / 0.966 (0.849 / 0.958) |

1. HELD, and too cautious: the listener passes all twelve sets with eight examples a syllable, and eleven with four (Spanish n, l falls 0.001 short).
2. HELD: the bands pass none.
3. HELD at the edge, on a count the statement left loose: there are twelve conventions carried by a consonant (two in each voicing-by-place set, one in each of sets 2 to 5), and the listener is at least 10 points above the bands in ten of them (8.6 for Spanish voicing against place, 9.8 for Italian voicing against vowel).
4. FAILED: both voicing sets pass in both languages.

With the same history of sound, the reader built on the listener follows whichever distinction the pointing used, in two languages it had not heard, for voicing, place, manner and vowel quality. The goal's bar of 80% on both members is met on natural speech in all twelve sets at 32 examples. Left open: intervals over histories and probe speakers, the history that leaves the convention unresolved, a controlled version, and length, tone and stress, which these sets do not touch.

### Knowing that the convention is still open. Statement (21:12)

Idea. Point at pa as one thing and at da as another, and nothing yet says whether voicing or place carries the difference: ba and ta are undetermined. The single reader answers them anyway, by whichever distinction happens to be larger in its distances. A learner should know that two readings fit, since that is when a contrastive example is worth asking for. Give it many readers, each attending to a different slice of what the listener hears, weigh each by how well it accounts for the pointing so far, and read disagreement among the readers that fit as "still open".

Theory. Reader m sees the frames through its own random projection of the 64 numbers onto 3; two tokens are aligned once on the full frames and reader m takes the mean cosine distance along that same path in its projection. Each reader is the ridge reader as before. Its weight is exp(−e), e being the taught examples it gets wrong when each is left out in turn (closed form for the ridge fit). The committee's chance of the second thing is the weighted share of readers that choose it; the probe is left unanswered while that share lies between 0.3 and 0.7. Sixty-four projected readers and the full-frame reader; projections fixed by seed; nothing fitted to these languages. When the taught examples cover all four syllables, readers blind to the distinction in use lose weight and the rest agree. When only two opposite syllables were pointed at, every reader fits, and readers that lean on different distinctions split on the two untaught syllables.

Test: the Spanish sets with the listener's frames. The open history points at the first and fourth syllable of a set only (eight examples of each); the other two are heard in the probes alone.

Predictions:
1. Under the open history the committee leaves at least 50% of probes of the two untaught syllables unanswered, mean over the six sets, and at most 15% of probes of the two taught ones (chance 0.4).
2. Under either full convention with eight examples a syllable it leaves at most 15% unanswered (0.6), and on all probes, counting an unanswered one by the side its share leans to, it is within 2 points of the single reader (0.6).
3. With one example a syllable the committee is at least 2 points above the single reader, mean over sets and conventions (0.35).

Outcome (21:19): FAILED, and stopped after two of the six Spanish sets, which took the whole time allowance. With eight examples a syllable the committee answered worse than the single reader (voicing by place 0.826 and 0.848 against 0.855 and 0.909; voicing by vowel 0.799 and 0.990 against 0.861 and 0.991) and left 14 to 22% of probes unanswered under a full convention. Under the open history it left 48% and 30% of the untaught probes unanswered and 17% and 6% of the taught ones; 50% and 15% were predicted. With one example a syllable it was 1.5 points below to 4 points above the single reader. A reader that sees three random mixtures of the 64 numbers is a poor reader, so the committee's disagreement is mostly noise and not two readings of the convention. One observation is worth keeping: under the open history of pa and bi, the single reader gives 90% of the untaught pi and ba probes to the vowel's side. It imposes a convention nobody taught.

### Open conventions by parts of the syllable and by newness. Statement (21:20)

Two plainer signals replace the committee. (a) Parts: the alignment path between a probe and a taught example is halved, giving a reader of the early half and a reader of the late half, each a ridge reader on its own distances; when a consonant and a vowel distinction are crossed, the two should side with different taught syllables on an untaught one. (b) Newness: a probe whose nearest taught example is farther than taught examples of one thing usually lie from their own nearest fellow (above the 90th percentile of those leave-one-out distances) is a sound not yet pointed at. Spanish is used to look at both signals and fix one rule; Italian then tests the rule once.

Expectation before looking, Spanish, open history with eight examples of each of the two taught syllables: the early and late readers disagree on at least 60% of untaught probes in the four consonant-by-vowel sets and on at most 20% of taught ones (chance 0.5); newness flags at least 40% of untaught probes at 10% of taught ones in the voicing-by-place set, where the parts cannot differ (0.4).

Spanish, looked at to fix a rule (21:23). Open history, eight examples of each of two opposite syllables. Raw disagreement of the two halves: untaught probes 0.573, 0.672, 0.623, 0.527 in the four consonant-by-vowel sets (mean 0.599, expected at least 0.60: missed by a hair) and taught probes 0.044 to 0.162; but under a full convention the halves also disagree on 12 to 29% of probes, since the half that does not carry the convention fits noise. Newness is a poor signal: 16 to 33% of untaught probes against 9 to 19% of taught ones, and 17% against 16% for voicing by place (expected 40% at 10%: FAILED). Telling one token of an untaught syllable from the taught ones is the discrimination task again, one token at a time.

Rule fixed on this: a probe is "open" when both halves' readers fit what was taught (each wrong on at most a quarter of the taught examples left out in turn) and choose differently. On Spanish this flags 0.573, 0.581, 0.623, 0.495 of untaught probes in the consonant-by-vowel sets, 0.044 to 0.134 of taught ones, and 0.06 to 0.18 under a full convention; in the two sets whose distinctions share a half (voicing by place, height by backness) it flags 0.21 and 0.20 of untaught probes and is of no use.

Statement for Italian, one run: in the four consonant-by-vowel sets the rule flags at least 50% of untaught probes in mean, at most 15% of taught ones, and at most 15% under either full convention (chance 0.5); in the two same-half sets under 30% of untaught probes (0.8).

Outcome on Italian (21:27), one run. HELD on both counts. In the four consonant-by-vowel sets the rule flags 0.359, 0.566, 0.612 and 0.559 of the untaught probes under the open history (mean 0.524), 0.042 to 0.086 of the taught ones, and 0.055 to 0.124 under a full convention. In the two same-half sets it flags 0.121 and 0.183 of the untaught probes. So when a consonant distinction and a vowel distinction are crossed and the pointing has not said which one counts, the learner notices on about half of the fresh syllables that two readings fit, at under one false notice in ten; when both distinctions sit in the consonant, or both in the vowel, it does not notice. Voicing by vowel is the weakest of the four (0.359): the early half hears voicing least surely.

### Acting on a fresh utterance: answer, hear again, or ask what it means. Spanish to fix the policy (21:50)

The reader now lives in the package as one object: it is taught heard stretches with the thing pointed at, and reads a fresh utterance from one or several hearings (scores averaged) into a choice, a margin (the chosen thing's score above the runner-up) and whether the reading is open (both halves' readers fit and choose differently). I first let it also settle an open reading by which half the contrastive examples favoured; on Spanish that made it stop asking after one or two questions with untaught syllables still read at 57 to 73%, so the settling was removed: it now stops asking when a half no longer fits what was taught.

Hearing again, a full convention taught with eight examples a syllable, Spanish, six sets, 2,880 fresh utterances: one hearing 0.894 right, with a second speaker saying the same syllable 0.948, with a third 0.977. By the margin of the first hearing:

| Margin of the first hearing | right with one hearing | with another speaker | with two more |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| lowest tenth (under 0.15) | 0.576 | 0.823 | 0.944 |
| 0.15 to 0.28 | 0.736 | 0.903 | 0.951 |
| 0.28 to 0.38 | 0.847 | 0.899 | 0.958 |
| 0.38 to 0.49 | 0.917 | 0.976 | 0.986 |
| 0.49 to 0.60 | 0.934 | 0.948 | 0.958 |
| above 0.60 (half of all) | 0.985 | 0.987 | 0.994 |

Rehearing only below a margin of 0.5 gives 0.947 while rehearing 41% of utterances; rehearing all gives 0.948.

Asking, open history (two opposite syllables, eight examples each), a stream of forty fresh utterances, the teacher holding either convention: never asking and hearing everything three times both leave the untaught syllables at exactly 0.500 over the two conventions, as they must, since the same answers are right under one and wrong under the other. Asking when the reading is open costs 2.5 to 5.7 questions and brings the untaught syllables in the stream's later half to 0.864, 0.644, 0.782 and 0.706 in the consonant-by-vowel sets, against 0.753, 0.586, 0.661 and 0.608 for as many questions asked at utterances picked blindly; 0.642 and 0.651 against 0.574 and 0.635 in the two same-half sets.

Policy and costs, frozen here for Italian. Time is charged at 0.025 of a right answer per second and a teacher's pointing at 0.10. A requested hearing takes one second and the syllable; asking what an utterance means takes two seconds and one pointing, so about 0.03 and 0.15. The learner asks what an utterance means when its reading is open and at least six utterances are still to come (one question raised later untaught answers by about 0.05 each on Spanish, and half the later utterances are of untaught syllables, so a question repays itself over about six); otherwise it asks for another hearing when the margin is under 0.5; otherwise it answers.

Statement for Italian, one run:
1. Hearing again: rehearing below a margin of 0.5 is within 1 point of rehearing everything while rehearing under half the utterances (chance 0.7), and at least 3 points above one hearing (0.8). Above a margin of 0.6 another hearing gains under 1 point, so it cannot repay 0.03 (0.8). A second token from the same speaker gains at least 2 points, and less than another speaker's (0.55).
2. Asking: in the four consonant-by-vowel sets, asking when open brings later untaught syllables to at least 0.65 in mean (0.6) and at least 5 points above blind asking (0.6); never asking and triple hearing stay at 0.500. Later untaught utterances are read differently under the two conventions in at least 40% of cases, taught ones in at most 15% (0.5).
3. Length (ta, tːa, to, tːo), which the listener does not hear: with the full convention in which length decides, eight examples a syllable give at most 0.65 right, and three hearings at most 0.70 (0.6): here neither hearing again nor asking repays.

Outcome on Italian (22:00), one run each; the first attempt ran out of time before printing anything, the listener's frames for a language are now kept on disk and each set is saved as it finishes.

### Discovery against teaching at one label budget. Statement (22:08)

Idea. Every listener so far was taught phone names for all 22.8 hours. The goal asks what a representation found without names is worth, and what the same names buy when given to it afterwards. Three learners with one network: (a) label-free: no names; two cuts of the same speech, placed up to 0.6 s apart and each distorted as another voice or microphone might (bands stretched along frequency by up to 15%, tilted, 0.1 s blanked), must agree frame by frame against the other frames of the same cut, neighbours within 30 ms aside; negatives come only from the same cut, so who is speaking cannot serve as a cue, and the two cuts start at different places, so counting frames cannot either. Its checkpoint is the last, since choosing would need names. (b) few names: the same network taught names on the fixed 9% of utterances (1.9 hours), nothing else. (c) all names: the recurrent listener already fitted. Then a reading layer (64 to 256 to 84 symbols) is taught on the frozen label-free frames from the same 1.9 hours of names, so (a) with its reading layer and (b) have seen the same named audio.

Predictions:
1. Telling phones apart (stage two, mean of four families on Spanish, Italian, LibriSpeech): the label-free listener is at least 3 points above the bands on all three (chance 0.6), and below the few-names listener on all three (0.7).
2. Naming frames of source speakers kept out: the label-free frames with their reading layer name fewer frames rightly than the few-names listener, by at least 5 points (0.7); the few-names listener reaches 0.62 to 0.68 (0.6).

### The acting test from sound, through registered operations. Statement (22:12)

The reader and the next step are now operations of the installed package: read (a reader holding what was pointed at, with one or more hearings of a fresh utterance, to a choice, a margin and whether it is open) and act (a reading, the hearings and utterances left and the two costs, to answer, hear again or ask). A fresh draw of Italian was exported as audio: for each of the seven sets, six histories and a stream of forty fresh utterances with two further speakers for each, 1,225 utterances in all. In the clean environment every utterance is heard by a request to the kernel (0.004 s of listening a second of speech at the median, 0.006 at the 95th percentile), and every reading and next step is a request. Each stream runs under four teachings (all four syllables pointed at by the first or by the second distinction; two opposite syllables only, the teacher holding the first or the second) and three ways of acting: answer at once, always hear three speakers, and the registered next step with the costs frozen above (0.03 a hearing, 0.15 a question, at most two further hearings).

Predictions, six segmental sets:
1. Full teaching: the next step is at least 3 points above answering at once (chance 0.75) and within 1.5 points of always hearing thrice (0.5), with under one further hearing an utterance in mean.
2. Open teaching, four consonant-by-vowel sets, later half of the stream, untaught syllables: answering at once and hearing thrice give 0.500 by construction; the next step gives at least 0.65 (0.6).

Outcome (22:15), one run of 122 s in the clean environment, 1,680 streams' worth of readings and next steps, all through the kernel.

1. HELD. Full teaching, six segmental sets, both conventions, 2,880 utterance-streams: answering at once 0.907 right; always three speakers 0.971; the next step 0.974 with 0.61 further hearings an utterance. Net of the frozen costs the three come to 0.907, 0.911 and 0.913: the next step also asked 1.5 needless questions a stream, wrongly taking a full convention for open, and that eats most of what the hearings gained.
2. HELD. Open teaching, later half of the stream, untaught syllables, mean over the two conventions the teacher may hold: answering at once 0.500, three hearings 0.500, the next step 0.755, 0.852, 0.767 and 0.770 in the four consonant-by-vowel sets (mean 0.786) for 4.0 questions a stream. Over the whole stream and net of costs: 0.738, 0.689 and 0.762.

Where asking and rehearing do not repay, measured in the same run: in the two sets whose distinctions share a half (voicing by place, height by backness) the next step leaves untaught syllables at 0.500 and 0.637 and nets 0.700 against 0.750 for answering at once; where consonant length decides, three hearings raise 0.683 to 0.729 for 1.4 further hearings an utterance, which nets 0.686. The learner has no way yet of knowing that it is in one of these cases, so it pays there for nothing.

The label-free listener, first attempt stopped (22:20). With the recurrent network the two cuts were matched almost at once: after 500 updates 99.9% of frames found their own moment, and on source speakers kept out the frames told phones apart worse than the bands (Catalan 0.600 against 0.647, English 0.563 against 0.576, mean of four families). A reader of the whole cut can tell a moment by how long ago something salient happened, which both cuts share and which says nothing of the sound at that moment. The run was stopped. The network was changed to the convolutional one, which sees only 180 ms either side of a frame; after 780 updates it matches 95% of frames and is level with the bands (0.641 and 0.578). It now runs to 5,000 updates, and the few-names listener after it; the predictions stand as stated, with less hope for the first.

### Finding a taught syllable in running speech. Statement (22:22)

Idea. So far every token was handed over already cut by the corpus's marks. The goal asks for finding and identifying to be scored apart. Finding: given eight taught examples of one syllable, say where it occurs in a whole fresh utterance from a speaker the teaching never used. Each taught example is aligned against every stretch of the utterance at once (dynamic time warping with a free start and end in the utterance), and its best stretch is the one with the least mean cosine distance along the path. The answer is the stretch found by the taught example with the least distance; the examples whose own best stretch overlaps it give a range for its start and a range for its end, which is the learner's statement of how sure the boundaries are. Identifying: given the marked stretch, which of the set's four syllables it is (the ridge reader with four things to choose among, eight examples each).

Test: Italian, the six segmental sets, the six histories and forty-utterance streams of the acting plan (1,440 searches). A find is right when the middle of the found stretch lies inside any marked occurrence of that syllable in the utterance (the corpus alignment, consonant start to vowel end). Controls: the bands with the same search, and a stretch of the same length placed at random.

Predictions:
1. The listener's finds are right in at least 60% of searches, mean of six sets (chance 0.5); the bands' in at most 35% (0.6); a random stretch in under 15% (0.9).
2. Among right finds the median distance of the found start and end from the marks is at most 30 ms each (0.6), and the stated ranges hold the marked start and end in at least half of right finds (0.4).
3. Four-way identifying on the marked stretch is at least 80% right in mean (0.6).

Outcome (22:23), Italian, 240 searches a set:

| Set | found, listener | found, bands | random stretch | start, end off by (median, right finds) | ranges hold start, end | range widths | four-way identifying, listener / bands |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| voicing x place | 0.658 | 0.208 | 0.029 | 10, 25 ms | 0.81, 0.62 | 57, 82 ms | 0.825 / 0.642 |
| voicing x vowel | 0.625 | 0.104 | 0.025 | 20, 15 ms | 0.82, 0.81 | 57, 85 ms | 0.875 / 0.633 |
| place x vowel | 0.650 | 0.117 | 0.054 | 15, 35 ms | 0.76, 0.63 | 60, 95 ms | 0.779 / 0.383 |
| manner (t, s) x vowel | 0.658 | 0.304 | 0.050 | 10, 25 ms | 0.84, 0.72 | 67, 85 ms | 0.800 / 0.629 |
| manner (n, l) x vowel | 0.567 | 0.196 | 0.054 | 10, 25 ms | 0.77, 0.63 | 56, 75 ms | 0.758 / 0.508 |
| height x backness | 0.608 | 0.150 | 0.013 | 10, 25 ms | 0.78, 0.62 | 56, 75 ms | 0.783 / 0.554 |
| mean | 0.628 | 0.180 | 0.038 | | | | 0.803 / 0.558 |

1. HELD: 0.628 found with the listener, 0.180 with the bands, 0.038 at random.
2. HELD but for one end: the found start is 10 to 20 ms from the mark and the end 15 to 25 ms in five sets, 35 ms in place by vowel; the stated ranges hold the marked start in 76 to 84% of right finds and the end in 62 to 81%, at widths of about 60 and 85 ms.
3. HELD at the edge: 0.803 four-way identifying on the marked stretch.

Finding is the weaker of the two: a syllable is found in running speech in five searches of eight, and identified on its marked stretch in four of five. A find counts any occurrence of the syllable in the utterance; the marks are the corpus alignment, not a second annotator's.

### The label-free listener. Outcome (22:48): FAILED

Five thousand updates on the 22.8 hours without names; at the end 98.9% of frames find their own moment in the other cut. Telling phones apart, stage two, same triplets, mean of the four segmental families:

| Test | bands | label-free | few names (1.9 h) | all names (22.8 h) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Spanish | 0.604 | 0.608 | 0.700 | 0.736 |
| Italian | 0.622 | 0.622 | 0.696 | 0.728 |
| LibriSpeech dev-clean | 0.664 | 0.632 | 0.714 | 0.789 |

Per family, label-free: Spanish 0.629, 0.575, 0.596, 0.631; Italian 0.645, 0.582, 0.623, 0.639, length 0.618; LibriSpeech 0.639, 0.586, 0.646, 0.657. Predicted at least 3 points above the bands on all three; found level with them on two and 3 points below on the third. Matching a moment across two distortions of the same recording can be done from detail that does not carry over to another voice; a stretch of the frequency axis by 15% is a small part of what separates two speakers. The one place it is ahead is Italian consonant length (0.618 against 0.554 for the listeners taught names and 0.558 for the bands): nothing taught it to ignore how long a sound lasts.

A reading layer taught on these frozen frames from 2.03 hours of named speech names 32.3% of speech frames for Catalan speakers kept out, 33.3% for Swahili, 19.1% for English, and 27.9% in unheard Spanish, against 71.5, 68.1, 56.3 and 44.0% for the listener taught all names.

Looked up afterwards, as after every miss. What is reported to work without names is predicting what comes next against other moments of the same speaker (contrastive predictive coding and its quantised form), on 100 to 360 hours, and clustering of speaker-normalised cepstra into Gaussian posteriors, which beats cepstra on the zero-resource tests; none of the reports isolates as little as 23 hours. I matched the same moment under distortion, which is neither. Predicting ahead is the next thing to try for this arm. Sources: van Niekerk et al., Vector-quantized neural networks for acoustic unit discovery (arxiv.org/abs/2005.09409); Bhati et al., Regularizing contrastive predictive coding for speech applications (arxiv.org/abs/2304.05974); Chen et al., Parallel inference of Dirichlet process Gaussian mixture models for unsupervised acoustic modeling (Interspeech 2015); Hermann et al., Multilingual and unsupervised subword modeling for zero-resource languages (arxiv.org/abs/1811.04791).

### A controlled convention: the same recording, slowed. Statement (22:55)

The natural sets vary two distinctions across different recordings. Here one of the two is made by hand, so that it is exactly the same in every token: each Italian pa and ba of the acting plan's first set is cut out with 30 ms either side and rendered twice, as recorded and slowed to 0.6 of its speed with pitch kept (ffmpeg's tempo filter), which makes it 1.67 times as long and changes nothing else. Four kinds result: pa, ba, slow pa, slow ba. In one language p against b decides what is pointed at; in the other the duration does. The histories are matched: the same eight recordings of each, in both renderings. Each clip is heard on its own by the installed listener, and read by the installed reader. Probes: the stream's twenty pa and ba from testing speakers, in both renderings.

Predictions: where p or b decides, at least 0.80 right (chance 0.55: a cut-out clip heard alone is harder than one heard in its sentence); where duration decides, at most 0.60 (0.75), because the comparison warps time and so cancels the one thing that differs; with only pa and slow ba pointed at, the reading of the two untaught kinds is marked open in under 20% of probes (0.7).

Outcome (22:55): HELD on all three, which is to say the failure came as predicted. Six matched histories, forty probes each. Where p or b decides: 0.833 right (0.70 to 0.95 by history). Where duration decides: 0.546 (0.33 to 0.68), on clips of 21 against 33 frames. With pa and slow ba pointed at, the untaught kinds are marked open in 10% of probes. Controlled and natural agree: this reader follows a taught convention when a difference of sound quality carries it, and is deaf to one carried by duration alone.

### Giving duration back to the reader. Statement (22:56)

Theory. Warping time is what lets two speakers' syllables be compared, and it removes how long each lasted. That quantity can be handed back as a fourth reader beside the whole, early and late ones: two stretches are unlike by the absolute log ratio of their lengths. To let it speak only when the pointing uses it, the reader answers by the whole comparison unless another reader accounts for the taught examples better by at least two (two fewer wrong when each is left out in turn); then that reader answers. Nothing else changes.

Predictions: the controlled duration convention rises from 0.546 to at least 0.85 (chance 0.7) with the p-or-b convention within 3 points of 0.833 (0.7). Natural speech must not lose: Spanish, one hearing after a full convention, stays within 1 point of 0.894 (0.6); the Italian kernel run stays within 1 point of 0.907 for answering at once (0.6). Italian consonant length, where the marks barely carry it, gains under 5 points on 0.683 (0.7).

Outcome (23:01): FAILED on the main prediction, HELD on the four guards. The controlled duration convention rose from 0.546 to 0.775 (predicted at least 0.85); the p-or-b convention stayed at 0.833; the untaught kinds are still marked open in 10% of probes. Spanish, one hearing after a full convention: 0.8938 before, 0.8927 after. The Italian kernel run, redone from the installed package: answering at once 0.9066 → 0.9090, three hearings 0.9712 → 0.9701, the stepping policy 0.9737 → 0.9719 at 0.59 further hearings and 109 questions in all (net of costs 0.9090, 0.9101, 0.9116). After a part convention in the consonant-by-vowel sets the stepping policy answers 0.8124 of the untaught syllables that come after its questions (0.7857 before; 3.96 questions a stream, net 0.776 against 0.738 for answering at once). Italian consonant length, where length decides: 0.683 → 0.717 answering at once, 0.754 with three hearings, 0.762 stepping (a gain of 3.4 points, under the 5 predicted).

Why the miss: the reader compares absolute lengths, and people speak at different rates, so a slowed syllable from a fast speaker can be as long as a plain one from a slow speaker. In the controlled set the slowed clips are 1.67 times as long, and the spread between speakers is of the same order. A length relative to the speaker's own rate (the stretch against its neighbours in the utterance) is the form the literature on quantity uses; a clip cut out of its sentence does not carry that, which is a limit of this controlled test as built, and the natural Italian length sets do carry it. Kept: the duration reader, since it costs nothing where length is not in use and helps where it is. Not done: lengths relative to the surrounding utterance.

### How many examples the convention test takes, read from the files already written (23:03)

No new run and so no prediction: the convention runs of 21:09 already answered with 1, 2, 4 and 8 examples a syllable, and only the last was reported. The lower of the two conventions, by examples a syllable:

| Reader | Language | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | sets at 0.80 on both conventions |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| frequency bands | Spanish | 0.576 | 0.619 | 0.672 | 0.704 | 0 of 6 |
| the listener | Spanish | 0.726 | 0.784 | 0.843 | 0.867 | 6 of 6: at 2, 2, 4, 4, 4 and 8 examples |
| frequency bands | Italian | 0.617 | 0.656 | 0.702 | 0.720 | 0 of 6 |

One example a syllable heard through the listener reads the taught convention as well as eight examples heard as frequency bands (0.726 against 0.704, 0.713 against 0.720). This is the plainest form of the question the goal calls its flagship: hearing the difference first does speed up learning which difference a language uses, here by a factor of about eight against the bands, in two languages the listener never heard. The comparison is against raw bands only; the six-view control of the word test was not run on syllables cut from sentences, because its views are stored for the word clips alone.

### What more speech would buy, read from the two amounts already fitted (23:04)

No new run. The convolutional listener was fitted on 1.9 hours and on 22.8 hours of the same speech (12 times as much). Mean of the four segmental families, stage two: Spanish 0.688 → 0.764, Italian 0.692 → 0.759, LibriSpeech 0.713 → 0.785 (bands 0.604, 0.622, 0.664). That is 6.7 to 7.6 points for 12 times the speech, or about 2 points a doubling. If that slope held, which is an extrapolation from two amounts and usually flattens, the 11 to 14 points still missing would take five to seven further doublings: some 700 to 3,000 hours of aligned speech. So more speech of this kind is a lever, but not one that reaches 0.90 in every family on this machine in a night; my earlier wording, "the level is set by the 23 hours", claimed more than these two points show.

### Other voices made from the same speech. Statement (23:04), before the fit is started

Idea. What the comparison lacks is sameness across speakers, and the fit has heard about 3,000 of them. Without more recordings, more voices can be made from the ones there are: before each update every cut has its bands stretched or squeezed along frequency by up to 15% (a longer or shorter vocal tract), a tilt laid across them (another microphone) and 100 ms blanked, the same distortion the label-free listener used. Known as vocal tract length perturbation (Jaitly and Hinton 2013) and spectrum masking (Park et al. 2019); both gave about one point of phone error on small read corpora. One change to the recurrent listener: the distortion. Same speech, names, updates, 64-unit layer and tests.

Predictions against the recurrent listener (Spanish 0.736, Italian 0.728, LibriSpeech 0.789 in mean of four families; 0.756 of frames named for source speakers kept out): frames named within 1.5 points either way (chance 0.6); the mean rises by 1 to 3 points in Spanish and in Italian (0.5), by less than 1 on LibriSpeech, whose language was heard (0.4); no family reaches 0.90 anywhere (0.9). If the mean rises by under 1 point in both unheard languages, made-up voices are not the lever either, and what remains is speech by more speakers or a different kind of learner.

HELD: the gap is 18 to 26 points where the language was taught and 7 to 9 in the unheard ones, against the 5 predicted. At an equal amount of names, discovery as built here adds nothing to teaching and loses to it: the frames found without names are worth less to a reader of names than the same network's own frames taught from those names alone. The separation the goal asks for therefore reads: what this listener can name, it was taught; what it found alone stands at the level of the bands.

The second amount for the recurrent network also sharpens the note of 23:04. From 2.03 to 22.8 hours it gains 3.6 points in Spanish, 3.2 in Italian and 7.5 on LibriSpeech, less than the convolutional one in the unheard languages (7.6 and 6.7). Eleven times the names moved the two unheard languages by 3 to 8 points depending on the network, so the estimate of what more speech of the same kind buys stands at 1 to 2 points a doubling there.
